Higurashi: Ryu Ga Gotoku-Hen
by Pyro81300
Summary

After the events of Yakuza 0, Kiryu Kazuma thought he'd stay in real estate and out of yakuza
business. However, when Nishiki tells him about how two Tojo Clan members were found brutally
murdered in Hinamizawa and how war might break out with the Sonozaki family, he finds himself
intervening and getting tied up in an eternal June that will push him to his limits. Join Kiryu and the
Higurashi gang as they change each other's destinies, and just maybe... Kiryu can help save a
certain girl from her tragic fate.
(DISCLAIMER: You only need to be familiar with Yakuza 0 and the whole 8 arcs of Higurashi for
this crossover. You probably can still enjoy this fine without knowledge of both, but be wary of
spoilers.)
ARC 1/DRAGON SLAYING ARC NOW COMPLETED!
ARC 2/DEMON'S TEARS ARC NOW COMPLETED!
ARC 3/RED SOUL BLUE FLAME ARC NOW COMPLETED!

Chapter 1: Prologue: An Old Friend &amp; New Foes
Chapter Notes

So, a couple of brief things.
- Timeline wise Kiryu is born 10 years earlier, and the events of Yakuza 0 also take place in
1978. (The timeline is messed up for a reason, but answering why is spoilers.)
- Kiryu is 24 (nearly 25) years old here since it takes place in 1983.
That's it, I hope you enjoy.

“Where would you like to go today, Sir?” The taxi driver asked.
“To Serena, please,” replied Kiryu.
“Very well, Sir. Hop in and we’ll be there shortly.”
Kiryu got into the back of the taxi and closed the door.
The driver had a slightly worried look on his face, as his new passenger reminded him heavily of a
drunk yakuza he picked up a few days ago. They threatened to break a window if he didn’t get to
their destination within five minutes. Attempting to break the awkward silence, the driver gestured
outside the window and stated “Y’know I half expected there to be rain tonight, but it’s an
uncharacteristically beautiful sky tonight in Kamurocho. Do you tend to prefer the rain or a clear
sky, Sir?”
"... I don’t particularly have a preference, but if I had to choose, I guess a clear sky,” replied Kiryu a
bit clumsily, as if the driver had interrupted his thoughts.
“... I see.” Not wanting to potentially upset his new customer, he waited a few minutes and asked
another question changing subjects. “If you don’t mind me asking, what do you do for a living,
Sir?”
“I run a real estate business,” replied Kiryu dryly.
“Aha, I could tell you were quite the successful businessman. I hadn’t expected a CEO though,
much less one of your age. You must have worked quite hard to get to where you are today. How
long have you been working?”
“Almost four-and-a-half years now. I started around January 1979.”
“Really, and in such a short amount of time, too? You must’ve been an incredibly hard worker, sir.”
“Well, … my father actually helped me get into the company. He doesn’t work for them, but you
could say he has connections.” Kiryu said, somewhat embarrassed.

The driver faked a laugh to break the tension saying “Haha, that’s fine, Sir. I don’t judge. We all
have our paths in life.”
The driver decided it was best to change topics quickly. “I believe around the time you started your
career, there was a big scuffle in the world of real estate. There was a small lot of land that
supposedly a bunch of yakuza ended up fighting over. Some inner power struggles within the Tojo
Clan, or at least that’s how the story goes. I remember hearing about it from another customer who
worked in real estate. Now I’m just asking this to satiate my personal curiosity, but would you
happen to know anything about that incident?”
Kiryu smirked a little, and then replied, “Why do you ask? Did you think I was a part of the
yakuza?”
The driver felt alarmed and quickly replied in a raised tone, “N-No, sir! I would never assume
something like that. I just, um, thought you might know since you got into real estate around that
time. Honestly, nothing more than that.”
“Heh, don’t worry. I’m just a civilian. I’ve heard a few minor details that may or may not be true,
but I only know what you and everyone else have heard about it.”
“I… see, Sir. We shall be arriving at your destination shortly,” replied the driver, who was now
slightly less on edge.
Kiryu sat back in his seat and began to reminisce.
He asks if I know about the Empty Lot incident. I was right at the center of it. How could I not
know about it? I still have nightmares about it.
… That’s a part of my past I’d rather leave behind. I still keep in touch with a few friends there, but
my part in the Tojo Clan is long over. I’m just a normal civvy now trying to make an honest living.
It’s funny, though. I wonder what younger me would say to his future self today.
I didn’t think I’d stay at this real estate agency, but Dad insisted that I did. Part of me still wants to
be in the Tojo Clan despite everything that has happened. My experience with the Dojima family
wasn’t exactly a happy one, but it was still a time I cherished. Getting to beat up arrogant punks,
not having a care besides what your next order was, Nishiki and I talking regularly at Serena with
Reina serving us some sake, etc.
Of course, it wasn’t all sunshine and rainbows. The number of times I nearly died during December
of that year…
Kiryu furrowed his brow as his shoulder started to itch remembering vividly getting shot there.
Never mind, why am I even pursuing that line of thought? The whole reason I decided to stay a
civvy was to get away from that. … Yes, even now, part of me still feels I should be in the yakuza. It
was more than just an occupation to me; it was my lifestyle. It was everything I idolized in my
father, though a poor part to idolize it was. I love and respect my father and appreciate everything
he’s done for me… I can also acknowledge he’s not exactly a saint.
It was for the best I committed to an honest living.

I could've gotten to the top of the Tojo, but that would mean joining the corrupt individuals that’d
do anything to achieve power and get what they wanted. I strived to follow the honorable code of
those like Dad and Kuze. I still do to this day, but the civvy life is the best for me now.
Kiryu then winced, recalling a specific memory.
... How long has it been since I thought about Kuze? I can still feel the impact of his punches from
our last fight. He was simultaneously the greatest man I ever met besides my father, and also the
murderer of the one man besides Nishiki I could call a true friend during those times.
If he saw me today, he’d punch my lights out and give a long lecture on how much of a
disappointment I’ve become.
I'm still good in a fight, and it feels like you need to be here in Kamurocho considering how
common they are. I almost never do due to my reputation, but I stay fit.
No way I could beat the boss in a fight these days, though. I was serious when I said I’d rather fight
100 Tojo Clan members than him, and I still stand by that statement. They are few and far between,
but people in this city exist that could take on waves of fighters before becoming exhausted.
Kiryu slightly smiled.
I suppose I did some crazy stuff myself. After that blew over, Nishiki would tease me, saying I could
take on the entire Tojo Clan and not break a sweat. That I was some “superhuman freak of nature”.
I’ve never met my real parents so I couldn’t say if it was genetics or what, but I guess I lucked out
as far as my fighting ability goes. ... Enough about that, though.
Kiryu sighed and noticed they were about to reach Serena.
…I wonder how Nishiki is. It’s been a month or so since we last spoke. I’ve been meaning to get in
contact with him, but life has become all too busy. I'm glad we were able to schedule a meeting
tonight for old times' sake.
“We’ve arrived at our destination, Sir. That’ll be ¥1,280.” stated the taxi driver.
Kiryu fumbled with his wallet for a second, handed the yen to the driver, and got out of the car.
“Have a nice evening, sir!” The driver said, being grateful that nothing bad happened.
“You too.”
The taxi drove off into the glamorously lit streets of Kamurocho Kiryu knew all too well.
Serena, huh? How many times have I been to this bar over the years? 100 times? 500? It might as
well be a second home to me.
Kiryu walked up the stairs and entered Serena.
“Ah, if it isn’t Kiryu, we’ve been expecting you,” said Reina upon seeing Kiryu enter.
Nishiki had been drinking some local sake. He turned around, his face lighting up at the sight of
Kiryu. He energetically said to him, “Yo! Kiryu, I’ve been waiting for you. About time you showed
up. Get into a fight on the way again?”

Heh, as usual, he’s not changed one bit.
“The only fights I get into these days is fighting to find some free time,” replied Kiryu half hiding a
smile.
“Oh please, we both know you still love a fight. You used to look for fights just to waste time.”
Kiryu rolled his eyes and took a seat next to Nishiki.
“Hello Reina, I’ll have the usual,” said Kiryu.
“Of course, I’ll have it ready right away,” replied Reina cheerily.
“You seem cheerful tonight, Kiryu. Usually, you have some frown and serious look plastered on
your face,” teased Nishiki.
“Hey, I do smile every now and then. I have some time off from work for once to see an old friend.
I’d say I’m allowed to be happy.”
“Haha, you’re always so easy to get going. Poor Kiryu, always destined to take even the smallest
things in life so seriously.”
The two chuckled and bantered as they began to catch up with each other.
“How’s Dojima?” inquired Kiryu.
“Oh, you know how he is. Always whining about his glory days, and how he should be the real
chairman instead of Sera.”
“Yeah, that sounds right. How about you and the Tojo Clan?” I know you’re basically the third in
charge in Dad’s family these days.”
“Pretty good. Kashiwagi has even talked about me maybe becoming the head of my own family at
some point.” Nishiki said with confidence.
“Really? Well, congrats! Try not to waste all your money on some ratty suit and you might get that
position,” said Kiryu jokingly.
“Oy oy, that’s usually your thing. It took you becoming the CEO of a company to dress in a decentlooking suit. It’s pretty much all you wear too, don’t you get tired of wearing the same old gray and
red combo? When you said you might wear that suit forever, I assumed you were joking.”
“Heh, I do love it. I have more than just one copy of this shirt and suit. Even I wouldn’t wash and
wear the exact same clothes every day.”
“And yet you’re the only man I know who has that many pairs of the same suit and shirt. I can only
imagine the bizarre look on the cashier’s face as you came in one day just to buy a dozen pairs of
the same suit and shirt.”
Both laughed and continued to drink their sake.
“Ok, Kiryu, be honest with me. Surely, by now, you’re dating someone, right? Don’t tell me the
great Dragon of Dojima is still single?” Nishiki asked mockingly.

Kiryu gave an annoyed look, and in a mildly harsh tone replied, “You know I’ve never been great
with women. I’m… just not sure if I’m ready for a relationship.”
“Haha, you should consider yourself a lucky man. Do you know how many guys would kill to have
what you have? You’re tall, handsome, rich, strong, humble, and kind. what more do I need to list?
You’re the ideal guy for women. The only thing stopping you from getting a girl is yourself.”
“... Look most of that money I just give away to the likes of charity or orphanages. I’m not saying
I’ll never date someone, and I know I’m not getting any younger. Just give me some time.”
Nishiki exaggerated a sigh and said, “He’s a lost cause, I swear.”
The two took a drink as they listened to the somber music playing in Serena.
“Well, if you’re not looking for romance, what else are you planning to do in the future?” asked
Nishiki.
Kiryu stopped drinking for a second and hesitated to answer.
What… do I want to do in the future?
Kiryu let the sake go down his throat and then replied, “Honestly, I’m not sure.”
“Oh really?” Nishiki said, a bit surprised.
“I’ve never been one for long-term planning. I just sort of took it day by day. I only had to think
about my next order when I was in the Tojo Clan. With this job, it did take some getting used to,
but I’m in a routine now.”
Nishiki pondered about what Kiryu said for a moment and then shrugged his shoulders. “Well, I
guess if you wanted to you could retire. You have enough money to probably last you for life.”
… Retire huh? Nah, I do still plan to work, but there is some appeal to the idea. Life is so busy
these days. I wouldn’t mind having the free time.
Even then, where would I retire at? Maybe in Sotenbori? … No, too similar to Kamurocho for my
liking. Hmm, Okinawa is a pretty nice place. Maybe I’d work for a few more years, save up, and
build an orphanage there. How much money would it take though, to keep that running for several
years? I have about five billion yen in the bank, but buying land and then building a whole
orphanage isn’t exactly a cheap goal.
Kiryu stopped his train of thought, as he noticed Nishiki now had a rather serious look on his face.
“Is there something wrong, Nishiki?” asked Kiryu concerned.
Nishiki reacted briefly shocked, realizing Kiryu had noticed his expression and then donned a more
cheerful expression saying, “Oh no, I was just thinking about something.”
Kiryu was still concerned, but he decided to not think about it and took a sip of his sake. There was
still some tension in the air, but out of respect for Nishiki’s privacy, Kiryu decided to not push the
issue if Nishiki wasn’t comfortable sharing.

Suddenly, Nishiki asks Kiryu a bizarre question. “Kiryu… have you ever heard of a small town
named Hinamizawa?”
Hinamizawa? … Is this related to whatever is bothering him?
Before continuing, Nishiki signaled to Reina to leave them alone for a bit as they wanted to talk
privately. While Reina was confused, she quickly realized it must be something important and went
to the back.
“Um, no, I can’t say I have. Why did you bring it up?” asked Kiryu, now genuinely worried.
Nishiki reclaimed the serious face he had earlier and answered Kiryu back. “It’s a small town in the
hills west of Kamurocho. It’s about a five to six hour drive from here. There’s also a more
developed city by the name of Shishibone near it. There’s a Yakuza group by the name of the
Sonozaki Family that runs the area.”
Kiryu relaxed a bit.
Ah, so it’s just some Tojo Clan BS. He’s probably looking to ask me for some advice on how to deal
with it.
“Ah, I assume the Tojo Clan got a bit too greedy and ended up messing around on someone else’s
turf?”
“... Not exactly. There was a man that was born in Hinamizawa that moved to Kamurocho about a
year ago. He took a loan from one of the offices under the Tojo Clan and racked up 3 million yen in
debt. He ended up running away back to Hinamizawa, and of course, two guys were sent to go after
him.”
Poor guy. They probably charged the guy some crazy interest rates to gouge money out of him, and
when he couldn’t pay up, they broke most of his bones. Worst case scenario, he’s sleeping with the
fishes now. These yakuza-run loan shark places are a dime a dozen here in Kamurocho. If I had my
way, I’d teach every one of them a lesson. You can still get money for the family as a yakuza,
without resorting to such underhanded methods.
I know I’m not entirely one to speak. I used to beat up people who owed money if they couldn’t pay
up. That was even how the whole Empty Lot incident started. At the least, though, those people I
beat up were usually scummy and were trying to run away to make a quick buck. I regret beating up
any of the innocent people, but also if you play stupid games expect to win stupid prizes. You don't
mess with the Yakuza.
Nishiki lowered his voice and then whispered, “... Those two never came back.”
They were… murdered? Well, that’s not entirely common upon entering enemy turf, and yakuza, in
general, don’t live long lives.
“... One of them was found to have supposedly killed himself by clawing out his own throat, and
the other was found in a sewer with their guts ripped out and several nails in each hand.”
Kiryu froze unable to comprehend what Nishiki had just told him.
“What… did you just say Nishiki?” Kiryu asked in disbelief.

Nishiki solemnly continued, “The man killed in the sewer was Koji Shindo. Nobody knows what
happened to the runaway, but he’s most likely alive too.”
A chill ran down Kiryu’s spine.
Koji Shindo?! … I don’t know him very well, but I know he was a good friend of Nishiki’s. He was
also extremely gifted at combat and had better instincts than your average man. You’d need to have
a considerably stronger two to three men to deal with him; much more so with him combined with
another capable yakuza.
And you’re telling me he… died… and in such a gruesome way, too? The yakuza aren’t above using
torture. Majima told me once how he spent a year in The Hole. It was some of the worst torture
imaginable.
Even that, though, is nothing compared to this. Something that causes a man to claw out his own
throat? Nailing a man down, and ripping out his inner organs? That’s not just torture; that’s a
scene in a horror movie. For what purpose would they even do such a thing? To set an example?
Not even the cruelest of yakuza would pull a stunt like this, and I refuse to believe the entirety of
this Sonozaki Family is just full of psychopaths.
“It has quite a few higher-ups shaken. Dad said he had never seen anything like it before,” said
Nishiki bluntly.
“What kind of sadistic human would do that, if you could even call them human?”
“I don’t know Kiryu. What we both know is that the Tojo Clan won’t take this sitting down. In
worst case scenario, this could lead to war. I’ve heard rumors Dojima is even seeing this as an
opportunity to maybe reclaim his former glory.”
A rush of emotions swirled through Kiryu’s mind.
They can’t be serious, right? A whole war against a group of country bumpkin yakuza? … No, they
could be serious, but something is missing here.
“Nishiki I understand that this isn’t just something the clan can ignore, but go to war? They
wouldn’t pull as drastic of a move as this, without some other reason.”
Nishiki opened his mouth to begin speaking again, but cut himself off.
Whatever this is, it must be something severe enough to warrant caution only placed towards the
likes of the Omi Alliance.
Nishiki then began to tell a horrifying story. “I don’t know all the details about this, so bear with
me. Supposedly, there’s been a series of deaths in Hinamizawa every year since 1979. It was only
two every year, but the part nobody seems to get is the deaths happening on the same day every
year during a local festival called the Watanagashi. They were all considered accidents, suicides, or
murders, but the constant element within all of them was an air of uncertainty. Each individual case
has been resolved by the police, but they’re not considered a connected series of deaths, despite the
strange… 'coincidence’ of them all happening on the same date.”
Kiryu was utterly speechless.

“It doesn’t take a genius to come to the conclusion the Sonozaki Family is behind the murders, or at
least that’s how the rumors go. There was never enough evidence to say specifically if it was them
or not, but they’re the first culprit that comes to mind. That’s why the Tojo Clan is taking this so
seriously. I’m sure the top brass had heard about these rumors before, but paid them no mind…
until now at least”
The two remained silent for a short while.
Nishiki then interjected: “Ah… ahahaha, sorry Kiryu, I didn’t realize this would mess with you so
much. We always let each other vent our problems to one another, so I figured this would be fine to
talk about. It seems this gave you a bit of a spook, though. Let’s just move on from that topic; we’re
here to have a fun night. No need to rain on our parade with depressing yakuza stories. It’s not
anything you have to worry about anyways, right? … Right, Kiryu?”
Kiryu didn’t respond, still trying to take in what he had just heard.
… Ok, let me get this straight. Some small town in the hills of Japan is also home to a yakuza
group more nefarious than even the Tojo or Omi at their worst. They kill two people every year on
the same day and can get away with there being no evidence of their involvement. They’re also
willing to make an example of two enemy yakuza that enter their turf in an incredibly brutal
fashion.
No, this can’t just be a group of yakuza. There’s something far darker and disturbing behind the
scenes here. Either that or the nature of the yakuza is just getting worse and worse every year.
Honor? Pride? These pricks have none of that. They’re nothing but a bunch of monsters, maybe
even demons masquerading as humans.
… And the Tojo is considering going to war, too? Normally I wouldn’t care about this war. It’s rare,
but usually, this stuff takes care of itself. Dad and Kashiwagi can more than handle themselves, and
Nishiki would probably be left behind to guard Kamurocho. He can also handle himself well, too.
It’s just… if Dojima is serious, this could spell disaster. He might act on his own devices, and use
this as an excuse to use reckless methods. Nishiki and absolutely dad would be sent to the front
lines. I probably shouldn’t worry, but still… I have such a horrid feeling about this. If something
were to happen to dad, Kashiwagi, or… Nishiki…
…
…
…
“Uh Kiryu, you good man?” Nishiki inquired.
The look on Kiryu’s face could only be described as deadly serious. He was gritting his teeth and
was squeezing his fist so hard his sake glass would have easily broken by now, if he was still
holding it. After a minute, Kiryu calmed down and finally answered.
“Let me handle this, Nishiki,” said Kiryu sternly.
“... Pardon me, Kiryu?”

Kiryu now looked Nishiki directly in the eyes with a serious look. “I said let me handle this.”,
repeated Kiryu. Nishiki had not seen Kiryu like this in years, but he all too well knew what it
meant.
Nishiki then, in a low tone growled at Kiryu. “You can’t be serious, Kiryu! I know you tend to be
reckless, but this is idiotic even for you. You’re the strongest man I know, but not even you can
handle this alone. You got out of the Empty Lot incident. You now have a life some would kill for.
You did all this to get away from the yakuza, and now you just want to jump right back into hellfire
and throw it all away? No, not on my watch.”
“Please Nishiki, hear me out. Think about it. I’m a civilian with deep ties to the Tojo that barely
anyone is aware of. I have an excuse/cover in wanting to retire somewhere as some rich CEO, that
has more than enough cash as proof. I can go undercover, and provide details to you or someone
else in the Tojo. I could maybe even get a job there, and gain the favor of the community. I can-”
“Stop, Kiryu,” Nishiki interrupted. “I full well know you’re not the type to concoct some hairbrained spy plot to figure out the truth behind a crime. You’re not a superhero; you’re just my
friend. If this is you worrying about me and dad, well, I appreciate the gesture. However, this isn’t
your battle. I know I couldn’t stop you with force even if I wanted to, but I sure can do everything
in my power to convince you not to pursue this as both my sworn brother and best friend. I also
know there’s more to this than you’re letting on.”
Kiryu lowered his head briefly in rejection but then raised it more determined than before.
“Nishiki I can’t really explain it, but deep down in my gut I know if I don’t get involved in this,
something terrible will happen. Maybe it is crazy to say this goes beyond even what the Tojo is
capable of dealing with, but that’s how I feel now. You’re right, it’s also insane to want to get
involved with this. You know what, though? I’d be lying if I said I didn’t have to convince myself
every day it was the right choice to leave the yakuza. It wasn’t just my occupation Nishiki, it was
my life. My very being, the core of who I was as a person. The least I can do is repay everything
dad and you have given me, and help you both with this. I can do all of this, while still being just a
civvy. I promise I’m not going to get killed. I refuse to die until I uncover the truth behind this. Yes,
part of it is wanting to protect you and dad, but I can’t just ignore this. Please Nishiki, I beg you.
Let me help with this.”
Silence enveloped the two. Time itself seemed to stop as the two looked at each other with equally
resolute wills. Nishiki eventually sighed and took a sip of his sake.
“Kiryu, I swear man. Why are you always like this? I know it’s what makes you… you, but you
really are your own worst enemy.”
Kiryu let Nishiki take a few minutes to figure out how to answer him.
… Ok fine, I’ll help you. I can’t stop you when you get like this. However, if you’re set on this,
you’d best 100% commit to it. Get someone to look after your company, pack whatever you need,
do whatever you have to do. Just make sure you’re ready. I’ll talk to dad, and he’ll put a good word
in. He’ll be disappointed, but also he knows how you are. He’ll understand.”
Kiryu smiled and thanked him. “I’m grateful, Nishiki.”
“However!” Nishiki hissed with a grim face. “You’d best not get into any serious trouble. If you do,
I’ll personally drive up to Hinamizawa and beat you up so badly you’d wish you were never born!

Promise me brother to brother, you’ll be safe.”
Kiryu, still with a smile on his face affirmed, “Of course, I wouldn’t have it any other way. I
promise Nishiki. I’ll be ok.”

~~~~

And thus began a new, unexpected tale for the Dragon of Dojima. A boy who just wanted to seek
redemption. A girl divorced from happiness. The daughter of an infamous family, and the cruel
birthright she carried. Her sister, a victim of heartbreak. A young girl, who just wanted to have a
happy family. And a girl and goddess dedicated to fighting against fate no matter how long it may
take to change. A cruel, nigh endless river of tragedy awaited. An absurdly cruel tale. And yet,
nothing was set in stone. How would the arrival of the Dragon change these people, and how would
they change him? Only time would tell.

Chapter 2: Dragon Slaying Arc Chapter 1: Arrival of the Dragon
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It’s the middle of July 1983. The cicadas raised their harmonious cry waking Kiryu from slumber.
Ugh, I never thought some noisy bugs would become my alarm clock, but life is just full of
surprises.
Kiryu got out of bed and got ready for his continued new life in Hinamizawa.
Man, it’s been about three and a half weeks since I talked to Nishiki that night at Serena and about
two weeks since I’ve been in Hinamizawa. Damn, a lot has happened since then.
Kiryu thought about everything that had happened since then as he showered.
Nishiki kept his word and talked to their Dad about it the next day. Kiryu knew considering he got
one pissed-off call from him on the phone later that day. He told him what he had said to Nishiki,
and then some. Once Kiryu had made his case, his father sighed and said he’d bring it up with
those at the top.
I'm still a little surprised they so readily approved me doing this. I know I got the moniker of
'Dragon of Dojima' from my times during the Empty Lot Incident, but it feels weird to have so much
clout all these years later. Is this why so many punks try to fight me? Do they hear about the rumors
of 'The Dragon'? Ugh, I honestly wish I never got that name. It's so tiring.
Secretly, Kiryu did like its relation to the dragon tattoo on his back. Back tattoos are considered
sacred by the yakuza. Each one tells a special story about the fate of the one who bears it. The
silver dragon on Kiryu's back represented a brave, ferocious protector, but also one pure of heart.
Nishiki, however, held a koi tattoo. To Kiryu, this represented Nishiki's unending ambition and how

Jirou himself took a look around, and then in a barely audible whisper continued, “There’s even a
rumor they kidnapped the Minister of Construction's son for ransom. At the least, he was gone for
almost a week and then found in the mountains near Hinamizawa. That was enough to finally halt
construction on the dam.”
Kiryu was mildly shocked, but wore a stern gaze.
While not the same as the sort of stuff the Tojo has done, it’s pretty similarly bad. Standard yakuza
behavior. However, to kidnap the son of a minister? I don't know if even the Tojo could get away
with that.
“However, the final nail in the coffin for this project would be the death of the Construction
Manager. It didn’t start as murder, but a fight broke out between the workers and the manager. He
ended up being killed, and his corpse was dismembered into six pieces.”
Kiryu looked as if he had seen a ghost.
… The workers… did what?
“It seems the plan was to divide up the body parts between six people so that the body could be
more easily hidden and the six swore each other to secrecy lest they be caught. However, one of the
workers that night went to the hospital for his injuries and out of guilt confessed to his crime. From

that, they were able to capture five of the six criminals; but one carrying the right arm of the victim
was never caught.”
A disturbing, but effective plan. Would be standard procedure in the Tojo.
“That’s not the strangest part, though. It’s not just that he was never caught; he straight-up
disappeared”
“... Wait, what do you mean? They never found him?”
“I mean, they really never found him. During the whole dam project, Oyashiro was the symbol of
hope and rebellion against the project the town used to rally each other into action. Belief had been
waning in the figure over the years, but this heavily revitalized belief in Oyashiro and again united
Hinamizawa. Some say that the missing criminal being ‘demoned away’, and that the Construction
Manager dying were both as a result of ‘Oyashiro’s curse.’”
Kiryu at this point was considerably disturbed.
Demoned away?! What the hell is that supposed to mean? People don’t just disappear for
supernatural reasons. The truth is that they really couldn’t find his body, or more likely is that it
was the doing of the Sonozaki family. Why would they want to silence him specifically, despite the
other five being caught? I don’t know, but it could be for a multitude of reasons. It’s been
established these people don’t run on common sense.
Kiryu then promptly asked, “Jirou, what is “demoned away” supposed to-”
Before Kiryu could finish, Jirou interrupted him now with a friendly expression. “Ah, I’m sorry,
Kiryu. That’s the extent of my knowledge. I’m only really familiar with those first deaths. I can say
that the deaths each year past that are considered a part of Oyashiro’s curse as well, but that’s about
it. I do have a good… friend that’s fairly knowledgeable about the history of Hinamizawa and the
murder cases, but she’s not with me as you can see, haha.”
Kiryu looked a little displeased but then remembered the other question he had in mind. “That’s
fine, but I did have one other question. Have you heard anything about two yakuza from the Tojo
Clan that came up here to Hinamizawa, and were eventually found murdered?”
It was Jirou’s turn now to be befuddled. “N-No, did that happen recently?”
“Yeah, I happened to hear about it one night on the news. Normally yakuza dying on enemy turf
isn’t uncommon, but it was more the state of their corpses that was so shocking. I’ll, uh, spare you
the details. I assume you’ll be eating dinner soon and I’d hate for you to lose your appetite.”
The color left Jirou’s face as he thought about what could’ve happened. “I’m… grateful. It’s
probably nothing I need to know anyways,” Jirou replied with a nervous smile.
Kiryu felt something was a little off, and he felt it necessary to ask Jirou one last question. “I
appreciate the in-depth recalling of the events, but I’m a little surprised you indulged so much info
to someone you just met. Not to offend you, it just sets off the skeptic in me.”
Jirou let out a chuckle. “Haha, well, in some ways you remind me of myself when I was younger. I
wasn’t too much older than you are now when these events happened, and they’ve stuck with me. I

just feel like I’m doing a favor for a fellow outsider and Tokyo resident. I mean, you also said you
were such a fan of mystery and drama, I figured you’d want the full story.”
“Ah… ah yes, I did say that,” Kiryu said embarrassed, realizing it was a somewhat dumb question
considering the lie he told. “You’re right, though. That was an extremely interesting story. Thank
you. Would you mind if I bought you some drinks sometime to repay the favor?”
“Oh wow, I wasn’t expecting anything in return, but I’ll certainly take you up on that offer at some
point.”
Orange light shined through the trees as both men realized the sun had started to set.
“Shoot, I’d best get back to my hotel before it gets dark,” said JIrou. “It was nice meeting and
talking to you, Kiryu. I wish you success in your new life here in Hinamizawa. Also, despite what I
said, you shouldn’t be afraid of anything. There’s certainly no curse, and just because it happened
previously doesn’t mean something will happen again at this year’s Watanagashi. The people here
are quite friendly, just uh… make sure you don’t bring up what we talked about here. Have a nice
night, Kiryu!”
“Um… you too! I hope you get some nice pictures of the birds here and enjoy yourself.”
Kiryu stood there, still mildly dazed from everything he’d just heard. Jirou waved and then walked
down the path. As Jirou left Kiryu’s sight, he finally noticed that the cicadas had been eerily quiet
for the whole conversation. They almost appeared to be silently judging him for learning forbidden
knowledge.
… This year’s Watanagashi festival is less than a week away. Would another pair of murders
happen again? … No, it’s not a matter of “would”, it’s a matter of “when”. Despite what Jirou
said, it’s happened four years in a row. Why would they suddenly stop on the fifth? It can’t be Koji
Shindo and his partner; those two were killed at least a month before the festival. So that leaves the
question of who will die this year, and when they’d strike.
Most people will be at the festival, so any stragglers still hanging around town at night are perfect
targets. I can’t pinpoint an exact location, but it would be somewhere here in this town. The more
distressing question is again, who dies? I don’t know the age or gender of the other victims that
died in this series of murders, so I can't pinpoint if they're just targeting men.
Kiryu suddenly recalled a book he had read once about ancient Japan and the rituals that happened
during those times.
At this point, I’m convinced they aren’t just normal yakuza. It's just a theory, but maybe Koji's
brutal death resulted from some ancient, religious ritual? It would explain the bizarre and horrid
death he endured. The clawing of the throat sounds like some sort of drug, but Koji’s death is far
more involved and sadistic. Ancient rituals like that would have several men or women sacrificed.
In the worst-case scenario, they’d even sacrifice… children.
A horrid possibility crossed Kiryu’s mind. One that awakened a primal level of rage within him.
Kiryu clenched his fists and growled in a deep but quiet voice acting as if he was threatening the
entirety of Hinamizawa.
“If any of those bastards so much as touch even a hair on any of my students’ heads, I’ll bury the
whole Sonozaki family. The Tojo won’t have to worry about going to war. I’ll take care of it

myself.”
Unbeknownst to Kiryu, the presence of a small girl was watching him from not too far away. With
a worried look on her face, she quietly talked to herself, “Oh no… I could be wrong, but… I think
he has the syndrome.”

Chapter End Notes

Elsewhere, the club had been doing their usual tomfoolery in the afternoon once school was done.
Keiichi then asked out of the blue, “Hey, what do you guys think of Teach?”
The other members paused the game, and Rena inquired, “You mean Mr. Kiryu? Why do you ask
Keiichi?”
“Well, I just thought about it, and I’ve only been here in Hinamizawa a little longer than he has.
We’re both in similar situations, so I wonder about him sometimes. At first glance, he’s a very
strong and reliable guy. He’s pretty relaxed and doesn’t seem to mind our antics as much as Ms.
Chie does. However, I feel there’s a lot more to him than meets the eye.”
“Hmm, I heard a rumor the principal challenged him to a duel, and he won." Mion replied.
“Huuuuuuuuh?! There’s no way he could’ve beaten our principal, right? Teach is strong, but the
principal is one of the strongest men in Japan.” Keiichi shivered. “I can still vividly remember what
happened when I had to touch his bald head as a penalty.”
“I heard that’s how he got the job. The two seemed to become best friends after that. The principal
must appreciate having a man on the same level as him in this village. … Fufufu, I mean Mr. Kiryu
must be incredibly strong if he can take a punch from our Rena fully powered up."
Rena blushed and fumbled with her words. “I-I didn’t mean to hurt him so badly. He should be fine
now, right? Right?”
Mion laughed and assured her friend, “Don’t worry Rena. Knowing the power of your punches, if
he can survive that he can survive anything.”
“Ooh, how many punks do you think he’s beaten up? He totally has the air of a guy, who could take
on a whole gang single-handedly.” Keiichi wondered.

Satoko clicked her tongue and mocked Keiichi. “Is through a lens of violence the only way you can
see him, Keiichi? While he might look like a barbarian, he has treated me like a proper lady as I
deserve. He’s also quite intelligent. I’ve rarely met an even match when it comes to my traps. Not
that I dare admit defeat to him. It’s only a matter of time before my genius gets the upper hand.”
“He reminds me of the main star of a yakuza flick. I can just imagine him going to an enemy
family, and wiping them out. He’d have some super cool tattoo on his back, and show it off as he
commences a shirtless battle with the final villain on a rooftop." Mion theorized.
“... I feel like you just made that last part up. What kind of yakuza films are you watching?” Keiichi
quipped.
“Only the goriest, most depraved, and darkest ones Kei. Something far beyond what you could
handle.” Mion answered with an overexaggerated smirk.
Keiichi rolled his eyes. “Rena, what do you think of him?”
“Hmm… Rena thinks Mr. Kiryu is a good person. I was afraid he’d get mad at me after what
happened, but he just smiled and encouraged me. He’s a very fun teacher to have.”
“I would agree. I know I would be pissed at you if you did that to me."
Rena’s expression became a bit more solemn. “Though, … I think Mr. Kiryu looks a little sad
sometimes."
“Sad?!” Keiichi exclaimed.
“He usually smiles, but sometimes he looks tired or worried. He might still be adjusting to
Hinamizawa. I think it might be nice to invite him to our club. Maybe he would feel more
comfortable here.”
“That’s… an excellent idea, Rena! We’ve never had an adult in our club before, but just imagine if
he loses and gets a penalty. It could result in some… interesting results fufufu,” Mion noted,
scheming up some unholy penalty.
Keiichi chuckled. “Can you imagine Teach in a maid's dress? We’d never let him live it down."
“H-Hauuuu, Rena would love to see Mr. Kiryu in a cute dress. I could take him home, and he
couldn’t object."
“Ohoho, I could have him teach Keiichi a lesson. Or perhaps, we could make the ultimate trick of a
trap together."
“Haha, hang on one moment guys. We don’t even know if he’ll accept our invitation. However, if
he does I hope he’s ready for the hardest challenge of his life!” Mion exclaimed.
Rika then suddenly interjected, “I’m… going to go to the bathroom. Please keep playing without
me until I get back.”
Before anyone could say anything, she turned away and rapidly exited the premises. The other four
were surprised as Rika hadn’t said anything up until that point.

When she had left, Keiichi's brow furrowed. “Did anyone else feel like Rika looked very dazed and
confused? She’s been normal all day, but I swear she looked very alarmed for a few seconds before
asking to leave.”
“Maybe she ate something bad and had to suddenly... you know.” Rena pondered, blushing a bit.
“It is rude to talk about such things in regards to a lady. Let us get back to our game now. Rika shall
be back shortly, I’m sure,” Satoko interrupted.
“Fufufu, well, she’d best get back here soon. Loose bowels or not, she’ll be facing a penalty if she
doesn’t come back soon.” Mion said ominously.

Rika didn’t go to the bathroom, but rather to the sheds behind the school. Now alone in a frantic
state, she began to speak with Hanyuu. She had just entered the body of this fragment’s Rika and
was trying to collect herself.
“What… what happened Hanyuu? I remember we were combining fragments, trying to solve
everything, and getting as many pieces for our side as we could. We were so close, I was getting
ready to speak to Akasaka in that one broken fragment when… something happened right? The
combined fragment started to crack, and I blacked out after that.”
“Au au au au au, Rika! Rika! Something terrible has happened!”
“Ok, calm down Hanyuu. Tell me what the date is?”
Hanyuu took a deep breath, and as calmly as she could stated, “It’s Monday, roughly one week till
Watanagashi…”
“One week?! Hanyuu, what happened while I blacked out?!”
“I-I don’t quite remember either. I was ready to put everything on the line and help everyone out in
this fragment. I thought this was going to be the last world, but I’m still stuck in this form. I’ve
only been here a little longer than you, but I’ve noticed someone… new in Hinamizawa”
“Hanyuu, there’s been certain fragments in the past where we saw a few people move in that
weren’t in Hinamizawa in other fragments. They were never important, though, in the grand
scheme of things. What’s different now?”
“Au au au, I… think he’s someone that works here at the school in this fragment. His name seems
to be Kiryu… something.”
Realizing Hanyuu wouldn’t have the answer, Rika began to rifle through the memories of this
fragment’s Rika to get information. After a few seconds, she began to reveal what she knew: “His
name is Kiryu Kazuma, but everyone calls him Mr. Kiryu. He seems to be a recently hired P.E.
teacher at school and moved here not too long after Keiichi arrived. He lives near Rena and seems
to be kind and good with the rest of the kids. For the first time, he taught us some self-defense
moves in class earlier today… that’s all I can gather Hanyuu. I can’t recall ever seeing him before
either, but why does he have you in such a panic?”

Hanyuu looked around to make sure no one was listening to them, not that anyone could hear or see
her in that form. She wore a grim expression and asked, “Rika, do you remember how we observed
Takano had an unwavering will, which has been the main reason she’s been able to kill you every
loop?”
Rika anxiously replied. “Y-yes, what does that have to do with this new Kiryu man?”
“... I wasn’t sure if I was mistaken at first or not, but I know now for sure. That man has a will as
unshakeable as Takano’s, if not possibly more so than her and all of us combined.”
Rika did a double-take bewildered at what she had just heard. “You are positive about this, right
Hanyuu?”
“I’m 100% positive”
Rika’s legs began to wobble, and pressing her back against the wall of the shed, she slid down to a
sitting position. She held her head in her hands unable to fully take in everything that had
happened. That aura of despair transformed into anger as she slammed her fist against the shed
tears running down her face.
“Dammit it! Why?! Why am I cast back into this hell?! Over 100 years of pain and torture. Over
100 years of dying over and over, trying to find a way out. I finally found out who kills me every
loop. I finally know why I couldn’t win ever. We were going to create the ideal 1983 fragment. We
were going to play all our pieces, no trust in our friends to make a miracle! We had everything set,
and now suddenly this bullshit happens?! To Hell with that!! I’m just supposed to accept this?!
Hanyuu, answer me! Why did this happen?! Did this ‘Kiryu person' suddenly screw us over? Is he
even involved?! You’ve been around for a thousand years; surely you can figure this out! Please,
Hanyuu, I beg you to give me an answ-”
“Enough!” Hanyuu commanded in a deep voice befitting the goddess.
Not another syllable escaped Rika’s mouth, as it was left agape in shock. This was the first time she
had seen Hanyuu genuinely angry in a long time, much less directed at her.
Hanyuu’s face softened as she began to lecture Rika. “Rika, I understand your pain. I’m frustrated
and confused too. I’m sorry, I can’t give you an answer. I don’t know the answer as is. However,
what I can say is that I refuse to let this deter me. I also refuse to be a bystander anymore. I’m
going to become a part of this game, and I will make sure we win it no matter what. I can’t do a lot
in this form, but I will still try my best. I swear it. Rika. I know things look grim, but we can
overcome this. Believe in your friends, and believe in me. Regardless of what comes, I promise we
can and will overcome it.”
Rika was awestruck, but eventually smiled and wiped away her tears. “You really have changed
Hanyuu. I can’t even imagine you saying that in the previous fragment. I guess you can be a decent
goddess sometimes.”
Hanyuu’s cheeks blushed. “Au au au, don’t tease me, please! I meant everything I said.”
“I know Hanyuu. You’re right, though. I’m sorry for losing my cool there.” She then collected
herself and began to speak sternly: "Let’s set some things straight here, and make a plan. We now
can only go up to roughly a week before Watangashi. We know Takano and the Mountain Dogs will
try to kill me sometime shortly after Watanagashi. As much as I hate to admit it, we likely won’t

get our chance in this fragment. We can, however, collect info on this 'Kiryu' man, and see what
else has potentially changed in this fragment for now. Something brought ‘Mr. Kiryu’ to
Hinamizawa, and whether the reason is, we need to find out the truth.”
Hanyuu nodded her head in agreement. “I’m going to go find Mr. Kiryu and follow him around. I
should be able to find out some key info and report back. Our friends were talking about maybe
inviting Mr. Kiryu to the club. Rika, you should push for that, and see if we can learn more about
him that way. Let’s do this!” She said enthusiastically as she held out her hand to shake it.
Rika looked away, stifling a laugh, and then looked back and smirked. “Oh Hanyuu, you poor
thing. Assuredly, you didn’t forget that even I can’t interact with you physically, right?”
Hanyuu’s face went red. “Au au au au, Rika, you’re the worst!”
“Hahaha, I’m sorry Hanyuu. I couldn’t help myself.”
Rika humored Hanyuu and held out her hand. Still mildly embarrassed, Hanyuu 'grasped' Rika’s
hand and shook it barely making eye contact.

It was now nighttime in Hinamizawa. The higurashi had grown quiet, and Hinamizawa was resting
as well. Satoko had fallen asleep, and Rika was sitting by her favorite window with the moonlight
casting down on her. It was there that the two girls began to discuss what they had learned.
Rika began speaking, “Ok, I talked to my friends, and they seem ok with Kiryu being a part of the
club. We plan to invite him tomorrow. Hanyuu, did you find anything out?”
“Yes, Mr. Kiryu took a walk before heading home and ended up meeting Jirou for the first time, it
seems. The two began to casually talk, but soon Mr. Kiryu brought up the incidents referring to
the… ‘curse of Oyashiro’.” Hanyuu said with a look of disgust.
I hate that phrase so much, but it’s the quickest way to clarify what I mean here.
Hanyuu continued, “Mr. Kiryu seems to be aware of the deaths, but doesn’t know the finer details.
Jirou then went on to tell him about Oyashiro, the curse, the gist of the dam war, and the events
surrounding the first murder. Mr. Kir-... you know what, I think, I’ll just call him Kiryu. I’m
considerably older than he is anyways.”
Rika smiled in response. “I’d say that’s fine. I’ll call him it when I’m around him or my friends, but
there’s no real reason to when we’re alone like this.”
“Anyways, Kiryu was going to ask about what ‘being demoned away’ meant, but Jirou cut him off
before he could ask. Now here is the key part Rika. Before they said goodbye to each other, Kiryu
asked whether Jirou had heard anything about two yakuza from the Tojo Clan that had been
murdered here in Hinamizawa in a brutal fashion, though he didn’t talk about how they were
murdered. He made it sound like he was just a fan of crime dramas and mystery, but I feel it’s
something deeper than that.”
Rika held up her hand inquiring, “Wait, back up. What is the Tojo Clan? I don’t recall that in any of
my memories.”

“I’m not entirely sure. I guess they’re some sort of yakuza organization like the Sonozaki Family?”
Rika pondered for a few minutes about what that could mean and then asked, “Do you think he’s
maybe a yakuza himself? Kiryu moved here from a place called Kamurocho in Tokyo. I know little
about Kamurocho, but I vaguely remember reading about how it’s the prime destination for
nightlife in Japan. I also remember reading it has a reputation for being the center of many
nefarious activities in the underworld. Assuming the Tojo Clan is located there, perhaps they sent
this Kiryu man undercover to try and find out more about what happened to those two murdered
yakuza.”
“Woah Rika, isn’t that maybe a leap in logic? I know you’re probably thinking it’s something
similar to the reason Akasaka came here in 1978, but Kiryu doesn’t seem to have the personality of
a yakuza.”
“Don’t judge a book by its cover. It’s just an idea at the moment, but it might be a trail worth
pursuing. My friends were joking about him being one earlier, but they could have been on to
something. He certainly has the build of one and has hawk-like eyes only those who’ve had their
life threatened one too many times have. One possibility is that he could be an ex-yakuza, but still
has ties to his family.”
“Au well, I guess it’s possible. It’s just, why would they hire an ex-yakuza at the school here with
kids?”
“If he has the resources, he could just have a good enough cover. Mii was able to help us hide
bodies in previous worlds; in comparison, a forged identity isn’t that crazy.”
“That’s true, Rika.”
“There’s also who killed those two yakuza, to begin with. In this case, it very well could be the
Sonozaki Family. They killed Rina in a way reminiscent of the Watanagashi in previous fragments
and she even died that way in the last world we were in. However, it also could be because of
Takano and the Mountain Dogs.”
“That’s true. We should look into that as well.”
“I can ask Mion about the Tojo tomorrow, and maybe I can catch Takano as well. Hanyuu, I’m
going to ask you to do me a favor that might make you uncomfortable, but it’s only something you
can do.”
Hanyuu had a resolute expression. “Of course, Rika. I’ll do whatever it takes.”
“Alright then. You know how just about every yakuza has a tattoo on their back, right? Even Mion
has one of a demon on her back.”
“Yes, what about it?”
Rika had a stern look and lowered her voice. “This is going to sound crazy, but bear with me. I
need you in the morning to go to Kiryu’s house, and see if you can catch him with his shirt off and
see his back. The most likely time you’ll be able to see that is… when he takes a shower or is
dressing.”

Two puffs of steam came out of Hanyuu’s ears as she became immediately red and flustered at what
Rika suggested. “W-What, Rika?! Au au au au, surely you’re joking, right? I-I can’t do that. Can’t
we find some other way?”
Rika smirked a bit and teased her. “What’s wrong, Hanyuu? You’ve lived for a millennium

“Au au au, I mean… I have, but it’s not like I’ve ever used my powers to do something perverted.
I’m not some filthy person trying to peep on people with my powers. I just… au” Hanyuu sighed,
and then says, “Ok fine Rika, I’ll do it. We’re low on time, and that would be the fastest way to
confirm this. You’d better treat me to some cream puffs tomorrow night, though, and I don’t want
to see you drinking at all this fragment.”
Rika chuckled to herself and smiled. “How foolish, Hanyuu. I don’t have time to waste away on
alcohol if I want to try my best here. We both already know that. Don’t worry though, I’ll reward

eternal June, even if it does take a few more loops.”
This was the most determined Rika had been in a long time. Hanyuu was still a bit surprised to see
this new Rika, but she too had changed and was just as eager to take this challenge on. “Au! Of
course, Rika! We will win.”
Rika began to brainstorm about what else could potentially be happening when she noticed
Hanyuu’s expression had changed to one of concern.
“What’s wrong, Hanyuu?”
“Nothing, it’s just… do you think Kiryu could maybe be our ally? Our friends seem to be very fond
of him. Once Jirou left, he also mumbled something angrily I couldn’t quite catch, but I think he
was saying something about protecting his students.”
“Hanyuu… you said it yourself. He is the most likely cause of this mess. He may not be our enemy
necessarily, but I doubt he’s our ally too. I never once considered Takano my killer and trusted her
as someone I thought I could call a friend, but now look where we are. The only people I can trust
are my friends, Akasaka if he shows up, and maybe the likes of Jirou, Ooishi, and Irie, depending
on what happens. We need to learn way more about our current circumstances and Kiryu himself,
before we can even remotely consider him an ally. I will act friendly with him to gain his trust, but
we should stay cautious for sure. You even mentioned earlier before the sun set how you thought he
may already have the syndrome.”
“I-I could be wrong, au au. It’s not like he was showing any particular signs of having it. I just
assumed him looking so stressed could have maybe caused it to flare up. He most likely has it by
now, anyway. I’m just not sure if he’s above L2 yet.”
“Either way, Hanyuu, my point stands. We need considerably more information than we have now,
before we can maybe trust Kiryu.”
“I…see”
As ready as both girls were to tackle the future, neither could anticipate what was to come. Kiryu
himself was also stuck in a web of confusion. Both parties needed to gain more information, and

needed to do so soon… or else.

Chapter 4: Dragon Slaying Arc Chapter 3: A Game of Luck
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It was Tuesday afternoon. Kiryu was resting in the teacher’s lounge, considering what to do for the
rest of the day.
Ugh, another day with not much progress. I talked with Nishiki last night about what I had learned,
but it sounds like the Tojo is starting to push more to go to war. Screw this, I need to get some key
information soon, or else I’ll have come here for nothing.
Jirou said a female friend of his might be able to tell me more about the series of murders, but at
this point, that’s not going to help me much. Ok so fine, the first murder under this “Curse of
Oyashiro” was by some workers and not the Sonozakis. They still could have been just as involved
in the other murders, and Nishiki told me they certainly don’t deny their possible involvement.
Kiryu leaned back in his chair and let out a sigh.
Even then, though, I don’t think it matters as much at this point. My top priority is figuring out who
killed those two yakuza. The Watanagashi murders being connected is just a possibility at the
moment, but nothing conclusive.
While Kiryu racked his brain, he wondered about a peculiar sight he had saw today.
Kiryu was not sure when, but at some point in his life he realized he could see certain “heat-like
auras” around people. Only incredibly strong men like Kuze had them, and he'd only see it when he
was fighting them. He brought the idea up with Nishiki once, but he just blew it off saying Kiryu
had taken one too many blows to the head.
Kuze wasn’t the only one to have had it. Kiryu had seen it most recently with Kaieda, but also
Tachibana, Nishiki, Majima, and perhaps most infamously was in his battle versus Shibusawa.
Kiryu was pretty surprised to learn that one day Majima could see them too and asked him what
they represent. Majima said they represented “those that have true inner strength.” Of course, he
did his usual maniacal laugh afterward and just said he was messing with Kiryu. Kiryu knew him
well enough at that point, though, to know he was lying. The line of thinking makes sense. All of
those people were the strongest people Kiryu had met.
So considering everything, Kiryu wondered why. Why the hell did Rika have a deep blue aura
during P.E.?
I can’t even begin to fathom why an 11-year-old girl has that aura. I felt something was a bit
special about her in my gut, but does she really have that same “inner strength” I and few others
do? Why did it also only show up today? I’ve seen her in class for over two weeks now. I just
somehow never noticed it until now?
I just don’t get it. This place gets more and more mysterious the longer I reside here. Is there
actually some stock in that “reincarnation of Oyashiro” stuff, or is it something else? She's acted
normal otherwise, but I can’t shake the feeling something serious has changed.

Kiryu once again sighed.
There’s a comically large gap between the number of questions I have and the number of answers
to those questions I’ve gotten. I’ve yet to get close enough to anybody to trust them, and I know I
don’t have much time left. If I only had a little more time, I could justKiryu’s thoughts were interrupted by the school bell signaling the end of the school day. Kiryu
grumbled to himself. “Hmph, well all this worrying isn’t going to get me anywhere. I can continue
to go into circles logically, or I could focus on what I can do today. I desperately need to do
something today too. I don’t know what, but the sinking feeling in my stomach deepens more as
each day passes by.”
Kiryu forced himself to have a smile on his face, as he walked out of the lounge. He usually said
goodbye to the kids, Chie, and Kaieda before leaving, so he figured he’d best wear a smile lest his
frustration seeped through and worried them.
As he was saying goodbye to everyone and was about to leave, Mion suddenly came up to him.
“Hey Mr. Kiryu, would you mind staying after school for a bit? We wanted to show you something
a little… special fufufu,” she laughed with a mischievous look in her eyes.
Kiryu was a little taken aback and wasn’t quite sure how to respond. “Um… sure, I don’t see why
not.”
“Great!” Mion shouted. “Come to the classroom in 15 minutes; we’ll be ready by then.” She then
ran back to the classroom leaving Kiryu alone.
… What was that about? What are those kids trying to pull now?
~~~~
Before Kiryu's eyes were gathered Keiichi, Mion, Rika, Satoko, & Rena. Each one had an
enthusiastic, but naughty look in their eyes. Kiryu was a little reminded of the many times punks
had tried to jump him In Kamurocho. Thankfully these were his students and not some goons about
to be sent to the hospital.
Mion would be the first to speak, “So Mr. Kiryu, I wanted to ask you something. You may know
me as the Class Representative, but did you know I also host an after-school club?”
“I can’t say I did Mion. Also just between us… I don’t mind you guys just calling me Kiryu. It’s
what my friends call me back home, and I’m not even too much older than you all. You can still
call me Mr. Kiryu if you’d prefer that, I just figured I’d give you the option,” replied Kiryu.
“Haha, that works out just fine. We usually refer to each other in our club like that anyways,” said
Mion. The other kids nodded in agreement.
“Well, anyways Mion, why do you keep bringing up this club of yours?”
“Well Kiryu, we’re not just any old club.”
Mion then crossed her arms and struck a confident pose.

“Behold! The Magician of Words Keiichi! The Unstoppable, Cute Thing Loving Rena! Trap
Master Satoko! The Bewitching Moe Girl Rika! And finally…” Mion pointed to herself. “The
leader of this elite club, I Mion Sonozaki! Together we make up THE premier club of Hinamizawa
Branch School! You may think we just play games here, but no. We put our lives on the line every
day! The loser/s of each game receive a harsh penalty, and one can only win by using every method
at their disposal. We decided you meet the qualifications to be in our club Kiryu. However, if you
accept our invitation, you may sorely regret it. Do you dare take on our invitation Kiryu?!”
Silence filled the room until Kiryu suddenly smirked and chuckled. “Oh, so you think you can beat
me at some paltry games? Believe it or not, I was quite successful at the likes of poker, mahjong,
and shogi back in Kamurocho. I would be wary of letting me into your club, to begin with. You
might fear what you’ve unleashed.”
A way to bond with the kids quickly? This is almost too good to be true. These club activities
themselves won’t reveal anything to me, but this is the perfect way to get to know them and gain
their trust. I wish I knew about this sooner, but I might finally have the lucky break I’ve been
looking for.
“Very well, Mion. I shall accept your invitation,” Kiryu announced with a self-assured expression.
The club members cheered, and Mion then said to Kiryu, “Prepare yourself, Kiryu. You get some
beginner’s luck today. We’re playing poker. The first to lose all their chips shall receive the penalty.
Don’t think you can take it easy, though, just because you’re experienced. We’re quite good
ourselves.”
“Try me,” Kiryu responded confidently.
“Oh, also you should know Kiryu, there’s another reason to not take it easy on us. The penalty for
today is to go tell Ms. Chie curry sucks… loudly fufu.”
Sweat begins to form on Kiryu’s brow.
… Oh, so it’s that kind of penalty. Well, I should be fine. On the off chance, I do lose, I can take the
resulting consequences … probably.
Mion walked to a locker in the back of a classroom full of numerous games and grabbed a card
pack and several poker chips.
How on earth does so much fit into that locker?! It looks way bigger on the inside than it does on
the outside.
The club members sat around a table with a seat prepared for Kiryu. “Come join us, Kiryu. Let’s
see just how good you are,” Mion gloated.
“Don’t say I didn’t warn you kids.”
~~~~
“How… did it come to this?” Kiryu muttered inaudibly to himself. A half-hour had passed at this
point, and Kiryu was in a poor position.

Look, I’ll admit, I’m not the best poker player in the world. Still, I’ve held my own against pretty
good players. I’ve even won games in scummier areas of Kamurocho, where they’d cheat. However,
these kids are way too good for their age.
Kiryu thought he had a pretty good poker face, but it's as if these kids were reading his every move.
Each of them were incredible in their own way. Keiichi lost the first few rounds but had an amazing
clutch factor thus far. Mion backed up her banter and had gotten a good amount of wins. Satoko
was good at leading the others on, and Kiryu could never quite get a good read on her. Rena would
challenge your bluffs and could read through just about any of their poker faces. Finally, Rika had
been pretty 50/50 on winning or losing, but she maybe had one of the best poker faces Kiryu had
seen.
I’ve lost most of my chips at this point, and if I lose just two or three more rounds… that might be
curtains for me.
Mion then dealt cards, and while Kiryu made sure to keep his poker face, a glint could be seen in
his eye for just a millisecond.
Two kings?! Wait, this might be what I needed to turn this around. C’mon, think Kiryu! There has to
be some sort of trick to this. These kids are good, but they’re not Kamurocho good. Mion even said
in the beginning that one can only win by using any options they have. I had a feeling this wasn’t
entirely a fair game, to begin with, but how could they be cheating? There must be something I’ve
missed. Maybe the deck itself?
Kiryu analyzed the deck and then froze.
Wait, that’s it! It’s the deck! This is an old, used deck with a lot of the cards having certain
scratches on them.
It was maybe five to six years ago Kiryu was doing a game with some lower-ranking Tojo
members. They weren’t entirely fond of him, being the son of a yakuza high up in the Tojo and
“having it easy”. They challenged Kiryu to a game, saying he needed to know his place. They had
used the exact same trick the kids were using now, and once Kiryu figured it out he won. Of course,
this was at the cost of having to punch the teeth out of some sore losers that day.
At this point, everyone had placed their bets, and Mion had turned over three of the five cards. A
king, an eight, and a seven. Kiryu desperately tried to recall what the identity of the two other cards
was based on their scratches.
What is it? What is it?! …Aha! That’s right! The fifth card is a king! I’m positive about it. Satoko
won a round earlier using it. I can’t remember the fourth card, but that’s fine. A four-of-a-kind of
kings should be more than enough to win this round.
“Oho, are you ok Kiryu? I saw your guard drop there briefly. Perhaps, you’re fresh out of luck?”
Satoko said mockingly.
“Fufu, I told you, you’d regret challenging us, Kiryu,” gloated Mion.
“Oh, don’t be so mean to Mr. Kiryu. He’s been doing pretty well for a first-time member,”
acknowledged Rena.

“Heh, well he still has a long way to go. It’s nothing personal, Teach. Let’s just say I was a newbie
not too long ago, and I think it’s fair you face the same trial by fire I did,” stated Keiichi.
A faint smile emerged from Kiryu. “Actually, I’m feeling pretty lucky.” Kiryu then bet half of his
remaining chips.
The kids were shocked to see Kiryu’s new confidence. “Feel free to fold, if you don’t feel like
playing this round,” Kiryu taunted.
Tension enveloped the room as the five kids remained silent and exchanged glances. They matched
Kiryu’s bet. Mion then revealed the fourth card.
Oh, it was a nine huh? Well, that’s fine, nothing to worry about. What will be revealed next is the
important part.
Kiryu then bet his remaining chips.
Satoko was astonished, and asked, “W-What?! Have you gone mad?”
“Do you think Kiryu has a plan? Does he?” Rena inquired, now worried.
Mion was at first bewildered but then went back to her previous smirk. “Ha! I’m impressed Kiryu.
It seems you finally found the fire you needed to win. I do wonder if you have a thing for
comebacks like our Keiichi here.”
“O-oy! He’s clearly just bluffing. Don’t fall for this Mion! He’s just trying to get us to fold
preemptively,” Keiichi said with not as much confidence as he would have liked.
“I’m afraid you kids are the ones that have a long way to go. You did stump me at first, but I’ve
seen my fair share of cheap tricks. It took some time, but I’d say I’m finally…” Kiryu then gestured
to the unique scratches and marks on his card. “... right on the mark.”
Not even Mion could hide her shock. The club members’ faces looked as if they had seen a ghost.
“You kids wouldn’t last a day in Kamurocho if these were your tactics.”
“J-just because you figured out about the scratches, doesn’t mean you’ve won the game yet!” Mion
shouted, now sweating a bit herself.
“Of course. Let’s continue the game then,” Kiryu said, still retaining a smug grin.
Everybody matched Kiryu’s bet again. Whoever won this round would completely turn the tables,
if not outright win the game. Mion then revealed the final card to be the fourth king, as everyone
also revealed their cards. The kids couldn’t believe their eyes at Kiryu’s hand.
“The fourth king, just like I predicted. Behold, a four-of-a-kind of kings,” Kiryu said pridefully.
The kids were defeated, and each began to fold their cards.
Kiryu leaned back in his chair, closed his eyes, and put his hands behind his head. “Let that be an
after-school lesson for today, kids. It’s ok though, you’ll have a chance to beat me next time.”
“Meep, it’s not over yet”

The other kids turned to look at Rika, who hadn’t spoken since the round started.
Kiryu opened his eyes and glanced at Rika. “Huh? Well, technically I’ll have to win at least one
more round. Still, though, I’m pretty much guaranteed to wi-”
Time itself seemed to stop for Kiryu.
… Why… hasn’t she folded her cards yet?
In Rika’s hands were a five and a six. Combined with the seven, eight, & nine cards, she had a
straight flush due to all five cards sharing the same suit. Unfortunately for Kiryu, a straight flush is
one of the few things in poker that can beat a four-of-a-kind.
“It seems like I win, after all, nipah!” Rika wore the smile of an angel, as if she had not just utterly
destroyed the pride of a man.
“Ah… ahahahahahahaha!” Mion would be the first to break the silence erupting into laughter. The
rest of the kids joined in soon after as they celebrated Rika’s victory. Kiryu could only sit there,
mouth agape at what had just transpired.
“Ohohoho, I should’ve known we could count on you, Rika,” said Satoko gleefully.
“That’s our Rika!” Keiichi joined in.
“Hauuu! How could Rena doubt Rika? She always comes through for us”
Mion then turned to Kiryu with an evil look in her eye. “Fufufu, you were very close, Kiryu. That
very easily could’ve turned the game in your favor, so I must praise your efforts for your first time
in our club. However, underestimating Rika was your fatal mistake. Shall we carry out the penalty
now?”
Kiryu didn’t look Mion in the eyes, but rather looked down at the table, completely humbled.
… Was I too reckless? Nishiki always says I am, but for it to screw me over here of all times?! …
This club isn’t your average school club. It's like I'm back in the yakuza, where one major mistake
can mean your pinky finger. In all honesty, I think I might prefer losing my pinky to what I’m about
to do next.
Kiryu then stood up and gave a slight bow. “As a man, I know when I’ve been defeated. I shall go
to Ms. Chie now."
As Kiryu left the room, Rika yelled at him. "Good luck Mr. Kiryu, Nipah!”
In reality, Rika had been putting on her usual persona and had been trying to learn anything about
Kiryu she could.
He’s smart and observant. He has all the confidence and charisma one could ask for. He can turn
situations around easily too. I only won that, because I got lucky… that, and playing with the same
deck for over 100 years makes it pretty easy to identify what card is what at this point.
He also seems to be at least somewhat acquainted with shady places, or maybe the entirety of
Kamurocho is full of filth. I didn’t fully believe Hanyuu when she told me, but I know now. He has
the same level of willpower as someone like Takano. He only showed it when he was trying to make

that comeback, but it was absolutely there. What the hell is going on, and how do we stop it?
What… if we have to stop him?
~~~~
Ah, Kiryu! I didn’t know you were still here. Did you need something?
Kiryu took a deep breath in preparation.
Let’s just get this over with.
Chie tilted her head in confusion. “Is something wrong, Kiryu?”
“Chie, please forgive me for what I’m about to say. I can only blame myself for being in this
predicament.”
Before Chie could say anything, Kiryu blurted out, “Curry is terrible, and it sucks!!”
Kiryu blinked and she was gone.
... People say humans don’t know true fear until they’ve had their lives threatened. I’ve had mine
threatened multiple times, and I can’t say I was ever in “true fear”. I was scared or nervous, but I
always pulled through. Now, though… I think I finally understand what people mean.
There's a presence from Hell itself behind me. She's grasping my shoulder with the strength of 100
men. I dare not look, lest I know the horrifying face of the demon behind me.
“... Ms. Chie?” Kiryu quietly asked, staring at the now empty chair in front of him.
“Kiryu… would you mind saying that again? For your sake, I hope I misheard”
“Ah… ahhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhhh!!!”

Chapter 5: Dragon Slaying Arc Chapter 4: The Curse of Oyashiro
Chapter Notes
