“Wahahahaha, I can’t believe you fainted, Teach!” Keiichi said, nearly falling over with laughter.
“Uh… yeah, I guess I did haha,” Kiryu said, feeling awkward about the situation.
Apparently, I yelled very loudly and fainted. The kids then rushed to check on me, and I woke up
shortly afterward in the medical room. The kids must’ve carried me there… they’re sweet, even if
they’re also technically the cause of this.
“Hauuu, you scared us, Mr. Kiryu. We had today’s penalty once before, and while she was
ferocious, she must’ve done something horrifying to you. Are you OK? Huh?” Rena asked
worriedly.
“I-I’m fine. I’ve dealt with worse. I think it was so fast and disorienting that I um… ahem.” Kiryu
coughed as any more would just prolong his embarrassment. “Anyways, kids it’s getting a little
late. We should start heading home, yeah?”
As if on cue, the somber song of the higurashi began to play.
Wow, it is pretty late.
As they walked along, the kids poked fun at Kiryu for fainting.
If it was anyone else I'd be annoyed, but I don’t mind it from them. I know they mean well. I’d be
way more bothered if Nishiki knew. Ugh… he’d never let me live it down if he found out.
As they got near the Sonozaki estate, Rika suddenly spoke up. “Mii, can I come by your house? I
wanted to borrow some manga of yours.”
Please, Mion, understand what I mean. This phrasing worked in previous fragments; surely it’ll
work here.
Mion quickly perceived Rika wanted to talk in private and replied, “Oh, yeah! You wanted volume
four right?”
“Meep, you guessed right,” Rika said with an adorable smile.
Thank you, Mion. Please have some info on this Tojo Clan.
“Satoko, I’ll catch up with you later. It’ll be a while, please make some dinner for yourself if you
get hungry,” Rika called out to Satoko as she left.
Satoko closed one eye and crossed her arms. “Hmph, don’t complain to me if you’re food is cold
when you come back. I’m hungry myself, and won’t be waiting long to make a meal for the both of
us.”
“It’s ok, Satoko. I won’t be too long, nipah!”

As Mion and Rika walked towards the estate, Kiryu was thinking to himself.
Would it take that long just to get a manga volume from Mion’s house? Are they planning to read
the whole thing together there? Eh, I guess it’s none of my business. I hope they enjoy reading…
whatever manga kids are into these days.
~~~~
Everyone waved and said goodbye to each other as they went their separate ways until it was just
Keiichi, Rena, and Kiryu.
“See ya, Teach! You honestly did well today for your first time in our club, but don’t think we’ll be
any less merciful tomorrow. You’d best come prepared!” Keiichi yelled as he walked to his house.
“Trust me, I will. Don’t look down on me, or else you’ll regret it,” Kiryu said with an assured
smirk.
In reality, these kids are tough. I swear I’ll be more guarded tomorrow, but I can’t guarantee I
won’t lose again. I’m also terrified of the prospect that today’s penalty wasn’t even the worst
they’ve done. I’d better bring my 200% from now on.
Kiryu and Rena both started walking towards their home when an idea wormed its way into Kiryu’s
head.
… Should I ask Rena about the murders of those two yakuza? We’re alone right now, and nobody
can hear our conversation. No, wait, it would be far too direct to ask that. I should lead into it
somehow… perhaps I should ask about the deaths related to that curse?
I know Jirou warned me not to talk about this, but I need to get information. I joined the club just
so I could have opportunities like this. I think at this point I’ve gained enough of Rena’s trust. As
long as I’m casual about it, things shouldn’t go awry.
“Hey, Rena? Do you mind if I ask you something a bit personal before we head home?”
Rena turned her head, and inquired, “Huh? What is it, I wonder? I wonder?”
“Well, I wanted to talk in private. The topic of what I’m about to ask is considered a little…
inappropriate from what I understand. I’m a newcomer to this village, and I was just curious about
it. I heard there was a whole conflict about a dam being planned to be built here five years ago. It
sounded pretty rough for the whole village, but all of you guys united and fought against it
eventually winning. It sounds really impressive, but I heard some unpleasant stuff about it. I wasn’t
sure if it was true or not, so I wanted to ask one of you kids, and I guess you happened to be the
one. I don’t know any way of asking this without it sounding blunt, so I’d best just do it that way.
Did anyone ever get hurt or… killed during the dam conflict?”
Rena paused for a moment not sure how to respond.
… What do I tell Kiryu?
Rena and the other kids had kept information about the curse of Oyashiro from Keiichi at first, as
they felt it was an uncomfortable truth he was better off not knowing. He eventually found out

anyway, though. He was creeped out but seemed to take it well after some time. Kiryu, however,
was a different case.
He gets along so well with the other villagers and us. I don’t want to ruin any happiness he might
have here. He’s looked so joyful, especially today. I… I don’t want to ruin his happiness here. I
abhor lying, but… just this once I’d best not tell the truth. Please, Mr. Kiryu, forgive me.
Rena put on a fake smile, and replied, “Ahahaha, where did you hear such a crazy thing as that?
Nothing like that happened here, silly. It does sound like a cool idea for a mystery novel, though.
Hauuu, that would be a fun book to read.”
Kiryu narrowed his eyes.
… Why is she lying? I’m not entirely being truthful here myself, but she has nothing to hide from
me. Is it just because I’m new here, and she doesn’t want me to know the truth? I clearly know
something, even if I’m being subtle about it. Ok fine, how do I continue this conversation?
Kiryu looked away from Rena, and in a sarcastic tone says “Huh, that’s funny. I was talking to a
man named Jirou Tomitake yesterday about it, and he told me about the first murder in this series of
events called the ‘Curse of Oyashiro’. It sounded pretty gruesome.” He then turned back to Rena
and looked her in the eyes. “I know we haven’t known each other for too long, but I expect you to
not lie to me over serious stuff as your teacher.”
Rena's eyes opened wide in surprise
Kiryu already knew?! … Wait, that means he lied too.
Rena herself looked mildly annoyed now, and in a respectful but stern voice, she said, “Mr. Kiryu,
with all due respect, did you not just lie to me now? I’m not sure if that’s the best example for your
students.”
Kiryu could only keep his mouth shut with a look of realization.
Dammit, I’ve already messed this up! Ok, stay calm Kiryu. Take control of the flow of the
conversation again. I did lie, but truthfully it was only because I didn’t know how to talk about this.
“You’re right, Rena. I apologize. I just wasn’t sure how to ask about it, so I lead you on. In truth, I
know about the details of the first murder, but nothing of the others. Thank you for holding me
accountable, though.”
Rena’s expression lightened and she said, “It’s fine, Kiryu. We just don’t like talking about it here
for… obvious reasons. It’s not pleasant for newcomers, and we don’t want to scare them off. I’m
also sorry for lying.”
A scary thought then took root in Rena's mind.
Wait… if he knows about the curse, does that mean he might want to leave?! If he does that,
wouldn’t he be cursed himself by Oyashiro? I can’t say anything else about the curse; it will scare
him more. I… I have to warn him somehow, though!
Her expression then became desperate. “I swear that era of Hinamizawa is over, Mr. Kiryu!
Nobody is going to die this year! Please don’t be afraid of Hinamizawa. I love this place so much.

The people here are so wonderful. I’ve had so many happy memories here, and you’ve become a
part of them too. Please don’t go anywhere…” Rena’s voice began to trail off as she looked down
at the ground.
Great job, Rena. Your little outburst there probably just scared him even more.
Kiryu just stood there silently.
I… don’t think I’ve ever seen this side of Rena before. ... Wait, don't just stand there, you idiot!
Comfort her!
Kiryu held up his hands, attempting to dispel Rena’s fear. “Woah! Rena! When did I say I was
going anywhere? I promise I’m not going anywhere.”
Rena looked up holding back tears. “Do… do you really mean that Mr. Kiryu?”
“Of course, Rena. I should’ve clarified this from the beginning. I’m just a big fan of crime dramas
and mysteries. This sort of stuff naturally interests me, but I wasn’t sure about how to get more
information. I figured now would be a good time, but it seems I’ve unintentionally caused you
stress. I swear, I’m not going anywhere.”
Rena began to cheer up, comforted by Kiryu’s words. “Hauu, sorry for freaking out on you a bit
there. I was just concerned, and let my emotions get the better of me.”
Ok, see Rena. He enjoys living here. He’s not going to get cursed. He won’t become a potential
victim this year. He’s… going to be ok. Calm down.
Kiryu gave a warm smile. “It’s fine, Rena. I appreciate your concern. I’m not scared of anything.”
Rena closed her eyes half out of relief, half from joy. “Hau! I’m so glad.”
“I mean, what is there to fear anyways? The elders believe in it, but between you and me, I think
we both know that the curse is a bunch of nonsense. There are no such things as curses.”
Kiryu went to give Rena a comforting head pat, but she was frozen still.
He… doesn’t believe in the curse? He doesn’t believe in curses at all? If he doesn’t believe, will he
be cursed this year? Can he still possibly die from the curse? Oyashiro can forgive people, but he
still punishes unbelievers. Will he become just like… Satoshi? No… I can’t let that happen. I can’t,
no no no NO! NO! NOO!!
Rena grasped Kiryu’s hand before it could reach her head.
“...Rena?” Kiryu was perplexed by Rena’s sudden change in manner.
“The curse is real, Kiryu.”
“...Huh?”
Rena then regained eye contact with Kiryu wearing a resolute expression.

“Finally, there’s Rika and Satoko. I’m glad you saved those two for last because they’re important.”
“They are?”
“Yes, they’re both orphans. Rika’s father was the main priest and head of the Furude family. He one
day died of an unknown disease, most likely the cause was a heart attack. His wife also disappeared

shortly afterward, but it’s believed she committed suicide and drowned herself in Onigafuchi
Swamp to ‘appease Oyashiro’.”
“As for Satoko, her parents were on vacation and fell off the side of a viewing platform mostly
likely due to leaning on an old rail that broke. It was considered a tragic accident. The body of the
father was found, but the mother was nowhere to be seen. It had just disappeared. And you seem to
be aware of what happened with the uncle and aunt a few years later.”
“Y-yes… I do.”
… Something is off here.
“That’s horrific and all, but how is it related to your investigation?”
“Oh, I figured it was obvious. These all happened on Watanagashi.”
Kiryu utterly froze. No amount of preparation made him ready for that realization.
… Holy fuck. Do you mean these three pairs of deaths are the ones that happened on
Watanagashi?! And they all three relate to Satoko and Rika?!
… No, the possibility was there. It always was there. I just didn’t want it to be true. Even after Shion
told me Satoshi disappeared on Shion’s birthday, in the back of my head I knew that was only a few
days after Watanagashi, but I didn’t want that to be related so badly.
“Kiryu, have you noticed a pattern regarding all these deaths?”
Kiryu was brought back to reality. “Er, maybe?”
“One person dies on Watanagashi, and one other disappears. They might not disappear on the same
night as Watanagashi, but it’s very soon afterward.”
Kiryu’s mind went blank.
… There’s no way. Really?!
“The dam construction manager died, and one of the six perpetrators disappeared in the first year.
Mr. Hojo died, and Mrs. Hojo disappeared in the second year. Mr. Furude died in the third year,
and Ms. Furude disappeared. Finally, the Hojo aunt died and Satoshi disappeared last year. That
brings us now to this year’s Watanagashi two days from now, and two more potentially unfortunate
victims. Freaky stuff, isn’t it? Nfufu… “
“... Freaky is an understatement.”
“They’re more connected than just that. It relates to the ‘Curse of Oyashiro’.”
“Yeah, what the hell was up with Ms. Furude?”
“It all goes back to the Dam War. Y’see there were some residents that actually approved of the
dam being built. Mr. Hojo was the leader of that group. That led to much tension between his
family and the rest of Hinamizawa, especially the Sonozakis.”
Yeah, no kidding. The last thing you want to do is piss off the yakuza.

“Even after the dam war, the Hojos were essentially exiled and considered outcasts by everyone.
Mostly because of Oryou Sonozaki’s influence. The parents’ deaths and the eventual deaths of the
aunt and uncle were considered to be Oyashiro ‘punishing’ them for going against his will. Satoko
Hojo is the last one left in Hinamizawa, but to this day she is considered an outcast by the
residents.”
“What?! She has nothing to do with that dam war!” Kiryu unintentionally raised his voice causing
some other people in the café to look his way. Once Kiryu realized he was making a scene, he
slumped down in the chair and cleared his throat.
“Sorry, didn’t mean to raise my voice there.”
“Nfufu, it’s fine. You’d be correct, it’s nonsensical. However, that village is deeply rooted in
tradition. Whatever Oryou says goes is what goes.”
… I’ll be damned, he’s telling the truth. I never really thought about it, but whenever I’d walk home
with the kids I never did see the others smiling at Satoko. They’d smile and wave at the other kids,
but I’m sure I saw one or two grimace when their eyes reached Satoko.
Kiryu wanted to be mad but remembered his goal. He took a deep breath and asked, “Ok, what
about Rika’s parents?”
“Mr. Furude was rather passive about the whole dam war incident, despite being the main priest.
Compared to the fiery determination of most everyone else, you can imagine they received
somewhat similar treatment to the Hojos. The Furudes also empathized with the Hojos, which was
more than enough to get a target on your back then. Some say the priest’s death was also
Oyashiro’s punishment.”
“... Just sounds like more batshit insanity to me.”
“Nfufu, I’d agree. I’d like to say one final thing. Do you have any guesses as to who actually might
be behind these cases?”
Kiryu recalled his conversation with Shion about Satoshi.
“Based on a conversation I had with someone I have reason to believe that Satoshi might have been
responsible for killing his aunt. I know the official statement is that some drug addict did it, but just
as a gut feeling I don't believe that."
“I’d agree. An absolutely tragic case if so, but it is the most likely case. It’s just a shame that seems
to be a common thread with both Hojo cases.”
“... Er, what?”
“Ah, I guess you wouldn’t know this. Most people wouldn’t. Now don’t freak out when I say this,
but … “
“... But what? You told me Satoko's parents fell off some cliff face because of an accidentally
broken safety rail, right? Where are you going with this?”
“... What if I told you Satoko possibly pushed them off?”

Kiryu didn’t move a muscle. A whirlwind of emotions swept through his mind. He said nothing,
prompting Ooishi to continue.
“Ms. Hojo cycled through multiple fathers for her two children. A cycle of marriage and divorce
that led to a rather unstable childhood for them both. Satoshi was at a mature enough age he could
handle it decently, but Satoko took it badly. She never had a good relationship with any of her
fathers, and they all eventually got tired of her and treated her badly. In fact, it wasn’t till she called
child protective services and faked abuse, that her final father realized he needed to step up and do
better. He cleared things up, but it left a lasting impression on him.”
“He did act like a better father after that as far as I know, but that sort of pain doesn’t leave a young
girl. Consider that the dam war stuff happened a few years later, and the resulting stress and
discrimination she faced the year afterward… “
“Ok, hold up. How does this lead to your claim?”
“I was about to say Kiryu. She was in the car with them on vacation, but her brother stayed home.
Nobody else was around, and no witnesses were there to give testimony. She was apparently
sleeping in the car, since she was feeling tired and didn’t want to join her parents. A park employee
was the one who awoke her to say there was an accident.”
“... Ok, makes sense so far. What gives?”
Ooishi leaned in and wore an extremely serious expression. “The first thing the employee said to
Satoko was asking where her parents were. She said that her parents fell off a cliff. How was she
able to know that despite seemingly being asleep?”
A harsh, horrific fear far worse than anything Kiryu had ever felt sprang to life at that moment. The
realization of the possibility made him feel hollow.
Ooishi continued in a solemn tone. “She also couldn’t see the guardrail from where the car was
parked. At most, she could maybe have made it out being broken, but why would her first thought
upon seeing that is that her parents fell off when they could have been anywhere?”
A migraine began to form in Kiryu’s head, and he half covered his eyes holding his head.
“Just… fucking stop, please. No more. I get the picture.”
“Mmm, I apologize. That one seemed to really rattle you. Would now be a bad time to ask a
favor?”
“... Just fucking ask it. I know you will regardless of what I say.”
“Nfufu, glad we don’t have to beat around the bush then. In exchange for telling you about
everything today, could I ask you to maybe ask at least one of the kids about this stuff?”
Kiryu took a clearly annoyed deep breath. “What would I even ask? You got one of the kids in
mind?”
“Hmm, perhaps Mion Sonozaki? You’re close to her, but she hates my guts. I couldn’t ask her
anything even if I wanted to, nfufu. To expand on one extra thing, I believe the Sonozakis have ties

to the first and third sets of deaths. While the Hojos might not be their fault, they’re still indirectly
to blame somewhat for them.”
“Anyways, I have to go. My lunch hour won’t last much longer, and I’d rather not be late for work.
Have a good day Kiryu, and be careful out there. Certainly wouldn’t want you to be one of those
poor souls that die this Watanagashi.”
Ooishi gave a wink to a Kiryu still holding his head. Kiryu didn’t say a word, and his eyes just
followed Ooishi as he walked out of the café. After Ooishi left, Kiryu still sat there not even
wanting to move. A couple of minutes passed, and he finally shifted his position and leaned back.
… It was foolish of me to think I’ve seen the worst the yakuza had to offer. I won’t say anything
about Mion or Shion, because I know they’re good people. The rest are fucking scum, though. To do
that to Satoko, how can I forgive them? Even if I don’t have proof yet, I’m starting to believe they’re
responsible for those deaths myself.
If nothing else, I’m going to make a bold move on Watanagashi night. I’m not going to let these
bastards get away with this for the fifth year in a row.

Around the same timeframe Ooishi had been talking to Kiryu that Friday, all the club members
(minus Rika) were meanwhile hanging out and enjoying their day off from school. Rika had left
early in the morning and told Satoko she was going to the library to research some things in
preparation for her role as the shrine maiden in the Watanagashi festival. In reality, she didn’t want
to waste another day just sitting around waiting for Kiryu to do something. She figured she could at
least do some research and learn more about the Tojo and yakuza in general. She didn’t know if
she’d find anything, but she had to try. Hanyuu was keeping an eye on Kiryu like usual.
Otherwise, the club members were happily talking to themselves. Suddenly, the topic of Kiryu
came up.
“... Did any of you guys happen to see Kiryu in Hinamizawa this morning?” Mion asked.
The other three shook their heads no.
“You did tell him about Ooishi last night, right Mion?” Keiichi inquired.
“Yeah, I did. He seemed a little pale last night. I hope Ooishi didn’t rattle him too much. Kiryu
might be staying in bed to rest, or at least I hope that’s what he’s doing. I’ve always hated that
bastard Ooishi, putting his nose where it doesn’t belong. I was afraid he’d pick on you Kei, but it
seems Kiryu was chosen instead.”
Keiichi gulped at the idea. “I’ve never met him before, but he doesn’t sound like someone you want
to get involved with. Have any of you guys had to deal with him before?”
“Eugh, too many times frankly,” Mion said frowning. “It’s why I should’ve given Kiryu a heads-up
sooner. It’s my own fault for not considering that Ooishi might gun it for him.”
“Hau, I’ve interacted with him a little. I wouldn’t necessarily say he’s a bad man, but he’s not one
I’d want to have as an enemy or become involved with either,” Rena stated.
Keiichi sat back in his chair pondering his friends’ testimonies. “Phew, it seems I dodged a bullet
then.” He glanced at Satoko, who had been quiet this whole time. He noticed she wore a troubled
look, and she seemed to be remembering something unpleasant.
He then recalled what his friends had told him about Satoko’s past, and realized his error. “I
apologize, Satoko. I shouldn’t have asked you that.”
Satoko was brought back to reality. Mion and Rena had also realized their mistake and were about
to apologize too when Satoko interrupted them. “Oh, you don’t have to apologize Keiichi. I’m fine,
there’s nothing wrong with me. Go ahead, carry on talking.”
The other three knew Satoko wasn’t being honest but went along with it to appease her. They
switched topics and returned to talking about the usual.

Truthfully, Satoko recalled some painful memories when Keiichi brought up the question. Of how
she was interrogated after her parents’ deaths, as well as after her aunt’s death and her uncle and
brother running away. She had been stuck at the police station with Ooishi or other police more
than any other kid in Hinamizawa, other than perhaps Mion.
She normally wouldn’t have thought about such things, even if the topic of Ooishi had been
brought up on another day. She was self-aware enough to realize she didn’t normally remember
those times due to how much she hated them. Regardless, that didn’t stop the harsh thoughts from
penetrating her mind.
Incidentally, Satoko usually gave herself a shot in the morning to deal with her “syndrome”.
Sometimes she would forget, and Rika would have to remind her. Satoko would fuss over it also
sometimes, but she realized it was important for her health. However, if she had forgotten to take
the shot and Rika wasn’t around in the morning to remind her …

Kiryu had arrived back in Hinamizawa. Not a cloud could be seen in the sky and the sun radiated
light over the entire town. A calm wind made the grass flow back and forth like waves at the beach.
Even the cicadas weren’t as loud as usual and were more of a relaxing noise in the background.
It was a lovely day anyone would enjoy, except for Kiryu at that moment. He felt like a zombie
sluggishly walking through the rural walkway. He was used to being warmer than usual due to
always wearing a suit, but he felt unnaturally sweaty all over. Kiryu was a man both incredibly
strong physically and mentally. However, he was nonetheless human and was starting to feel his
own mortality.
One resident said hello to him like usual, but all he could manage was a side-eye glance and barely
raising his hand. The neighbor brushed it off as Kiryu feeling sick, which he appreciated not
wanting to hold a conversation with anyone.
I have to get home and rest a little. Maybe I can do something more this evening, but I won’t be
able to keep up at this rate.
… Was this village always so peaceful? I can’t help but feel wary after hearing everything from
Ooishi. I once enjoyed the calm this village offered, but now it just adds to my anxiety. It’s too calm
here, as if you dared to shake up the order of this place you’d get swallowed up by the Earth itself.
Of course, I also acknowledge I’m dead tired, and probably full of shit. Not a bad idea to be wary,
but I’d best not slip down that slippery slope. I just…
Kiryu remembered how paralyzed he felt hearing Ooishi’s theory about Satoko being a murderer.
… I want to call it BS, but he has no reason to mess with me regarding that stuff. He’s a sly old
man, but I can tell he takes pride in his work. I just refuse to believe something like that could be
true.
If she did do it, it must’ve been some sort of accident. Maybe she has some mental illness like Rena
or some other problem. Maybe something I would have no idea of. I refuse to believe she would
intentionally kill her parents, I’m going to even refuse to believe she did it accidentally. Because if I
don’t… that would be too sad.

*pat* *pat* *pat*
Kiryu stopped as if one more step would have him fall off a cliff. Every muscle on his body tensed
up. As tired and worn out as Kiryu was, he still had his honed sense of danger, despite being out of
the yakuza for so long. Most would stay frozen afraid to look back, but Kiryu whirled his head
around to see the source of the noise behind him.
Nothing was there. Just the empty walkway he had traveled through many times at this point.
Kiryu’s eyes searched for any signs of life, but a grand sum of zero was shown to him.
Kiryu slowly turned back and continued walking.
Fucking lovely, I’m now hearing things that aren’t there, too. Can beat the toughest yakuza out
there, but can’t beat my own mind. Nobody is following you, just relax and head home.
*pat* *pat* *pat*
Every fiber of his being warned Kiryu of something heinous being there, but he forced himself to
ignore it. Whatever it was, he was too tired of dealing with these incidents to want to bother with it.
He walked for another two minutes, before finally not being able to take it anymore, and whirled
around at lightning speed.
“If there’s someone following me, you’d best show yourself you bas-!!”
Kiryu cut himself off upon recognizing a familiar face. This time there was someone there. Not
even two meters away, it was someone he knew and cared about deeply. Satoko Hojo stood there
mouth agape at Kiryu’s threatening yell.
Despite everything, Satoko was both the first and last person Kiryu wanted to see. He didn’t know
if he could keep his composure around her after everything he’d learned recently, but also the sight
of her filled him with warmth and peace.
Kiryu awkwardly coughed and attempted his best to act normal. “I’m sorry about that, Satoko. I
didn’t realize it was you. I thought you were… someone else. ”
Satoko recovered from her shock and crossed her arms. “-yYou gave me a scare there, Kiryu. It was
rather rude of you to greet me that way. Is that how a teacher should greet his students?”
Kiryu nervously laughed. “Ahaha, sorry about that. I’ve just felt a little… stressed today. Anyways,
what are you out here for? Were you… following me?”
Dark thoughts crept into Kiryu’s mind, but he tried his best to ignore them. The Satoko before him
was the cute angel he wanted to teach and protect, not some demon under the persona of a little
girl.
Satoko looked mildly annoyed. “I was heading out to get some groceries. I happened to spot you
and was about to say hello to you, before… that happened.”
Kiryu felt an arrow pierce his heart.
Damn it all! I don’t how much longer I’ll be here, but I don’t want to hurt any of these kids’ feelings
before leaving. Especially Satoko, so why did I have to freak out like that? Clearly, those footsteps
were just... well, I don't know what they were but it was obviously nothing.

“I’m so sorry, Satoko. Even if I’m feeling a little… on edge, that was incredibly inappropriate of
me. Please forgive your teacher for his harsh words.”
Kiryu slightly bowed his head. Satoko didn’t expect him to do that, but quickly covered her
reaction up by pretending to still be judging him slightly.
“W-well, as long as you know what you did wrong that’s all that matters. I wasn’t planning to hold
it against you, to begin with.”
Kiryu felt his mind calm down a bit. It wasn’t much, but he cherished being able to have a normal
conversation with one of the kids. It may not last long, but something was better than nothing.
“What’s Rika up to? Usually, you two are inseparable.”
Satoko uncrossed her arms and finally donned her usual adorable smile. “Oh, she just went to the
library in Okinomiya. She said she wanted to brush up on some history to better execute her role as
this year’s Watanagashi’s shrine maiden.”
Kiryu felt a shiver run down his spine at the mention of Watanagashi, but he made himself stay
calm.
“It is only two days away. She’s always such a mature and dedicated girl. It must be rough to have
that much responsibility at her age, but she takes it in stride.”
Satoko closed one eye and gave a judging glare. “Hmph, perhaps a little too much. I worry about
her sometimes, but I suppose she can take it.”
Kiryu felt uneasy and rapidly wanted to change the topic. “By the way, I believe your birthday is
coming up. Is there anything you’d like for it?”
Satoko’s eyes widened at Kiryu remembering her birthday. She looked at the ground pondering the
request when a mischievous smile crossed her face. “I’d love for you to help me set up a trap for
the rest of the club members. I’m a genius, but even my traps seem to have met their match.”
She glared at Kiryu with honest respect, and Kiryu smirked back acknowledging their unorthodox,
but friendly rivalry. Satoko continued, “However, the two of us together would be unstoppable. In
fact, maybe we could come up with a trap that entangles every student!”
Kiryu chuckled to himself. “Haha, let’s stay in reason. I’d rather not get fired after all. I’m sure I
could help create something, if it’s just the other club members, though.”
Satoko’s smile beamed as brightly as the sun overhead. “That’d be wonderful! I’d love to become
partners in crime with you, Kiryu. The club members will never see it coming.”
Kiryu greatly enjoyed their conversation, but his exhaustion never did fully leave him. He felt it
lurking around his legs pleading at them to rest.
“It was nice talking to you, Satoko. I’m going to head home now. Make sure to not be out too late
getting groceries.”
As Kiryu began to walk away, he heard Satoko whisper something. A statement that would change
everything.

“I really wish I could see Nii-Nii again.”
Satoko herself, later on, wondered why she said such a thing then. At the least, she didn’t mean to
say it aloud, much less for Kiryu to hear it.
Kiryu himself wanted to ignore her saying that. He wanted to pretend that nothing was happening,
but he had to face it. He had already stopped cold in his tracks. He also heard Satoko gasping in
surprise that Kiryu heard her. His mind went blank. He wanted to run like hell, not have anything to
do with that moment. He fought against it as hard as he could and took a deep breath quietly.
“Satoko, … I’ve learned some things recently. I… hope you get to see your brother again one day,
and I’m so sorry about your parents.”
It was all Kiryu could muster to say. If he was in a better state physically and mentally, he’d face
the girl. He might even have come up to her, hugged her, and whispered those words of comfort
into her ears. He couldn’t even look her in the eye in reality. Foreboding emotions and feelings
swirled around him as if he was stuck in a tornado of fear and uncertainty. He already regretted
saying something, but he was afraid he’d regret it more if he didn’t say anything.
After a minute of holding his silence, he forced himself to take a few steps.
Satoko was still in shock that Kiryu had said that. She felt something unnatural had changed in the
atmosphere.
How does… he know about my parents? Was it because of what Mion said…
Satoko wasn’t sure if she should ask this or not but felt she needed some closure. She started to feel
anxious and thought it would be best to ask for both their sakes. “Did Ooishi tell you that?”
Kiryu stopped mid-step. His foot not so much returned as wobbled to the ground.
*pat* *pat* *pat*
There were those ominous footsteps once again. Kiryu didn’t even think a single thought. He
reacted on instinct and turned around to face Satoko. And yet she hadn’t moved from her spot. She
only wore a face of concern and now caution at Kiryu’s sudden turnaround, but her feet remained
where they had been a few minutes ago.
Kiryu felt more panicked from this. Nothing made sense, and he felt like a caged animal backed
against a corner. He dropped all pretenses, and his face turned into a scowl. With a blunt voice, he
asked Satoko a question. “So? Does it matter how I found out the information?”
Satoko felt on edge. She had never seen Kiryu like this before and felt something was deeply
wrong. His face looked fearsome like he was a hunter and her the prey. “W-well, didn’t Mion warn
you not to talk to him?”
Kiryu felt surprised at himself about how straightforward he was being. He didn’t mean to direct it
at Satoko, but he couldn’t keep pretending that nothing was wrong. In the deepest reaches of his
head, something was also worming its way into his brain. Something he truly didn’t want to have,
but one can’t pretend forever.

It was doubt. It was barely noticeable, and maybe even Kiryu didn’t consciously notice it. It was
still there, though. The slightest bit of doubt about Satoko and her true character. He felt something
had been considerably off ever since she approached him.
“Satoko, it’s nothing to be concerned about. I had some business with him, that’s it. Go get your
groceries.” Kiryu said in a more serious voice.
To Satoko, it sounded more like a threat. Kiryu sought to leave this place as soon as possible, but
Satoko called after him before he could even move. “Ooishi isn’t a good person! He… yelled at and
interrogated me so much. He’s a mean man that… back when… ow, ow.”
Satoko held her head. The only thing that resulted from her trying to remember the fuzzy details of
that “incident” was a headache. Horrific visions flashed through her mind, and she couldn’t shut
them out. She was now starting to remember more than she did earlier, and she didn’t like it.
W-Why am I thinking about this right now? What is… going on? Is Kiryu doing this? No, he’s just
standing there. So why do I feel suddenly… so scared? Why does he remind me of Nii-Nii before…
he disappeared?
“Y-you weren’t like this till you met him, Kiryu. Something changed… what did you two talk
about?”
Every second this went on, Kiryu’s heart beat faster.
Why does she want to know so badly? Why the fuck does it matter?! Can’t two adults just have a
conversation, and it not mean anything?
… No, who am I kidding? This was possible. If someone saw me yesterday talking to Ooishi, who’s
to say someone else didn’t see me today? Even if no one did, Satoko can be a sharp kid. My
absence from Hinamizawa today along with me suddenly knowing key information about the
“curse” here? Put 2 + 2 together, and no shit I’m suspicious to her. I need to defuse this situation,
perhaps I should just be honest…
A fleeting moment of rationality helped Kiryu to regain a semblance of composure, and while he
still had it he told Satoko the truth. He locked eyes with her and dared not break eye contact. “Yes, I
talked to Ooishi today. He… told me all about your past. I’m sorry for doing so without your
permission, but I promise I have my reasons. I still see you as-”
Satoko’s body felt limp. The rest of Kiryu’s words didn’t reach her ears. Like a once dormant
volcano erupting, her mind spewed out all sorts of morbid thoughts.
What do you mean the truth?! What did Ooishi tell him?! Does he think I… what does… Is he
looking at me like that because he thinks I did something?
Satoko’s mind went in circles. She couldn’t coherently finish a thought. At last, the only thing that
came to mind was what she said during her interrogation.
“I-I don’t know what happened!!” Satoko cried out into the otherwise serene scenery. Kiryu’s
mouth was still open. Not another word dared seep through after her outburst. “I-it was an
accident!”

Kiryu began to shake all over. He didn’t know when, but the cicadas had become much, much
louder than before. The noise felt deafening to his ear, and the only thing that overrode that sound
was Satoko’s cries.
“S-Satoko, what do you mean?”
“I… I… I didn’t do anything. They died because of an accident. It.. wasn’t my fault. Why are you
acting like I did it?”
Kiryu started to shake even harder. He felt something was about to break. All he could do was
pathetically attempt to comfort Satoko with the remaining courage he had left. “S-Satoko that’s
not,,. I mean… “
Satoko lowered herself to the ground and put her hands on her face. Tears started to leak down her
face. It wasn’t the usual alligator tears Satoko normally had, or the immature ones she had when
she didn’t get her way. Her mind felt warped and confused, and she could only cry out in pain not
being able to understand two conflicting realities running through her mind.”
“I… I was asleep! I didn’t do anything! I *sob* didn’t do anything to them, I couldn’t have I… I…
“
Satokos’ incomprehensible wailing continued, but through it, Kiryu faced the harshest truth. He
stopped shaking. He stopped doing anything, even breathing. He finally knew the truth. One of
many truths, but a devastating one regardless.
The girl in front of him wasn’t a pure angel. Rather, she was a fallen angel. A poor child that
already had blood on her hands at such a young age.
Kiryu had wanted answers. He wanted to get to the bottom of at least some of these mysteries here.
At that moment, though, he regretted it more than ever. Satoko had confirmed his worst fears, and
yet before him, he didn’t just see an object of pity.
He also saw a being that caused him fear.
Fear that everything he had ever known was flipped upside down. Nothing was logical, nothing
was comprehensible, it was all the worst, most horrific things. The girl before him held deep sins.
Perhaps not intentional, perhaps because of a tragedy. They were there nonetheless.
And yet, his genuine feelings of caring for Satoko did remain. Even after everything, they wouldn’t
vanish entirely. He had his doubts and fears about Satoko. He wasn’t sure what he could even do to
comfort her now, but he couldn’t just stand there.
… Hey, me? Why aren’t you comforting her? Why are you letting the same thing with Rena happen
again? Do something, anything.
Kiryu for the first time took a step toward Satoko. It took everything in him to do so, but he
claimed the willpower necessary and followed through. He threw everything he had into the next
thing he could say. It wasn’t a graceful quote, but it was all he had. “Satoko, I don’t blame you for
anything. You’re a good person, you’re-”
The words escaped him as Satoko looked back at him with just as much fear as he had. He felt
confused and horrified that he had maybe said the wrong thing. It was then he finally realized

where he had gone wrong.
He had never considered what he must’ve looked like to her. Perhaps in all his own fear and doubt,
he had looked at Satoko with disgust. He was too focused on everything else to have noticed it
then, but he now recalled the face he wore. A judgemental scowl, one that resulted from
understandable fatigue. However, it was also one that immediately brought back to Satoko’s mind
memories of Ooishi interrogating her. The same judgemental, scary face that imprinted itself into
Satoko’s mind.
Satoko wasn’t so much afraid of Kiryu, as afraid of reliving that past trauma. To Kiryu though, she
looked utterly horrified of him. That he must’ve looked like some type of monster. A yakuza whose
name put fear into everyone who heard it. One that had far more blood on his hands than Satoko
did or ever would. For the first time, he actually regretted being the Dragon of Dojima. He had
always needed to have the look and expressions of an intimidating, harsh, and tough man as a
yakuza. However, it was the worst timing for those mannerisms to return here and now.
Nothing was said. Nothing was heard. Many things could have been said and heard at that moment,
but the words didn’t reveal themselves to either one of them. So what could Kiryu choose in that
situation? It was the last ditch thing he had. Something he did much of during the Empty Lot
Incident. He ran away.
He screeched at himself in his thoughts to go back. Perhaps even a few cries to go back escaped his
lips audibly. He left Satoko there all alone. He mentally wanted to go back there more than
anything else, but his body wanted just as much to escape. It was going to shut down or suffer
critically if he didn’t escape that situation then.
Kiryu was running on instinct once again only this time being brutally self-aware of what he was
doing. He ran even faster than that day from Rena. He ran with every bit of the remaining strength
he had. Self-loathing and adrenaline coursed through his body with both being the dominant forces
controlling him.
He finally reached his house and unlocked the door. He closed, locked it, and then stood there just
like had with dealing with Rena. That would be it, though. He didn’t realize he had fallen and was
on the floor till after he collapsed. He couldn’t do anything more. He had fallen to the floor onto his
side and rolled over onto his back from the momentum. It hurt, but Kiryu couldn’t even feel the
pain.
In his last bits remaining conscious, he did something he hadn’t done for a long time. Not since the
death of his close friend, Tachibana. His eyes watered and he cried. He cried for the first time in
nearly half a decade. Perhaps if he had any energy left, he would’ve had an emotional breakdown
then. But not even that could happen with his rapidly dwindling energy. Kiryu’s eyelids couldn’t
stay open any longer, and he entered a deep state of unconsented slumber.

Rika was still at the library completely unaware of what was happening in Hinamizawa. The Tojo
wasn’t exactly an unknown organization, but more concrete details about them tended to be
secretive and scarce. The same could be said for the Sonozaki Family. Due to the many yakuza
films and crime fiction out there, however, it wasn’t impossible to become well-versed in how they
tend to function. At the least, on a somewhat exaggerated level.

Rika didn’t have the time to go through entire yakuza films or read whole books, so she focused on
any information she could find on the Tojo in particular or generalized info on the yakuza. She was
already somewhat aware of the inner workings of the Sonozakis due to talking with multiple Mions
across countless fragments. Comparing it to the limited information on the Tojo she could find,
they weren’t all that different.
As perhaps interesting as that information could be, she still wasn’t making ideal progress.
Dammit, there has to be something here! Please, just give me a little luck. I’ll take anything at this
point.
For once the dice rolled in a lucky fashion. She had been searching through old newspapers
randomly in the crime sections hoping for some info. She was about to put one from a few years
ago back in the stack, but a small column in the newspaper caught her eye.
She moved the newspaper into the sunlight beaming in from the library windows to get a clearer
view of the text. She nonchalantly read through the column, until about halfway through she froze.
Her eyes widened as she read through the rest of the text. She was both happy to have found
something but also chilled by what she had discovered.
She was about to call Hanyuu to update her on what she had found when the deity herself showed
up in front of her panicked.
“What’s wrong, Hanyuu?”
“Au, au, au! It’s an emergency, Rika! Satoko and Kiryu they’ve… they’ve collapsed!”
Rika didn’t say anything back, and her face turned white. She didn’t so much as question Hanyuu
what she meant. She recalled how when one dice was rolled to be favorable, one other could just as
easily be rolled to have undesirable outcomes. In that instant, she cast aside the newspaper she was
reading and ran out of the library. She got on her bike and pedaled down the road fiercely like a bat
out of Hell.
As the newspaper fell to the ground, the column Rika had been reading was facing up. The text
read as follows:
“It’s been about one year since the events of the ‘Tojo Clan Civil War’ as many readers have come
to refer to it. Not much has been revealed about it since then, but it shook the very foundations of
the Kamurocho underworld. Some of our readers have even written in about their own experiences
and memories of the war at that time.”
“One common thread many readers have identified was a man in his young twenties, who seemed
to be at the center of much of the action. Nobody knows his identity these days, or what’s happened
to him since. Some think he died in it, others think he was responsible for saving Kamurocho from a
terrible fate. Some have even said there was another young man with an eyepatch and long hair
that had a much bigger role in the whole affair.”
“Unfortunately our dear readers, it’s nearly impossible to put together the full truth. As a journalist
myself, I’ve seen the ‘truth’ mean many different things and interpreted in many different ways.
What I can say today is that one reader last week wrote in, and gave us a very interesting tidbit.
They’ve chosen to remain anonymous, which isn’t the worst idea when talking about the yakuza.”

“Allegedly, they saw the tattoo this young man in his twenties had. It was a vivid image of a silver
dragon sprawling along his back. He recounted how it was such a remarkable scene as the young
man fought alongside another supposed yakuza with a koi tattoo, that he could never forget it.”
“He also alleges that this man is a legend in the Tojo. While not active anymore, many titles have
been foisted upon this mysterious man. Perhaps the most common being the title of ‘Dragon of
Dojima’.”

Chapter End Notes

Why does he want to know? I can get why he asks, but… still, something feels not right.

… Is that Rika?

Kiryu was hiding in the woods not too far from his house and was spying on Rika.
What the hell is she doing? She’s just standing there… and why does it look like she’s talking to

Shit! How the hell does she know where I am?

I’m almost there to the bridge. I don’t know why the hell she’s chasing me, but something bad is

How the fuck?! There’s… there’s no way a little girl like her should have even known where I was

Rika… I’m so sorry. I hope I didn’t injure you badly. Maybe you were telling the truth, but I can’t

Other than that, if I do have this “syndrome”, can I deal with it for now? I’ll... probably be fine if I
can just get to a hotel and rest. Please forgive me. I promise to all of you kids, once I’ve completed
my objective I’ll come back and apologize to every single one of you with all my heart. Just… hang
in there till then, please.

Chapter 14: Dragon Slaying Arc Chapter 13: Determination and
Despondence
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It was nearly 11:00 p.m. Kiryu had walked a long time before finally reaching a bus stop. A mix of
caution and paranoia forced him to stay wary of his surroundings. It took some time, but a bus
finally came.
After traveling on it to Okinomiya, he perused a local drug store and got some over-the-counter
mood stabilizers. Kiryu wasn’t a medicine man, but he had heard once they were useful for dealing
with hallucinations. After that, he scouted a hotel and booked a room.
Utterly exhausted, he crashed onto the bed. The room’s cleanliness was of questionable quality, and
Kiryu swore he saw a smidgen of dried blood in the corner. It was the type of hotel room a gangster
would use to lay low, which was exactly why Kiryu picked it.
He could go to the finest hotels in Japan anytime with his money. Now, he needed a temporary
abode to rest and sort things out. Laying on his back and staring at the musty ceiling above him, he
focused on his next course of action.
I need to lay low. I can’t go back to Hinamizawa, till… maybe Sunday evening. Forget keeping up
any relationships there. I should assume my cover is blown, and that there are people actively
trying to hunt me down.
… I just don’t get it, though. Was that really Rika? That girl looked so much like her, but she acted
and even sounded differently from the adorable girl I know. … There’s no way she was an assassin,
but there was absolutely something off about her. I know she said she was holding a shot, but that
was a knife. There’s no way it wasn’t. She even lunged for me and tried to stab me with it. I just…
don’t get it.
These thoughts had been haunting him for the last few hours. Despite knowing better not to dwell
on them, the same questions kept coming up in his head. He finally shook his head and picked up
the phone.
This is getting me nowhere. Let’s just update Nishiki, and go to sleep.
The phone rang and rang. Kiryu sighed impatiently.
You’d better not be out with some ladies at a cabaret club, you prick. Don’t let me down here.
After a few rings, a familiar voice came through. “Hello?”
Kiryu sighed in relief. “Nishiki, it’s Kiryu.”
“Kiryu? … Are you ok, bro? You never call me this late, and this isn’t the number you gave me.”
“I’ll be straight with you. I’m in a hotel in Okinomiya. I literally ran away from Hinamizawa not
too long ago.”

Nishiki had been relaxing in an office when he bolted right up at hearing that. “What the hell

… I can’t just say I was attacked by a pre-teen girl. He’ll think I’ve really lost it.

They’re extremely secretive.”
Kiryu recalled how he had once actually heard about them. All he knew is that they were some type

Kiryu was genuinely surprised. I know they’re high up in the underworld, but I’ve only ever heard

The question hit Kiryu like a sack of bricks. He was too tired to have fully realized that no mission

“... Don’t tell me you actually want to go back to that hellhole? You almost got killed, and that’s not

“R-right, I’ll be careful. I’ll come back as soon as I can, Nishiki. Just give me a few days. I’ll stay

“Alright, quit being a titty-baby. I can take care of myself, as I’ve proven. This is nothing compared

Kiryu hung up the phone and laid back in his bed. The decayed ceiling gladly welcomed his
attention, but Kiryu wasn’t focused on it. He was still reconciling with the idea that everything he

… Is that it? Do I just clear things up with Ooishi, and head home now? Maybe call Shion as well,

The kids… dammit, this was the last way I wanted to leave them. I still have so many questions I’ll

life in Hinamizawa is over. There’s no going back now. All I can do is hope I have a chance to send

… But hey, maybe that’s fine. I was never supposed to be in Hinamizawa, to begin with. It’s a town

something horribly wrong with that place.
… Just forget this ever happened. Leave it all behind, and go back to work. That’s what’s best. I’ll

Watanagashi will pass by, and I…
I…
I…
Kiryu suddenly burst from his bed sitting up. Sweat had begun to form on his brow, and he held his

He slowly stood up from his bed and took a slow walk toward the bathroom mirror. He looked at

a resolute pair of eyes stared back at him regardless.
“… No, there’s still some sick fuck out there causing all this. Mission or not, at this point, it’s

The world might not have been able to reply back, but Kiryu passionately proclaimed his promise

Friday had been a long, arduous day, but Saturday finally arrived. For once, Kiryu had gotten a
decent night’s sleep. Despite his ambitious goal, he still needed to actually create a plan. He first
reached out to Shion to update him on whether Kasai found anything. She gave him an answer he
was used to at this point. Nothing. At this point, Kiryu would’ve been more surprised if she had
actually found something. He kept their conversation brief and gave a polite goodbye. He once
again asked her to not tell anyone of their conversations though, with an air of deceit as he implied
they would be keeping in contact.
The reality was much grimmer. Kiryu was flying solo. He called Ooishi and lied saying he had
found nothing out. Ooishi was a little skeptical, but he also half-expected that to be the reality
considering his own poor luck in investigating. He accepted Kiryu’s answer, and that was that. Both
his contacts were deceived and Kiryu was only relying on himself now.
There at a table in his room, he sat, staring down at a map of Hinamizawa. He wracked his brain on
how to approach this self-appointed mission.
I need a way to be around HInamizawa without being recognized. I dare not try to infiltrate the
festival. They know me and what I look like well, so I need to keep to the back roads. I have an idea
for a “disguise”, and I think it can work as long as they don’t see my face. I’d better remain
cautious, regardless. As for where the killer will strike…

… I can rule out the general festival area. There are far too many people around. Most likely, it
wouldn’t be near any housing areas or businesses either. The back roads or general wilderness
surrounding Hinamizawa is a good place, but Ooishi and his police should have those areas
covered. The killer would also somehow have to knock their victim unconscious and then drag them
to a place to kill and bury them, which all sounds far too risky.
Kiryu took a deep breath and laid back in his chair
C’mon, think outside the box! I’m… not a killer, but I know I can get into the head of one.
Kiryu doubly focused his effort, and meticulously scanned the map. His eyes landed on the Irie
Clinic.
I… can’t rule out the idea of the Irie Clinic being related to all this, but that’s as likely as any
business in Hinamizawa. Dr. Irie cares about Satoko as much as I do, and I can tell. There’s no way
he would ever let harm come to her. Even if she is… involved in those crimes, he would still accept
her with open arms. What else is there…
Oh, there is that dump where Rena likes to go treasure hunting. That would actually be a perfect
area to dispose of a body. … However, how is the killer going to get the body over there, to begin
with? I’m sure Ooishi has accounted for the dump just in case.
He thought and thought… and thought some more. Kiryu analyzed this situation more than perhaps
anything he ever had in his life. The old Kiryu would just bust in without so much a thought. It was
only through working a proper job for years that he began to develop the habit of planning
somewhat ahead. He was still doing something crazy, but the man now had a method to his
madness.
A man can only think so much, though. He slammed his fist on the table and lit a cigarette.
Technically, the hotel had a “NO SMOKING’ rule, but it was rare any of the staff actually enforced
it. He strode around his room and looked out the window.
“Is there something major here I’m just blind to?” He asked himself quietly. “I’m positive the killer
intends to use the festival in some way, but how? Rika is supposed to perform near the shrine, but
how would-”
Kiryu froze. The gears clicked in his head, and suddenly everything came together. … A shrine
nobody is supposed to go into, the gruesome rituals done in Hinamizawa’s history, whatever is
going on with Rika… it has to be connected to that shrine!! I can’t be positive but somehow… I just
know something will happen in that shrine that night.
A plan had finally begun to form. A simple plan that perfectly fits Kiryu. Sneak into Hinamizawa
and stake out behind the shrine hidden from the eye’s view. It was far from a perfect plan, but
Kiryu could pull it off. Watanagashi was on its way, and the Dragon was now ready to face it.

Rika lay in her bed. The pain from her bruised rib was still present, but not as bad as it could be.
After her encounter with Kiryu, she painfully walked back to her house over the course of an hour.
It was a long, dreary night. Many feelings flooded Rika, but an overwhelming feeling of failure is

had taken after getting home, and the empty glass of wine she had nearby.

Irie had called earlier in the morning, and confirmed that Satoko was ok. The other club members

It was now evening in Hinamizawa. The Watanagashi festival had begun. Not only did just about
everyone in Hinamizawa come out to the festival every year, but multiple tourists would visit as
well. While tourism had declined considerably ever since the dam war, there were always those that
either didn’t know or didn’t care and came regardless. It was the highlight of the town celebrating
its long history. How could one afford to miss it?

Dozens if not hundreds of booths lined the town, taking up any space they could find. Games, food,

Multiple police officers were patrolling both the festival, the area of the town outside the festival,

Katsuya over a walkie-talkie. “Anything new on your end, Katsuya?”

could be suspicious.

“Oh, nothing. Just a nickname I’ve given him.”

the room, and finally recognized where he was. He took multiple deep breaths before becoming
something resembling “calm”.
… Was all that just a dream?
Kiryu looked at his calendar on his bedside stand and couldn’t believe his eyes. It was the week
before Watanagashi. Tuesday to be specific. Not only had Rika traveled back in time into a new
fragment, … but so had Kiryu Kazuma.
