Chapter 18: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 1: An Emotional Start
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

It had taken a few minutes, but KIryu’s heart rate was beginning to calm down. As his mind began
to grasp the situation he was in, he looked down at his chest. His undershirt stared back at him,
stained from dinner the night before. No stab wounds were present, nor was there any pain. And
yet, it felt all too real in his head. The scorching pain, the cold metal of the knife that made his
organs burn, and above all else the screeching of that girl that delivered him divine punishment.
“... What the actual fuck is going on?” He whispered to himself.
He glanced at his calendar again, and sure enough, it was still Tuesday. And Watangashi was
coming up this Sunday. The clock read 9:00 a.m. He pinched himself not once, not twice, but three
times just to make sure he was awake. He then sat still letting the reality of it all sink in.
His brain was still sluggish, but it was finally kicking in. Thoughts began to form, ones relating to
what had happened at the end of the previous loop. The realization a worst-case scenario could be
present hit him, and it was finally the thing that made him jump out of bed instantly.
THE KIDS!!!!
~~~~
Kiryu wasn’t even fully dressed. He hadn’t showered, had only thrown on a T-shirt and some
shorts, and his hair was an unkempt mess. It was quite the sight for the residents of Hinamizawa
wondering if perhaps Kiryu was uncharacteristically late.
He was late, but he didn’t care. He ran with only one goal in mind. He needed to know the kids
were ok. He still wasn’t entirely sure what was going on, but he needed to confirm their status
before anything else.
It wasn’t long before he finally reached the school. He grabbed and opened the door so hard, one
would think it was about to be ripped off its hinges. He bolted towards the classroom and finally
came to a stop.
He was about to open the door but hesitated. He feared what would be on the other side. That
perhaps this dream and maybe even his life itself would end, if he looked inside. He had to face
reality eventually though, and he came here for a reason. He took a deep breath and opened it
quickly.
…
And to his surprise, he was met with a heavy eraser to the head. He flinched and looked down at
the dust-filled weapon that had struck him. He looked up to see the classroom with everyone in it.
Everyone including Mion, Keiichi, Rena, and a laughing Satoko pointing at him. “Ohoho, I finally
got you, Kiryu!”

The other kids laughed, and Chie was surprised at Kiryu’s rough appearance. He didn’t care about
any of that, though. All he could do was let out a breath and collapse to his knees. The tension
instantly spiked, and Mion and Chie were the first to rush to him. “Kiryu, are you ok?!” Chie yelled
out.
At this point, the rest of the kids had gathered around. Kiryu looked up and saw the faces of his
precious students. Four of which he had killed with his own hands. The images of their mangled
and blood-stained corpses flooded his mind. And yet here they were alive as if nothing had ever
happened.
And yet he knew it had happened. He knew what he had done. Even if God himself existed, and
had miraculously given him another chance like he so selfishly begged in his last moments, it
hadn’t changed what he had done. Immense guilt and sorrow filled him. All he could do was look
at the ground and softly whisper, “I’m sorry.”
“What’s wrong, Kiryu? You’ve done nothing to apologize for,” Chie said to try and calm him
down.
The rest of the students chimed in with similar phrases. How could they know what had happened?
It was as if his actions never existed. Kiryu knew his crimes, and he was the only one that did. Even
if the people before him hadn’t been harmed by him, all he could do was apologize continuously as
his eyes teared up. “I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m sorry, I’m sorry…”
There was only one student that hadn’t gotten up. A young girl with blue hair in the back of the
classroom. A girl that was experiencing a whirlpool of emotions.
~~~~
Earlier that morning:
A new fragment, another Rika possessed as a vessel for the hundred-year-old witch. She awoke in
her new body, as she had numerous times before. She quickly sat up and observed her
surroundings. It was 6 a.m., and Satoko was sleeping right next to her. She was smiling and seemed
to be having a nice dream. The memory of her corpse from the last fragment was fresh in her
mind.
Only one more thing was needed to fulfill the usual process of entering a new world. “Hanyuu,
what day is it?”
A solemn goddess floated next to her. “Tuesday… “
Rika clicked her tongue in annoyance. Rika stayed silent, got up from her bed, and began to start
getting ready to cook some breakfast. “R-Rika, do you have a plan?” Hanyuu cautiously asked.
“… No, Hanyuu. Not at the moment. Can you confirm if anything major has changed?”
“Not that I can tell.”
“I suppose we’ll find out shortly. Can you tell where Kiryu is?”
Hanyuu paused for a moment and tried to search for something, anything. “I don’t sense him, but I
also don’t sense Takano around, either.”

Rika paused. “Then let’s assume this timeline is the same as the last one, at least until proven
otherwise. Presumably, Takano is in Kamurocho, Kiryu’s location is unknown, and from the
memories of this Rika, I know Kiryu is already in the club and is relatively friendly with us.
Though, if he is here according to my memories, why can’t you sense him?” She asked side-eying
Hanyuu.
She looked like a dear in headlights unable to answer. “I-I don’t know! Au, au, au!”
She squeaked in frustration, and Rika could only sigh. “We’ll see him soon enough, either way. He
should be there at school first thing as usual.”
“Should I see if he’s at his house?” Hanyuu inquired.
Rika nodded her head. “I’ll wake up Satoko, and start getting ready for school.”
Hanyuu nodded back, and she disappeared from Rika’s view. Rika returned her attention to making
breakfast, but her eyes looked near glazed over. Whatever we do, we have to get Kiryu’s help this
time.
~~~~
Now in the present time, Rika looked at the disaster of a man before her. The man she had turned
into a demon against and had robbed the life of was there again before her. The man that for all she
knew was responsible for changing the flow of time and denying her a happy ending. And yet,
before her, a miracle was also happening. Keiichi was one thing, but this man that had appeared out
of nowhere had remembered the previous timeline. And here he was begging, sobbing for
forgiveness for the sins he had committed.
Who or what are you, Kiryu?
After all the tragedy and misunderstandings and horrific ending of the last timeline, here before her
was the opportunity of a lifetime. Someone she could explain the truth to, perhaps someone who
was experiencing the same thing she had for the last century. She recalled what she said to Keiichi
when he remembered, and considered her words carefully.
Getting up from the desk, she walked towards him. The scene was just like Keiichi’s. Both realized
their follies, begging for forgiveness for sins no one could know. She was the only one that could
solve this dilemma, and thus she began acting the role she was given.
“Do you remember, KIryu?” She asked the trainwreck on his knees.
As distraught as Kiryu was, he instantly froze at the familiar voice. He looked up and there was his
executioner. He did not see the red-eyed demon as before, but rather how the girl was that night she
chased him. Her deep, amethyst eyes stared down at him with a myriad of emotions. The one that
seemed to stand out the most though, was one of pity.
“Do you remember?” She asked once again.
Kiryu was entirely absorbed by her presence, and it was only after hearing her ask twice that he
could focus enough to answer back. “Yes.”

Rika didn’t immediately respond back but rather nodded as if confirming her suspicions. She then
wore a childish smile and completely changed like flipping a switch. She reached out and patted
Kiryu on his head. “There’s nothing to worry about. It was just a bad dream. You did nothing
wrong, nipah!”
Kiryu held still. He couldn’t imagine the look on his face, most likely it was one of bewilderment
and maybe slight embarrassment. He knew instinctually she was faking her act, but his heart almost
stopped with what she said next. “Meet me behind the school at lunch,” she said in a disturbingly
calm whisper.
She had retained the faux innocent mask the whole time, and Kiryu looked at her with uncertain
eyes. He wasn’t sure if he could trust Rika, but he dared not refuse her after all that had happened.
Tension decreased, and Keiichi would break the silence. “So Teach, just had a bad nightmare?”
“Gosh, it must have been horrific to have rattled him this much. Are you ok now, Kiryu? Are you?"
Rena asked earnestly.
“... Yes, I’m ok. I apologize for my appearance and the sudden outburst. I know this must look
ridiculous to you all.”
“N-no, it’s fine. Things happen, don’t worry about it,” Chie said, trying to cheer Kiryu up.
“I’m sorry,” apologized Satoko. “There was some bad timing on that eraser.”
For the first time within the last few days, Kiryu was able to genuinely smile. Satoko being alive
and well was enough to make him happy. “I’m fine, Satoko. Didn’t hurt a bit. Seems I’ll have to get
you back now, though.”
Satoko’s face lit up. “Try your best. In the end, you’ll never get me.”
Despite the odd circumstances of that morning, the classroom was now back to its normal, happy
self. At the least, it would be that way till lunch rolled around.
~~~~
It was nearly noon. Kiryu apologized for his unbecoming looks and said he would go back home
and return shortly. After a proper shower and being accompanied by his usual red and gray combo,
he began his journey back to school. The number of questions he had now made the previous
amount look tame in comparison. He could only hope Rika could answer them all.
… I can’t even begin to understand what’s going on. I don’t even know if that Rika girl is human, or
if she’ll try to attack me again. Either way, she’s the only path forward I have now.
As he neared the school, he could hear the bell ring signaling lunch break. Students were gathering
together, trading food, and talking about their day. Rika made up an excuse that she forgot
something at home, and would be back shortly. In reality, she was waiting on Kiryu behind the
school.
A concerned Hanyuu floated next to her descendant. “Do you think it’s a good idea to be so direct
with him, Rika?”
“... What other options do we have?”

Hanyuu couldn’t find an answer, so she said nothing. After a few moments, Rika would speak up.
“Hanyuu, is it possible for other people to time travel in the Sea of Fragments?”
“Despite how long I’ve lived, the Sea of Fragments is still a mysterious place to me. I have control
over it to a degree, but I’ve never met another being there besides you…”
Her voice drifted off, and Rika waited for her to continue. “However, it’s not impossible that I’m
the only deity. There are numerous planes of reality and dimensions even I’ve not ascended to.
There could be someone or something helping Kiryu with its powers that is in a higher realm.”
Rika shuddered at the thought of this all-powerful entity making even Hanyuu’s powers seem
tame.
“However,” Hanyuu said, interrupting Rika’s thoughts. “We’ve seen how Takano’s willpower can
affect the very flow of time in each fragment. She may not be able to time travel like us and she
certainly rejects any help from deities, but her will is strong enough to effect the fragments even so.
It perhaps is the same way with Kiryu.”
Rike remained silent. At this point, she was just worried KIryu wouldn’t show up. As if on cue, the
dragon turned the corner and suddenly there the two were. Mentally prepared for whatever happens
next, but unsure of how to begin.
Kiryu had all his wits about him and was ready to enter a fighting stance if need be. Though he
wasn’t entirely sure if he could fight whatever it was that was in front of him. Perhaps she was a
little girl or something not of this world.
Rika in comparison was empty-handed, and was powerless to stop Kiryu, if he really wanted to do
something to her, he certainly could. She was betting it all on this meeting, as perhaps the only
way not just her, but maybe them both can find a way out of this.
Kiryu would be the first to speak up. “Who the hell are you, and what is going on?”
Rika let herself relax, and for once she got to be her true self in front of someone else. “My name is
Rika Furude,” she said in her natural, deep voice, unlike her age. “You know me, you… just don’t
know the true me. However, I believe we’ve found ourselves in the same spot.”
Kiryu kept silent and listened, even though her voice still threw him off. Rika would continue
saying, “It might be hard to believe, but I think you’ve seen it yourself. I’ve been stuck in a time
loop for over a century, and I think you’ve somehow gotten involved in it.”
Kiryu was utterly speechless. What could he even say in response? Rika had just said something
completely absurd, and yet it made sense. The fact he was now alive again and so were the kids,
her almost unnatural maturity for her age, the unique presence he felt from her, everything about
the mysterious girl clicked into place.
And yet that also confirmed something horrific. That nightmare actually happened, the actions he
committed, it was all real. So heart-achingly real.
The horror was blatant on Kiryu’s face. He stared at his murderer, the one he had accepted death
from. The one he felt above all else deserved to take revenge on him for what he had done, and yet
now he was alive again—caught up in a mess far beyond even his capabilities.

Rika wasn’t sure how to respond. She was able to find the right words to help Keiichi when he
remembered, but this time was different. She had completely lost herself and had become a
murderer. It wasn’t the syndrome, it was just her having finally broken. And now her victim was
right there alive again confronting her.
She was a good girl, and he was a good man. Both were lost in a maze of spacetime, both
interconnected regardless of their consent and now the only ones that could help each other. She
took a deep breath and began to speak. “I… don’t think I can find any right set of words to you.
What happened back then… I won’t make any excuses. I did something horrible to you, and… all I
can ask is please forgive me.”
The girl fell to her knees and bowed. Kiryu stared at her more confused than anything. What is
she… she’s apologizing to me?
Rika continued, “I don’t know if you can even fully understand what I’m saying or have been
through, but I need your help, Kiryu. I’ll help you however I can in return, I’ll give you anything I
can. I’ll do whatever you need me to do, just… please help me!”
She began to break down and the tears came pouring out. In reality, it had only been a handful of
hours between the end of the last world and now. She was still reeling from all of her emotions and
had been barely keeping it together internally. Now faced with no other option, she could only beg
the man in front of her despite everything.
“I’ve been killed so many times, I’ve tried for so long to escape this Hell. I just… *sob* please,
save me!”
She cried out for help and continued to weep. Kiryu looked at her with a mix of befuddlement and
confusion. She was right. He couldn’t fully grasp what the girl had gone through. However, he
didn’t need to. He could see that in front of him was a lonely girl begging for help. One that needed
him despite everything. And yet, he still found himself hesitating.
“You’d… want me to help you even after-”
“It’s not your fault!!” She yelled out not letting Kiryu finish. “You didn’t do anything wrong! It’s
that damn syndrome that controls you! You had a sickness that caused you to not be yourself, and
become violent. So… so many of my friends have fallen to it across numerous timelines. I’ve seen
them suffer and kill each other so many times that when you fell to it and did it I … I just lost it!”
Rika was in complete hysterics, but something finally clicked in Kiryu’s head. The speech Rika
was giving the night she confronted him. He remembered every word she said, and everything he
had experienced. All his fears, distrust, his hallucinations, and delusions, they all were explained.
And yet, even so, the guilt would not go away. He despised and blamed himself for succumbing to
such a disease. Even if it wasn’t entirely his fault, he still committed those horrid sins. He was still
the one that took their lives. He swore to never take a life outside of self-defense. Nishiki saved
him from that fate, and he spat in his face.
There was only one thing he could do. While he may not be able to be forgiven for those actions, he
knew he had to still atone. And the only way he could would be to help the girl in front of him.
There were still the unsolved murders of those two yakuza, the threat of war between the Tojo and
the Sonozakis, on top of those mysterious men who seemed to be related to Takano.

It was an incomprehensible amount. Way more than any one man could do, with the one exception
being Kiryu and he knew it. He promised he would protect these kids, that he would protect this
town, and that he would stop the madness of Watangashi. He couldn’t live with himself if he didn’t,
so he asked the mess of a girl in front of him a simple question.
“Will you let me help you?”
The girl stopped sobbing and looked up at Kiryu. Her tear-stained eyes gained an ever-slight
glimmer of hope.
“I’ve committed something unforgivable. I’ve killed those you love, and even if they’re alive now
their deaths still happened. I may not fully understand your situation, but I know you’re in trouble.
If you will allow me to help you, your friends, and potentially save them all and this town itself. I
promise… “
He got down on one knee and was near eye level with Rika. “I promise I’ll do everything in my
power. All I need in return from you is whatever info you may have if you’re willing to share it.”
He held out his hand. The girl couldn’t believe her eyes. After a century of Hell and torture, she had
found the most unlikely of allies. She was sure under the right conditions, her friends would be
more than willing to help her. Even then though, this man was worth an entire army. She had seen
his power, she knew of his legends, she knew he was almost superhuman. In the blink of an eye, the
dice had been rolled and had given her the most desirable outcome she could ask for as of right
now.
She grasped his hand, and he helped her up. “You’re… willing to help me even after what I did to
you?” She asked weakly.
Kiryu paused. He was surprised on some level to finally realize the girl regretted her actions. In his
eyes, he thoroughly deserved it. However, he also understood that no girl her age should ever be
driven to something like that. If easing her guilt was involved in helping her, so be it.
“Please forgive yourself. I’m alive in this world.”
“Maybe, but… I didn’t have the syndrome. I chose to kill you, and now your friends and family in
that timeline are… “
She couldn’t bear to finish. She stared at the ground, and Kiryu chose his next words carefully. “We
can’t change the past, Rika. We can only move forward.”
She looked up at him with puffy eyes. “I’ve seen people I hold dear die in my arms. I was unable to
save them, I was unable to help them. If I could redo it of course I would, but I can’t. I don’t know
how I got involved in literal time travel and of course you and everyone’s lives like this, but I’ve
been miraculously given that chance here somehow. Even if I don’t remotely deserve it, I’ve been
given a second chance to save this place. You want to protect your friends, right?”
“... Yes,” Rika answered resolutely.
“It’s the same for me. I came here because I didn’t want war to break out, and I wanted to protect
my family. If we work together, I know we can save those dear to both of us. But I need your help,
so I’ll once again ask you. Will you let me help you?”

“Yes!” She didn’t even need to think about it. Maybe it was fate she met this man, but she needed
him and he needed her.
Unexpectedly, Kiryu then knelt again and embraced the girl. “Even if I don’t understand
everything, I can get this. You’ve been through Hell itself, and I’m so sorry I could not have been
there for you earlier. If we both have suffered from being unable to save others… then I promise
we’ll break that cycle. No matter what.”
Just as soon as she had stopped, water began to form in her eyes again. She rested her head on
Kiryu’s shoulder as her tears stained his suit.
While having been entirely absent from the conversation, Hanyuu had watched the whole thing
with a neutral expression. Now she had a bittersweet smile on her face. She couldn’t speak or
interact with the man, but she was the happiest she had been in a long time. Thank you, Kiryu.
Thank you for fighting for my daughter’s happiness. I promise I’ll help you as much as I can. I
swear it.

Chapter End Notes

It's tricky to write a heavy-handed and emotional scene like this, but now was the best time I
felt considering everything leading up to this. I hope you enjoy what this future duo will get
up to in the future, since this is only the beginning.

Chapter 19: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 2: Mad Dash
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

After some time and her being embraced by Kiryu, Rika calmed down and assessed the situation.
The best way for Kiryu to help her would be for him to know everything. However, being so caught
up in her emotions, she realized she might have already made a fatal blunder. The Mountain Dogs
had eyes and ears everywhere, and she couldn’t just blabber off their secrets. As far as she knew
they didn’t tend to survey this spot behind the school, but if they had seen that scene between her
and Kiryu…
“Hanyuu, do you sense anyone around?” She asked telepathically.
Hanyuu took a moment to search around and shook her head no. Rika nodded and then whispered
to Kiryu, “There’s no one watching us right now, but there could be if we don’t leave soon. I’ll
explain everything when I can.
Kiryu’s eyes lit up, but he stayed calm. He let go, and asked, “Then where or when would be the
best way?”
“... Come to my house tonight, and pretend you’re picking up a book you lent to help me study. I
have one in the house I’ll hide a letter with everything explained in it, and you can read it when you
get home.”
Kiryu nodded, and the two promptly returned to school as the bell rang.
~~~~
School had ended, and Mion’s club was about to start. Traveling through time was a first for Kiryu,
so he was still getting used to possessing this world’s Kiryu and having similar memories, but not
precisely his. The most significant changes he could determine is that he had managed to get into
the club a little earlier this time than in the last world, and Shion was seemingly enrolled at the
school this time. However, she seemed to skip class here and there. He also hadn’t met or talked to
Ooishi yet.
All that said, he now was being faced with perhaps his greatest challenge yet. One that would take
every fiber of his being. A task so daunting, that not even he was sure he could complete it. It was,
of course, avoiding the penalty of Mion’s latest club game. Somehow. he had to avoid being tagged
by the five misfit kids before him for 30 minutes.
He sighed and looked at the eager kids. The scene resembled a pack of wolves preparing to hunt an
innocent deer. How do I get myself into these situations? When Mion suggested something like tag,
I should have assumed something was up. It’s been a long time since I last played it, but I don’t
recall “5 vs. 1” being something right at the start.
“Alright Mion, so let me get this straight. I have to evade ALL of you for 30 minutes, and I win.
But if I get tagged once, I’m out?”

“Yep!” She confirmed eagerly. “Obviously, you can’t go out of HInamizawa, and while you can use
the back roads you can’t go into any of the forest areas. Also, you can’t hide or stay in one place.”
“And you can use the forest and hide, I presume?”
Mion smirked. “Well sure, we need every advantage we can get. You’re our P.E. coach, you should
be able to run circles around us. Five kids should be nothing for you.”
Kiryu was unamused. Oh sure, the five kids in this town that could probably take on a whole army,
if they wanted to. Maybe Rika will at least take it easy on me?
He shifted his gaze to Rika. She only gave her usual smile back. Knowing who the girl really was,
her act still unnerved him somewhat. Nah, if anything she’s the wild card. She cut me off when I
was fleeing for my life. How the hell would I escape her here? That isn’t including maybe some of
Satoko’s traps and whatever the other kids are planning.
He smiled to himself. Then again, it’s not like I plan to just lose. Mion’s right, I should have no
trouble as long as I’m alert and careful.
“Do I at least get a head start?”
“Sure! We’ll give you a … how about 30-second head-start?”
“Oh, aren’t you confident? I expected a five-second one or none at all.”
“Oh no, it’s only fair to you, Kiryu. I mean, you need something for it to be remotely fair. We’re all
but guaranteed to win,” Mion said, her eyes glimmering with confidence.
“... We’ll see,” Kiryu responded, equally as confident.
“Want to do the countdown, Rika?”
“Meep, sure.”
Kiryu turned around, the school behind him. Like a track star ready to run the 100-meter dash, he
was prepared to take off at a moment’s notice.
“3, 2, 1, Gooooo!” Rika shouted.
And he was off. Kiryu wasn’t a track star, but he was still a physically fit young adult. He looked
behind for a brief second, and the kids weren’t even there anymore. A few minutes had passed, and
he was in the center of Hinamizawa. While he had gotten a few confused looks from the locals, he
ignored it because it would become apparent soon enough it was the kids and their usual
shenanigans.
He slowed down to a walk and considered his options. Ok, it’s been about four minutes. I already
know they’re going to be cheating, so I can hide if I want. … Though, that would be lame, and I’d
hear no end of it. Unfortunately, my pride is on the line here if I can’t win with their criteria.
He then spotted something that could be useful in a nearby trashcan. It was a raggedy old stuffed
animal someone had thrown away. He picked it up and put it in his pocket.

It was a good thing to as out of the corner of his eye, he could see a young girl rapidly approaching.
"Mr. Kiryu!" Rena yelled. "I'm going to get you!"
Kiryu didn’t hesitate and bolted. I should have known they activated her Kyute Mode! She's so fast!
Between businesses and local shops, he ducked and weaved. Rena, to his disbelief, was catching
up. Rena wasn't the only one though, he was sure he had seen Keiichi a few times. They’re trying to
cut me off.
Six minutes had passed and now he could even see Rika had circled around and nearly cut him off
before he dived into an alley. So that's three now, where are the other two?
Kiryu had no time to think, though. He quickly looked back only to see the gap between him and
Rena was about six feet and closing rapidly.
“Rena! Think fast!” Kiryu threw the old doll behind him, and it flew past Rena. She instantly
hyper-fixated on it and lost all focus on Kiryu. It took her five seconds before she blushed and
realized what Kiryu had done.
“That’s not fair, Kiryu!” She yelled after him, but it was too late. Kiryu was long gone. He smirked.
Sorry Rena, but I knew you’d fall for that. Now as for the other two… no three.
In focusing on Rena, he had missed that Mion had now joined the chase. Mion to the left, Rika to
the right, and Keiichi behind, he was going to get cornered soon or led into one of Satoko’s traps.
Not to mention, Rena would be back soon enough.
Kiryu glanced at his watch. Only nine minutes, huh?
He was about to leave the town area and go into the back roads around the forest. I’ll have to lose
them there.
Kiryu picked up the speed and went as fast as he could. He blitzed through the trails, the only
sound keeping him company was his breathing, frantic footsteps, and the never-changing noise of
the Higurashi. A few minutes passed, and he couldn’t see the kids anywhere.
12 minutes in, if I can just keep up this pacHe was cut off as he accidentally ran right into a homemade trip wire, and a collection of buckets
on a string swung towards him.
“What the-!”
He barely dodged it, and in his panic, he triggered another and a bucket fell on his head. “Ack!”
Disoriented and his vision obscured, he could hear Satoko yell, “I got you!”
Everything around him seemed to stop. He instantly focused his senses. He could still hear, and he
could tell the direction a small pair of footsteps were coming from.
… Now!
Just as Satoko was about to tag him, he moved out of the way and put his leg out to trip her.

“Wha-?!” Satoko never saw it coming and took a tumble onto the sidewalk. Kiryu took the
opportunity to take the bucket off his head and checked to see if Satoko was injured at all. He
didn’t even need to ask, as Satoko was already back on her feet, about ready to give chase. She was

Kiryu smiled. “Just good instincts.” And after that, he split. He was nearly halfway through the
allotted 30 minutes, but he was stuck on a one-way trail. He couldn’t enter the forest surrounding
him, and he could be cut off at any moment.
Sure enough, a minute later he saw Mion ahead of him maybe 20 feet away. She had her arms
crossed and had clearly been waiting for him. “Took you long enough, Kiryu.”
Kiryu came to a stop and observed his predator. “Can’t a guy jog in peace?”
“I’m afraid not. Do you even have time to stand around here?”
Kiryu stayed calm and observed his surroundings. There was no escape, … or at least that’s what it
looked like. “You’re right, I’d best get running. Unless you want to come get me first.”
He could hear footsteps approaching behind him, and Mion herself was getting ready to initiate the
pincer movement. “Sure, I’ll take you up on that offer.” Mion bolted towards Kiryu. “Kei, get

Kiryu didn’t have to look behind him. He started running towards Mion. 20 feet between them had
turned to ten. Mion assumed Kiryu would try to slip by her without being tagged, but she wouldn’t
let that happen. However, he did something completely unexpected. He jumped, grabbed onto a
sturdy branch, and used the movement to swing over Mion’s head.
She was so amazed, she didn’t see Keiichi about to crash into her. “Mion! Watch ou-” It was too
late. The two collided and fell backward.
“Mion, what were you doing?!” Keiichi yelled at her.
“I didn’t expect him to swing over me like Tarzan!” Mion responded. “Where is he now?” She
looked up, and Kiryu was long gone. She clicked her tongue in annoyance. “Go on ahead, Kei. I
have a plan. It’s a big risk, but I can see it working.”
Keiichi nodded and started running.
18 minutes had passed. Kiryu was out of the forest and was running through Hinamizawa once
again. Though, he was now back to square one. Rena and Rika had been waiting in town for him,
and Satoko had taken a shortcut through the forest to close the distance. Okay, not much time left,
but what can I do to stall?
He had more than enough stamina to keep going, but he feared getting caught in a dead-end.
Suddenly, an idea occurred to him. There is that one alleyway with a dumpster…
After a few close calls and switching directions suddenly at least four times, 22 minutes were
down. Except, Kiryu was now caught behind a wall and four determined kids blocking his path.
“We… got you now!” Keiichi said, trying to catch his breath. All four kids were pretty tired, with
Kiryu barely breaking a sweat.

“Oh, do you?” Kiryu replied. “Is it too late to strike a deal?”
“Deal? What deal?” Rena inquired.
“Meep, me thinks he’s trying to just stall for time,” Rika stated, much to Kiryu’s chagrin. Dammit
Rika, can you give me a break here?
Kiryu shrugged his shoulders. “Well, it was worth a shot.” To the disbelief of everyone, he jumped
onto the nearby dumpster and then jumped as high as he could. He grabbed onto the roof above and
pulled himself up.
“W-What?! Y-you can’t do that!” Satoko yelled, accusingly.
He looked down at the stunned kids and stifled a chuckle. “Never said anything about using the
roofs.” He winked at them and with a running start, he jumped to a nearby roof. This one was
shorter than the previous one, and he was able to jump off and safely land on a nearby pile of
empty boxes.
The risk had paid off. He was able to completely confuse the kids on what direction he was taking
for a few seconds and was now considerably far from them. 24 minutes, six left. Just enough time
to run to his final destination.
They can’t complain if that’s still a part of Hinamizawa.

Only two minutes remained. In Hinamizawa, the few tourists that come will often be recommended

Okay, I can just rest here, and any minute I’ll win. Sorry kids, you did a great job but you underestiHe didn’t finish the thought. In briefly dropping his guard, he hadn’t noticed Mion had stayed
hidden and was now ready to tackle him. “Kiryu!” She yelled.

Kiryu was speechless. The girl had completely outwitted him. “... How did you know I’d come

“I didn’t. I just had a hunch you might, and hoped you would.”

Kiryu peeked into the memories of this fragment’s Kiryu, and sure enough, he had mentioned it a

Even during the Dam War, I got arrested a few times for throwing bricks.”

Kiryu was almost stunned. Here before him was a regular teenage girl talking about the yakuza as

“Do you ever have to deal with other yakuza groups? Where I come from, the Tojo Clan is pretty

Mion hesitated to reply. She was visibly shaken by the mention of the Tojo for only a split second,

She was lying, of course. There was the potential threat of war between the two, and both knew it.

“... Yeah, it could end up pretty awful.”

“Yep,” Mion continued. “I’m the Demoness of Hinamizawa. That’s why you lost.” She once again

Staring at the young girl, he was reminded of the young master, Diago. A young kid born into a
powerful yakuza family, one most likely expected to lead the family in the future. And yet with

Mion couldn’t meet Kiryu’s gaze. She looked away unsure of how to answer. After a minute

a bad thing?”

Kiryu wasn’t sure how to reply, so Mion continued. “You’re right, it’s not easy. Most girls my age

Mion kept her smile and shook her head no. “All that would cause is a power vacuum, and
everyone fighting over who gets to lead.”
Kiryu looked down at the ground in frustration. “I know that, but… even then.”
He looked back up only to see Mion much closer now. The girl before him had the most steadfast

Kiryu stayed silent hanging on her every word. “Just between you and me, even Grandma is hoping
to step back and take the Family in a new direction. One less like a yakuza, and more… safe and

change that.”
She looked away and faced the town below her. “This is my home. This is the community I grew
up in. These are the people I’ve made memories with and want to keep making more good
memories with. I want it to continue growing and prosper, and the only way to do that is to change

She looked back at Kiryu. “I want to be there leading the charge.”
“People like you are going to be the future of Hinamizawa, Kiryu.”

Kiryu was speechless. How could he say anything to the girl before him? One who could do
anything she set her mind to. One who’s conviction would not be swayed no matter what.

“There you are!” Keiichi cried out.
The two turned to see the rest of the kids had finally caught up. “We’ve been searching the last ten
minutes for you, guys! Why are you just standing up here? Did we win?!” Keiichi bombarded Mion

She nodded. “Of course, we did. I was the one who tagged him, of course. Y’know, not to brag.
Just saying.”
The kids cheered, and Kiryu remembering he’d have to deal with the penalty now took a big sigh.

Rika approached him. “Talk about anything interesting?” She asked softly.

“I have my ways, nipah!”
Kiryu still could not understand the mysterious girl before him, but that wasn’t what was on his

“The future of HInamizawa,” huh…

Chapter 20: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 3: Desire for Happiness
After receiving a penalty and meeting up with Rika, Kiryu was now home. It was evening, and the
higurashi sang their final melody before nighttime approached. Kiryu had done as Rika said and
had acquired the book with Rika’s letter. Despite everything that had happened, he still couldn’t
believe the contents of it.
In it, he found an incredible story. The origins of Hinamizawa Syndrome and its effects, the truth
behind the Watanagashi murders, Takano and the Mountain Dogs being Rika’s killers, and Rules X,
Y, and Z. Finally, the last section of the letter would talk about Rika’s ancestor Hanyuu.
This bit will be the hardest to wrap your head around. I’m sure you know of the legends of
Oyashiro. She’s my ancestor and the one whose powers have let me loop for over a century. I’m the
only one who can see or talk to her, but people at a critical level with the Syndrome can hear her
footsteps. I wouldn’t be surprised if you experienced it yourself last loop.
Kiryu froze up. Oh… that would explain a lot.
In simple terms, she’s like a ghost. She’s been my one companion throughout all these loops. Even if
you can’t see her, please know that she has been alongside me this whole time. She will be one of
our biggest allies.
This would have concluded Rika’s letter, but Kiryu had asked her a favor.
Finally, I don’t know why you asked about her specifically, but I’ll tell you what I can. Mion is
incredibly kind, compassionate, and loving. She will do anything to minimize suffering. She created
the game club to give Satoko and Satoshi shelter from their abusive family. She also created it as a
place to spread love and fun for everyone. She gave up on her feelings for Satoshi so that her sister
could be happy.
As the heir to the Sonozaki Family, she can easily fulfill the role and be equally cold and merciless.
Beneath all that though, is a girl who does deeply care for everyone and wants to lead the Family
in a new direction. Out of all the loops, she is the only one of my friends who has never contracted
the Syndrome. Chalk it up to her steadfast moral compass, her trust in her friends, her often being
the first to communicate and solve issues, etc.
Call it what you want, but she’s a natural-born leader. She’s never the one to suffer from it, … but
she’s almost always the one who suffered from the others getting it. I so desperately want to avoid
that happening in this loop, if possible Kiryu. I want none of my friends to suffer anymore. Please,
tomorrow talk with me about what to do next.
Sincerely, Rika
And with that, Kiryu was done reading. However, he was not remotely done absorbing all the info
he had just read. He looked over the letter again, reread certain sections, and repeated that for about
twenty minutes. At last, he sighed and went to the bathroom.
He washed his face and took a long look at himself in the mirror. I know what I said today, and I
intend to keep it. At the same time, how the fuck do I navigate this? What can I do to help this girl?

If something goes wrong again, would I even be able to loop with her or remember what happens
next time?
Anxiety and doubt wracked his mind, but he shook his head. Never mind, I can’t be acting how I
did last loop. I’ll figure it out like I did the Empty Lot.
He clenched his fists. And above all else, I will stop that Takano from ever hurting my students
again.

suffering from a god to one of mankind. As the man had done so to the girl before, so did the
goddess repay his actions by forgiving him and granting him the possibility of a peaceful future.

Chapter 22: Dragon Slaying Arc Bonus Chapter: Life Without
Living
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The year was 1988. Five years had passed since the Watanagashi of 1983, and the horrific events
that followed it. Even compared to the previous series of murders, it was unlike anything anyone
had ever seen. Every news outlet seemed to have covered it, and even half a decade later it was the
most common thing talked about in relation to the small town. Whatever good reputation
Hinamizawa had left, had vanished that night. Unlike the previous incidents however, there was an
identified killer. It was ruled a murder suicide with six victims in all.
A young CEO of a real estate company named Kiryu Kazuma was ruled as the murderer. There was
enough evidence to suggest he had done it. Blood of four of the five victims were found on him,
and the ways the victims had died leaned towards the man having done it using his bare hands. The
silver dragon tattoo on his back along with more research into his past quickly revealed ties to the
Yakuza, which further solidified the possibility of him being the criminal.
However, the whole case was rather bizarre. For one thing, the supposed murderer had died from
multiple stab and gunshot wounds. While the police had ruled it a murder suicide, there was
possible evidence he had been killed himself by one of the victims. A young girl by the name of
Rika Furude. She had been found dead, holding a gun with a knife next to her. Cause of death was a
shot through the head. Further investigation revealed her fingerprints had been on the knife and
gun. Had the girl possibly killed the man, and then killed herself?
Ultimately, whatever she had done didn’t matter. The case was complicated enough as is, and the
fact this crime had even happened in the first place was an awful look for the police. In an attempt
to save face, they quickly resolved the case and pinned it on the yakuza. Even if the girl had killed
him, she was now dead and there was no way she could have killed the other four victims
considering how they died.
For the police to even remotely consider that a pre-teen girl was a murderer and not a victim, much
less one that was near worshipped by the local people would have been catastrophically bad for
them. So it was brushed aside for a much more likely and reasonable story.
More details of the case leaked over time, and multiple conspiracies came out of it. Some thought it
was some final ritual of whatever horrific cult inhabited Hinamizawa, others thought maybe it was
a government cover up. Some even considered this was the result of Oyashiro itself, punishing the
evil denizes of the town. Nonetheless, the police would find themselves in good fortune.
That would end up being the last of the Watanagashi murders. It was also the last Watangashi to
have been held since then. With the heir of the Sonozaki Family and the last Furude being among
the victims, even the incredibly traditional residents of Hinamizawa could not bear to continue it. It
was now forever tainted with the blood of the victims, and no one dared suggesting to restart it out
of fear of the murders returning.
Within the last five years, about ⅓ of the residents have moved out. Some moved to Okinomiya
near by, others travelled much farther away. And with that came even more bizarre happenings. A

pattern emerged over time. Those who fled Hinamizawa seemed to change heavily. They either
often committed suicide some year or two after leaving, or would end up murdering someone else.
The already discriminated against residents were now nothing more than outcasts. The remaining
people in the town were mostly self-sufficient, but not a single soul had moved to the town. To say
the town had a bleak future would be an understatement.
We now turn our attention to a graveyard on the outskirts of Tokyo. There stood a gravestone with
the name “KIRYU KAZUMA” etched into the stone. It was heavily vandalized with multiple
messages saying things such as “Murderer!”, “Go to Hell!”, etc.
There stood a lone man in front of it. He looked to be in his late 20s, maybe early 30s. He was tall,
and wore a white suit jacket with a black dress shirt and black slacks. His hair was sleeked back,
and he looked he hadn’t slept in days, possibly years. He looked down at the gravestone with a mix
of emotions, mostly numbness.
No one else was around. After some time, he began to speak to himself in a low tone. “Well, Kiryu.
It’s been five years. I don’t know where the time went, but here we are. The Tojo is doing ok. Not
as well as it could be and there are fears for the future, but not everything is bad. I finally became
the leader of a family last year, and I have good people under me. Just three currently, but they get
the job done. You have to start somewhere, right?”
He paused for a few seconds, and then continued. “Y’know, I really do wonder what happened to
you. I know what everyone says, I know what even Dad said. I know what he said on his deathbed
last year. That it was his fault, and that he should have never brought you into the Yakuza. I don’t
care what anyone says.”
“I know you didn’t do it. You were set up, framed, or something. But I know damn well you didn’t
do it.” He began to tear up slightly. “There’s no way you could have. I was the only person in
contact with you those last few days, and I know something was up with you. Someone or
something drove you to this. This wasn’t you. I… I refuse to believe it was you even now.”
He wiped a tear from his eye weighed down by black bags underneath. “I’m sorry, bro. I told
myself I wouldn’t get emotional. I don’t know if you can even hear me, maybe I’m just still in
denial even now. Maybe this is just my way of coping with something I’ll never truly be able to
understand. I…”
His voice trailed off. He stood there for a few minutes staring vacantly at the resting place of his
once friend. “... I don’t know anymore, Kiryu. The last five years I’m not even sure how much I’ve
been living. You broke your promise and left me, and now so has Dad. What’s the point in being a
successful yakuza, when for all the power, money, and women I’ve attained I still feel nothing. ”
“... I’ve not felt anything I think, since that day. Only exception being with Dad passing. However,
as horrible as it is to say, it was… nothing compared to…”
He cut himself off again. “Sorry, I know you’d probably punch me, if I said anything else about
Dad. I just… what do I do Kiryu? Do I quit the Yakuza and live an honest life like you did? Can I
even do that at this point? Do I have… any hope of finding any sort of happiness?”
No answer came. As much as the man maybe wanted one, the dead could not speak to the living.
After some time, he found himself softly laughing. Not to anyone in particular, it was just a pathetic
attempt to console himself. What am I doing? It doesn’t matter how often I come here or try to find

answers. It’s really fucking sad I can’t move past this. They say time heals all wounds. How many
more years is it going to take to heal mine?
He paused when he noticed someone else had entered the graveyard. It looked to be a young
woman in her late teens or early 20s. She had long green hair, and wore a black dress. She wore a
black funeral hat, and seemed to fit right in with the scenery. He assumed she was there to visit a
friend or relative, and figured he had stayed long enough and did not want to intrude on her
personal time.
He was about to leave, when he realized she was walking right towards him. The hat made her
expression hard to make out, but it seemed somber to him. She was some ten feet away when she
stopped, and looked straight at him. She asked him a simple, but unexpected question. “Did you
know that man?”
The man was unsure how to answer. He had visited his friend’s grave many times, but this was the
first time he had ever had company. “P-pardon?”
“Did you know that man?” She repeated in a monotone voice.
“... Yes, who are you?”
The woman did not reply. She simply stood still, and the man was not 100% sure if she was a
human or perhaps a spirit that had decided to speak with him. Finally, she spoke. “Just someone
who wonders. Wonders why I trusted the man behind you. The one who took everything from me,
and had the audacity to leave as well.”
The man was stunned, to say the least. “W-who are you?!” He said, unintentionally raising his
voice.
“... My name doesn’t matter. I just happened to be nearby, and wanted to ask a few questions, since
you seemed to have known him well.”
“Are… are you related to one of the victims?”
She didn’t answer. She ignored him, and continued her questions. “Do you know why he did what
he did?”
This woman frustrated the man, but he controlled his temper. He figured for now it was best to just
answer. “No, I don’t. I… I don’t even think he did it, truthfully.”
At this, the girl finally changed her expression. Her mouth remained closed, but up close you could
tell she was gritting her teeth. “Bullshit,” she said in a soft tone.
“W-what?”
“BULLSHIT!!” The girl had ripped off her funeral mask, and stared at the man. Whatever
expression he thought he had saw had completely disappeared, and all that remained was a furious,
heartbroken girl. To his shock, she pulled out a gun and aimed it right at him.
“W-woah! Hang on! What are you doing?!” The man asked frantically.
“Something I should have done a long time ago,” she said in a deep, threatening voice. “It’s
because of you…. because of you…”

She couldn’t even speak coherently with how much she was shaking from rage. “They’re all dead
because of you!”
She began to walk towards him, gun in hand. The man tried to back away a few steps, but ended up
tripping and falling on his back. Before he knew it, the girl was right above him aiming right at his
head.
“Don’t you dare say he didn’t do it! I know you sent him to Hinamizawa! I know it was you, who
gave him the idea! Don’t you fucking dare say it wasn’t his or your fault!!”
The man wasn’t sure how, but the girl had found out the origin of all this. A night, the man had
regretted for the last five years. He wished he had never spoken about that cursed town to him.
Maybe Kiryu would still be with him, and they could be happy together. That was just a wish
though, and the cruel state of things was all too real.
In truth, he always blamed himself. Unfairly of course, it wasn’t him that had murdered the
children. Still though, he had sent Kiryu there to Hinamizawa, and he loathed himself since then.
He had had nightmares of a situation like this happening. Someone killing him to avenge the
victims.
And yet, to be in that situation right now, he felt almost peaceful. He wasn’t that different from his
brother at the end of the day. If the girl in front of him so decided to pull the trigger, he would not
complain. For in his mind, maybe this was the only way he atone.
He looked at the girl with a mix of understanding and acceptance. “Go ahead, pull the trigger.”
At this, the girl was fazed. She had expected the man to beg for her to not kill him, maybe bribe
her, or even put up a fight. All she saw though, was a man that looked dead inside. Perhaps more so
than her. She had come ready to do whatever it took to kill him. A sibling for a sibling, and yet she
found herself unable to even hold the gun correctly.
“I… I really will shoot! Do you hear me?!” The man did not respond, but simply nodded his head.
He closed his eyes and waited for the bullet to be shot. What was just a few seconds felt like an
eternity for the both of them. After what seemed like eons, the girl slowly but surely lowered her
gun. The man opened his eyes to see she had dropped it to the ground.
“... Why?” That was all the girl could muster to say. Tears stained her cheeks, and she didn’t know
what to do with herself. “Why? You know him better than anyone, right? Please tell me why? Why
did he betray me and kill Sis? Why did he kill Keiichi, Rena, Rika, and Sa… Sa-!”
At this, the girl lost control of her emotions. She fell to her kness, and bawled. The man did not
move. He could do nothing, but stare back at her. Wishing he had the answers. Wishing she had put
him out of his misery. After a long silence, he finally spoke. Perhaps out of obligation to her, or just
for himself. He said, “I don’t know.”
The girl looked up at him, her vision blurry from tears. The man continued. “I have no answers for
you, and I don’t think I ever will. All we can do is… just live on. Continue to live for them, or else
they died for nothing. I wish I were dead. I wish you had shot me then and there, but… I suppose
Kiryu would hate me for that.”
The quiet enveloped the two again, and after some time the girl spoke up. “Do you truly believe he
didn’t do it?”

“... I don’t know. I just know… something drove him to this. And it drives me insane that despite
my best efforts, I’ve found nothing. Nothing, nothing, and still nothing. I don’t expect you to
believe me, but… I hope you can find peace someday”
The girl didn’t reply. She just stood up, grabbed the gun and hat, and turned around. She took a few
paces, and then said one final thing. “There is no peace for me to have anymore. I will live for
them, but that’s all I can do. Maybe once I’m dead I’ll finally find it. Maybe once you’re dead, and
rot along with him I can find it that way. Maybe once the whole Tojo has been buried will its many
victims find peace. All I know is that I never want to see your face again. Go to Hell, you bastard.”
And that was that. That was the last time either of them saw each other. The girl never did give the
man his name, but it wasn’t hard to tell she was Shion Sonozaki. A woman that had lost everything,
and was still going downhill in life. She was a regular alcoholic by then, and one day a few years
later she died from a fall. She was drunk on a balcony, had for some reason gotten on top of it, lost
her footing, and fell forty feet to her gruesome death.
Even if her life was tragic, she still got her wish in a way. The man was named Akira Nishikiyama,
and had died in prison some five years later. He had killed his own boss committing patricide. They
found his body one morning with twenty different stab wounds. The Tojo’s strength continued to
diminish, and after a major war with the Omi Alliance it found itself a shell of its former self.
Eventually, it was disbanded and the thousands of members joined the Omi, some other criminal
orginization, or tried to live on the straight or narrow.
As for Hinamizawa, it did remain. While it heavily struggled for many years, it eventually was able
to recover its reputation somewhat. A handful of people moved in, and the town would eventually
become something similar to its prime. The Watanagashi would stay dead however, and truth be
told it was probably for the best. For several decades to come, people would still fear the curse of
Oyashiro. In some ways, it still existed with the many incidences concerning ex-residents. Time
would go on, and eventually even that final Watangashi would be forgotten by most people. But
nothing would ever truly erase the scars of that night.

More like the errand girl.

Chapter 24: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 6: Ye Olde Traps

That creeping sense of unease wormed its way back into Kiryu’s mind. Please, oh please let this

It was Friday morning, and that meant big things. It was an important day for everyone. Everyone

Kiryu's eyes opened. The first thing he noticed was not the sun shining through his windows, but
rather the sound of the ever-present higurashi. A sound he had mixed feelings on, but one that was

Last night, he and Rika learned from Hanyuu that Takano had never returned. A fact that was

As he got dressed, his mind drifted to Satoko. Rika had mentioned offhand that she was at a

mouth, were they even words or just noises of a despondent animal? It was mostly
incomprehensible, but bits could be picked out from the stream of sorrow. Words such as “forgive”,
“I’m sorry,” “my fault”, etc. How long had she been like this, and how much longer would she fall
deeper still?
A set of footprints could be heard coming down the hall. After a moment, she appeared in the
doorway. It was Oryou Sonozaki staring at her mess of a granddaughter on the floor. It wasn’t one
of hatred, but more of pity. Mion saw her out of the corner of her eye and looked up. She said
nothing but just looked at Oryou, her face splattered with tears. “Grandma, p… p-please, help me.”

Her cry for help was almost pathetic. It was a barely audible voice, one that took everything just to
muster out every single word. Oryou took a deep breath in and out. “Well, accepting this wasn’t
your fault would be a good first step.”
Something stirred in Mion. She gritted her teeth and buried her face in her hands. “But it was!” She
sobbed. “If I hadn’t brought her here… if I had just been more careful! Why?! Why did this have to
happen?!”
Oryou had no true answers. She could only state what she knew. “Life is cruel. It is also equally a
fragile thing. Too many people die young. I’ve seen it happen too much.”
Mion didn’t reply, she just continued to cry. A few minutes passed, and she finally spoke. “... What
am I supposed to tell the others? How can I face them? How… how can I face Shion?! Because of
me… because of me!”
A slap rang out. To Mion’s shock, it was Oryou herself who had delivered it to her. “Get ahold of
yourself. The Heir of all people should know what comes next.”
Mion’s head was empty. As much as she loved her grandmother, how could she expect her to be
able to think under these circumstances? “I… I don’t understand.”
Oryou stared at her and then sighed. “I’m sorry. I always forget that as mature as you are, as much
as you are the perfect pick for the Heir… you are still just a young girl.” Oryou put her hands on
Mion’s shoulders. The best way she could think to comfort her, as she continued. “Like I said, it
was an accident. … but it can’t stay that way.”
Mion’s blood rand cold. “W-what are you…”
“Mion Sonozaki, you are the Heir to our Family. You know the significance of someone dying on
our property. Much more so it being the last of the Hojos.”
Bile rose to Mion’s throat. She wanted to throw up. She wanted to empty every part of her, and
never have to hear such a horrid thing again. And yet, she couldn’t. She knew what her grandma
meant. She knew her duties also as the Heir. And yet, it locked her in place as her brain desperately
tried to understand the situation she had found herself in.
Did she really think the police would trust her? That it was just an “accident’? Especially right
before Watanagashi? Someone like Ooishi has been chomping at the bit to get something like this
for years. Ooishi wouldn’t trust her, for sure. Neither would the police, likely. Would the rest of her
family even believe her? What about the residents of Hinamizawa? Would even her friends trust
her? Would Kiryu trust her?
Mion was speechless, so Oryou took it upon herself to continue. “We’ll have to get some sort of
body double. It’ll be challenging due to it being a child, but it’s not impossible. You both will be
‘sick’ with something to keep either of you from having to show up. We’ll…”
She stared at Mion’s face. What could be used to describe it? Perhaps broken, or non-functioning.
Oryou sighed again. She thought long and hard about what to say next. “I’m sorry, Mion. I
shouldn’t be pushing you so hard. You can get through this. I’ll handle it.”
This seemed to wake Mion from her stupor. As her grandma looked away trying to decide what to
do next, she spoke up. “I’ll… I’ll do it.”

Oryou looked back. Her face was the closest thing her old bones could do to resemble shock. “...
Are you sure?”
“... Yes,” she said finally standing up. “I am… Mion Sonozaki. I am the heir to the Sonozaki
Family. I must hold myself responsible and fix this. I promise Grandma, I’ll… I’ll solve this.” Her
words limply dropped off her lips. She meant what she said, and yet every fiber of her being felt
disgusted. She wanted so desperately to tell Keiichi and the others what had happened. To beg for
forgiveness, but she couldn’t. She was the Heir, and she had to see that through. If this got out there
would be no more Sonozakis, and as much as it pained her heart. As much as she was killing her
sense of self to deal with her horrific task. She was the Heir, and she couldn’t back down no matter
what.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter 28: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 10: Even With Love, Can It
Be Seen?
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

After much hustle and bustle, the preparations for the festival were done. Goodbyes were said, and
final touches were made. The sun slowly began to disappear across the horizon saying goodbye as
well. The higurashi sang their song, but that was nothing new. At least, it was not for Rika, as she
walked to her home.
“Everything ok, Rika?” Hanyuu asked.
“Yeah, I’m just worried about Satoko and Mion,” Rika answered. “Can you remember a fragment
where either got sick before Watanagashi?”
Hanyuu thought about it. “Maybe once or twice? I’m not sure. There’s always been the chance of
someone… well…”
Rika sighed. “Yes, I know. There’s always been that dan syndrome. However,” she said, facing
Hanyuu. “Mion has never gotten the syndrome before. I know that for a fact. She’s the one person I
can always rely on no matter what. I… I trust her.”
She turned back and began walking again. “It’s Satoko I’m more concerned about. I know Oryou
said she’d call Irie about it, but I’ll double-check with him in case.” Everything has gone well so
far, perhaps too well. I need to make sure everyone stays safe.
Hanyuu seemed flustered. “I understand what you’re saying Rika, but shouldn’t I at least check on
them both?”
Rika paused. “... It can’t hurt, but make sure you talk to Kiryu first. We need to stay in contact.”
Hanyuu nodded. “You got it!”
Hanyuu was about to leave when Rika spoke up. “By the way, thank you, Hanyuu. For…
everything honestly.”
“Where is this coming from?”
“I know it’s not the first time I’ve said this recently, but I am truly grateful for all you’ve done for
me.”
Hanyuu avoided eye contact. “You’ve said a lot of nice stuff to me recently. I appreciate it, but… I
don’t believe you should think so highly of me.”
Rika tilted her head. “Why? It’s a miracle I’m still here, and it’s all because of you.”
Hanyuu sighed and put on a more serious expression. “That’s all I’ve really been doing. For the
past century, I’ve been… mostly selfish, I think.”

Rika’s face became somber. She had an idea what Hanyuu was talking about, but she wanted to let
her finish speaking. “All this scouting out and information gathering. All the stuff I’ve done in
general to help. Isn’t it… horrific of me that I’ve not started doing that till now. Couldn’t I have
found out who the murderer was, if I had just been braver? Every time I ran away after you had
gotten captured because I didn’t want to see you die. … Isn’t that the definition of selfishness?
Could I not have caused this century of suffering to end much sooner?”
Rika closed her eyes. Her guess was right on the mark. “We both ran away, Hanyuu. I lost hope and
didn’t believe in my friends. I probably could have remembered Takano killing me, if I tried. I
didn’t though, so I could escape the pain. I suppose I couldn’t entirely blame myself. Physically,
I’m still just a child, and mentally it took a very long time to reach how I am today. Still, you’re
forgetting something important.”
“W-what, Rika?”
Rika softly smiled. “It was Keiichi remembering his sins that was the catalyst for my hope.”
Hanyuu went to say something, but nothing came out. There was a pause, and then she spoke. “I
know, but wouldn’t knowing Takano’s identity have helped?”
“Perhaps, but also perhaps not. What if I had zoned in on trying to kill Takano? What if I had
become a murderer? What if I had never learned her background, and wanted to save her? What if I
completely lost sight of everything I had been working towards, focusing just on revenge and
survival?”
At that, Hanyuu didn’t have an answer. “Perhaps, you’re right. It was selfish of you, but I can
somewhat understand where you’re coming from. If we do find a happy ending, you… won’t be
able to stick around forever. And then you’ll be all alone again.”
Hanyuu bit her lip. “That doesn’t excuse my actions. I may be able to forgive the sins of man, but
who can forgive the sins of a god?”
“I don’t know, but I’ve already forgiven you long ago, Hanyuu. I’ve given you your fair share of
bad treatment, but that’s just… how family is sometimes. We’ve only ever had each other. It’s
because of our love for each other that we can see past our flaws and sins. It’s because of your love
for humanity you died for them, and want to create a world without sin. And it’s because of your
love you’ve inspired me to want to forgive and save everyone… even someone like Takano.”
Hanyuu couldn’t utter a word, but she eventually smiled. She let out a big sigh as well. “You have
no idea how much of a relief it is to hear those words. Thank you, Rika. Let’s continue going
forward aiming for both of our goals.”
Rika nodded her head. “Of course, it’s getting late, though. You’d best head on over to Kiryu’s
place.”
“Right!” She waved goodbye and disappeared from view. And with that, Rika began to walk home
again.

The mountains surrounding HInamizawa would soon swallow up the sun. It normally wouldn’t take
this long for Rika to get home. It was only about a ten-minute walk from the shrine, but her

conversation with Hanyuu was an important one. One she was glad to have finally been able to
have done.
She was now within sight of her home. It was a shabby old thing, but it was perfect for the two
girls. She took out a key from her dress pocket and unlocked the door. It opened to the dark, but
familiar hallway. The click of a light switch was heard, and the room was filled with artificial light.
“Satoko, I’m ho-”
She cut herself off remembering Satoko wasn’t there. It was just muscle memory for her at that
point. Usually, Satoko would have dinner ready by now. Something simple and cheap, but enough
to tide over the two girls.
In reality, it always felt so incredibly lonely, when she wasn’t there. Memories of previous
fragments where Satoko was trapped with Teppei filled Rika’s head, and she flinched at the graphic
images of Satoko’s despondent face. The bruises that stretched all over her body like a canvas of
torment.
She shook her head violently desperate to be rid of them. That’s not happening. That’s not
happening. She went into the living room and sat down. She sank deep into the chair. She was half
tempted to grab some wine, but she didn’t want Hanyuu to be feeling it. She looked over at the
phone. One that the Mountain Dogs had most likely already bugged. Not that that mattered when
she was just calling the Irie Clinic.
She picked up the phone and heard it ring until eventually, Irie picked up. “Hello, Rika?”
“Meep, how is Satoko doing?”
“Ah, Satoko! Yes, she’s at the Sonozaki estate still. I examined her, and it seemed to just be some
food poisoning. With enough rest, she should be good by tomorrow evening. One of the members
of the family came and picked up her medicine.”
Rika sighed in relief. “Thank you, Irie. I’m happy to hear she’ll be better soon. The medicine
should still work fine, right?”
Irie hesitated for a moment. “I… can’t 100% say there won’t be any side effects, but she should be
fine. It’s certainly a lot better than the alternative…”
Rika silently nodded. “Please take care of her, Irie. I know you can do it!”
“Thank you, Rika. Have a good night.”
“You too.”
As Rika hung up the phone, she relaxed in the chair. See Hanyuu, I told you everything was ok.
Irie had also just hung up. He looked back at a tall, burly man. He had sharp eyes, the type one got
spending most of their time in the underworld. He was a member of the Sonozaki Family.
Somewhat low on the ladder, but trusted enough to do his job well. One that had been observing
Irie for some time now. Beads of sweat ran down Irie’s face.
“There, I did what you wanted. Now, please leave. I’ve been on good terms with the Sonozakis for
years now. What have I done to deserve this… this harassment tonight?”

The yakuza’s expression didn’t change. “Not my place to say, pal. I’m just doing my job, and that
currently is to make sure you do yours.”
Irie gritted his teeth. He wished he could be braver, but he knew well what the Sonozakis were
capable of. He dared not get on their bad side, but he was at least brave enough to ask a question.
“What has happened to Satoko?! You’d best have not done anything to her!”
“You think I know, bud? Even if I did, I wouldn’t tell your sorry ass. I suggest you start closing up
and pretend none of this ever happened. At least, if you know what’s good for you.”
“... F-fine! Be that way, but I’d be more worried about your family. I can’t do anything to you, but-”
“Hang on fuckface, a call is coming in.” Irie was brutally cut off, as the yakuza’s phone began to
ring. He desperately wanted to speak up, but kept calm and listened. After a few minutes, he hung

The way he had phrased it was ominous to Irie. Before he could even consider what it would be,
the yakuza spoke plainly. “Tomorrow morning, Satoko Hojo will be feeling well enough to attend
the festival. You will have seen her and deemed her to be healthy. She won't show up for the
festival, though. Monday morning, a corpse will be found. It will be Satoko Hojo’s. It will be a
fake, but you will deem it as the real body. That is all, have a good night.”
Irie was speechless, as the yakuza began to leave. A wrath and fury rare for him welled up inside
him. However, before he could even yell out, he found himself a few inches away from a gun. It
was aiming right at his head. “Don’t get any ideas now. A pawn should know its place. And don’t
think you can get away with telling the police or anything, we have eyes everywhere this
Watanagashi.” The yakuza gave an evil smirk. “Consider it a family reunion of sorts. We’ve got
just about the whole family in Hinamizawa at this point. Sure would be a shame, if something
happened to you.”
Irie was still facing down the gun in front of him. “I… I may not be able to do anything, but you
don’t know what you’re messing with. There are people besides you and your family working in
the shadows here.”
The yakuza tilted his head in confusion, and then his eyes lit up. “Ohhhhhhh, that’s right! Thanks
for the reminder, bud. I had nearly forgotten to tell you this. Seems uh… the Tojo Clan has
delivered us a message. One that you are free to share since the whole damn town will know by
morning.”
Irie held his breath. Whatever came next, he knew it was bad news.

The sun had just about disappeared now. The evening had given way to nighttime, and the warm
darkness surrounded Hinamizawa. In the Sonozaki Estate, Mion stood hunched over in her
bathroom. It wasn’t a pretty sight. She had vomited for the second time that day, some blood mixed
in this time. She wanted to look away from what had spawned inside her, but the guilt and anxiety
that had caused it to begin with forced her to look on. She felt it was an accurate reflection of
herself. Disgusting and putrid, something that shouldn’t be seen by other humans.
She wasn’t actually supposed to be sick, but she might as well have been now. She had always been
able to shut down her emotions and tackle whatever was needed for her. She was the Heir to the

Sonozaki Family, she had to. She had given the orders to confront Irie and to search out a body
substitute for Satoko. All of that with the cold, heartless persona she had developed for such
situations.
But where was that now to save her? She couldn’t run away from this. She couldn’t look away, and
pretend nothing was wrong. That wasn’t remotely how she was, to begin with. She always was the
one to take charge, communicate, and be a leader for everyone. Stuck between her friends and her
role as the Heir, what could she do, though? What was the right path she should take?
She finally forced herself to look away. The rancid stench caused her to gag, as she flushed it down.
She took yet another pill to help with her stomach, praying for any sort of relief from this hell she
had found herself in. “God, please save me. I don’t know if you exist or not, but please forgive me.
Please, please forgive me for what I’ve done.” The girl went on like that for a while.
No one was there to comfort her. She only had herself. She nearly jumped out of her skin, when she
suddenly heard the phone ring. Slowly, she turned to it. The thought of picking up that phone made
her stomach churn, but she had to. Whether it was the police or someone else, she was the only one
there right now. The rest of the family was busy guarding the estate, and Oryou was busy herself
with how to deal with Satoko’s death. She finally mustered the energy to pick up the phone. “Hhello?”
“Hey, Mion. How is Satoko?” Did her heart stop beating, or did her brain cease to function? Either
way, she spoke not a word. It was the last person she wanted to have heard. “Mion, are you there?”
Keiichi asked.
“... K-Kei, is that you?” Mion’s voice was weak. Perhaps it was both a blessing and a curse she felt
sick since Keiichi bought it immediately.
“Damn, are you alright, Mion? Er, sorry that’s a stupid question. Obviously, you’re not. I just
wanted to call and see if you and Satoko are ok.”
“Y-yeah, we’re doing ok. Irie came over, and diagnosed it as food poisoning,” she said, lying
through her teeth. Luckily, Keiichi couldn’t see her.
Keiichi smirked. “Ahhhh, that’ll do it. Must’ve been from your cooking, huh?”
Normally, Mion would be irritated at Keiichi’s quips, but it was almost a reassuring comfort. A
brief escape from reality. “Kei, c’mon. You’re gonna give me crap when I’m like this?”
“Hehe, sorry. Couldn’t resist. By the way, do you think both of you will be able to join us at
Watanagashi, tomorrow?”
It felt like someone had stabbed her. She hadn’t thought about the festival, she hadn’t wanted to. It
was just one more thing Satoko would never be able to do again. One more thing Mion herself
wasn’t sure if she’d be able to do again herself. All she could do was lie and lie till it all came
crashing down. ‘I-I don’t know, maybe. We’ll have to see.”
“Mmm, in that case, you’d best get some rest. I hope I didn’t wake you or Satoko up.”
“No, she’s asleep right now in the guest room. Thank you for checking in on us.”

“No problem! Get better soon, I got some club games I have to beat you in next week,” he said,
grinning.
“You wish. Good night, Kei.”
“Good night, Mion.”
And with that, she hung up the phone. The only thing keeping her from rushing to the bathroom
again was the stomach medicine doing its work. Not that it made her feel any less awful. She put
her face into her pillow, as she began to sob. She had lied to one of her friends. Something she
strived to never do. She had lied about Satoko being ok. She had even given Keiichi some hope that
she might see them both, or at least one at the festival. Something that would never happen again.
But the worst thing of all was that she had lied to someone she loved. Someone who even if he
miraculously loved her back would assuredly never forgive her for what she’s done.

2 things:
1. I've always wondered about what is like... not a plot hole, but kind of a weird thing about
Hanyuu. People always ask why she couldn't just like follow Takano, and see her as the
murderer. That it makes Hanyuu come off as extremely selfish, and tbh I've seen people hate
her over it. This throws in a bit of headcanon, but I wanted to tackle it and I do believe Rika
would be the type to not only be aware of it, but forgive Hanyuu for it. If you were someone
that read Higu and had this complaint, I hope I tackled it in an at least somewhat satisfactory
manner.
2. Yeeees, I know. There's some Umineko sprinkled in here. I won't spoil anything about it,
but it does very much feel like both a deconstruction and reconstruction of what Ryu did with
Higu. I just think it's fun to play around with the themes a bit here. I promise I won't be cheeky
and add in some Umi reference every chapter.

Chapter 29: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 11: Unexpected

Sunshine weaved its way to Kiryu’s eyes. A familiar buzz played in his ears. One that existed
somewhere between background noise and a slight annoyance. After a brief meeting with Hanyuu
last night, he had learned about Mion and Satoko being sick. While somewhat worried, he was sure
Irie would be able to take care of them both.
He was going through his typical morning routine when his phone suddenly rang. “Hello?”
“Kiryu! Some serious shit is going down right now!” Nishiki yelled at him over the phone.
Kiryu immediately paused what he was doing, and made sure he didn’t miss a single word. “What’s

After some back and forth his eyes lit up. He hung up the phone, finished getting dressed, and left
as fast as possible.

The morning sun shone down on Okinomiya brightly. Kiryu had just gotten off the bus and was
rushing down the street. He nearly knocked over a few passersby, as he barrelled down the
sidewalk. After a few blocks, he finally found what he was looking for. There was a small crowd
surrounding what looked like the scene of a crime.
Taking a moment to catch his breath, he cautiously approached. It’s not that he didn’t believe what
Nishiki had told him over the phone, but he had to see it for himself. He couldn’t get too close due
