Kiryu looked around to see if there was anyone he could potentially ask to confirm who exactly had
died. That was until one of the other people in the crowd spoke up. “Do you think it was the work
of the Sonozakis?”
“Nah, the word is going around it was the Tojo.”
“Yeah, but why the hell would they kill some nurse?”
“Same reason this sorta stuff always happens. Don’t poke your nose where it doesn’t belong, and it
won’t get bitten off.”
“Excuse me!” Kiryu spoke up. The two men turned to face Kiryu. “Would either of you know the
name of the murder victim?” Both were baffled not just at this yakuza-looking man asking them for
info, but also that he was asking in such an unusually straightforward fashion. The two looked at
each other, and then back to Kiryu. “Her name was Miyo Takano. What’s it to you?”

And with that, Kiryu’s heart dropped. He didn’t answer, but instead let out a sigh. “Nothing, just…
wanted to know.” And with that, he left the two confused men. He had purposefully avoided having
a cigarette for a few days, but now was the best time he could think of to have one. One that would
not help dull the headache he could already feel forming in the back of his head.
~~~~
One bus ride later, and he was back in Hinamizawa. It was about noontime. The town was quite
lively brimming with tourists. While the number had gone down over the years, there was still a
healthy amount of visitors to the village every year. It was one of the few things that kept the
village’s economy going.
There were also several cop cars patrolling. With the recent murder, everyone was on high alert.
The general public wasn’t aware at large of what had happened, and they were determined to make
sure no more murders happened that day. Of course, Ooishi was there. He was doing his rounds
along with his subordinate, Katsuya. “You hanging in there, Katsuya? This heat is a killer, I tell
you.”
His subordinate never could quite get used to his superior’s very casual and sometimes odd way of
saying things. “Yes, Sir. There have been no signs of anyone suspicious thus far.”
“Nfufufu, that’s how it always goes.”
There was a brief pause between the two until Katsuya asked a question. “Sir, what’s your take on
Miyo Takano’s death?”
“Take?” He said, scratching behind his ear. “It’s a tragic murder, for sure.”
Katsuya slightly rolled his eyes. “No, I mean that it doesn’t seem to fit the pattern of past
Watanagashi murders. It’s been consistent for four years, why would it suddenly change up? And
more specifically, why do the Tojo and not the Sonozakis seem to be responsible?”
Ooishi gave a sly smile and turned up the air conditioning a notch. “It’s simple really. It’s a
distraction.”
Katsuya looked puzzled. “A… distraction, Sir?”
“Nfufufu, my ‘take’ is that the Sonozakis are working with the Tojo. I’m not sure yet how they
mutually benefit from this, but it is far too much of a coincidence for it to happen today. I’m
positive those damned Sonozakis are seeking to continue the Watanagashi murders.”
“So you think the Tojo just killed some random nurse that works here to keep us busy?
Ooichi’s eyebrows furrowed as he turned the AC up to max. “It’s not that I haven’t explored other
avenues. The yakuza are a cruel, heartless people. There is no real difference between the Tojo or
Sonozaki Family. They’re all criminals at the end of the day. There’s the obvious notion she was
involved in something illegal, and I’m finding myself now a lot more interested in that Irie Clinic
she worked at.”
He returned to his usual smile. “Regardless, our job is to protect the people here tonight. We can
worry about who killed her and why later. You know the drill at this point.”

“Yes, Sir!”

Meanwhile, Kiryu had speed-walked through the crowded center of the town. He was heading for
Rika’s house. He wasn’t sure if she had received the news yet, but they had to discuss what would
happen next. The conversation with Nishiki kept replaying in his head.
“What do you mean Takano was murdered?!”
“I’m not sure what happened. I just know whatever deal she was trying to strike with the Tojo went
south fast. Some sort of major disagreement, and well… I wonder if she was killed right here at
HQ.”
“Nishiki, when did you first hear about this?”
“An hour or so ago, but I’m sure it must’ve happened last night. It takes about six hours to drive up

He was finishing the last bits of his cigarette when he found himself in front of Rika’s house. He

As he walked in, his memory flashed back to the nightmare that was the end of the last loop. He
wasn’t exactly fond of coming here, but they had to make a plan. As he walked in, he saw Rika

He struggled to find the right words to say. “Rika… I…”
“It’s fine.” Her voice was quiet. “I should have seen something like this coming.” She remained in

Kiryu sighed and sat down in the seat across from Rika. “I’m assuming this is the first time Takano

“Yes,” Hanyuu chimed in. “I… I don’t know what to say.”
“Does this mean… Rika is safe now?”
“Takano is dead, and that’s what you’re asking?” Rika had slightly raised her head, her eyes a mix

Neither Kiryu nor Hanyuu had an answer. Sensing he had been a bit insensitive, he switched his

The question stung Rika, but it was an important one to answer. In truth, she wasn’t sure what she
felt. She was far more forgiving of a person than she should have probably been, but that didn’t

But in the end, that’s just now who she was. Whether she wanted to or not, she knew Takano better

the first things this girl said upon seeing Satoko’s death was that it was a fake body? Was she just in
denial? No, she said it with almost too much confidence.
There was none of the usual relaxed feeling he had, Ooishi was staring at Rika fully suspicious.
“What do you know, girl?”
Before Rika could answer, Kiryu set down the body and got up. He was about to leave when Ooishi
put a hand on his shoulder. “Woah, hang on there Mr. Dragon. I know you’re a busy man and all,
but I can’t imagine you’re going shopping now.”
Kiryu didn’t reply at first. He simply looked back. Ooishi reflexively pulled back his hand. It was
an expression he had seen more than once. The eyes of a man, who had nothing to lose and was
certainly not about to be stopped by him. “I’m going to the Sonozaki Estate. If you want to follow,
be there in 20 minutes. I’m going with or without your help.”
And with that, he began walking away. Rika quickly followed after Kiryu yelling for him to wait.
One of the cops walked towards Ooishi. He looked like his nerves were shot. “S-Sir, who the hell
was that man? I’ve seen a lot of dangerous folks in my time on the force, but that man… that man
was different.”
Ooishi wiped the sweat from his brow. His fear finally fading. “That was the Dragon of Dojima. …
And he certainly lives up to the legend.”
“Sir, what should we do?”

“... Call for all the units we have. Have the Sonozaki Estate surrounded immediately. Something
big is about to happen, and we’re going to need all the damage control we can get.”
“And that man, Sir? Should we do something about him?” The officer reluctantly asked, unsure if
they even could do anything to the man.
Ooishi paused and then gave a sly smile. “Can’t believe I’m saying this, but I’m more worried
about the Sonozakis.”
~~~
Kiryu was in his house. He had already put on a bulletproof vest and was putting on what appeared
to be some sort of gauntlets. He was about to put on some brass knuckles when Rika burst in. She
was huffing and puffing from trying to keep up with Kiryu. “K-Kiryu, wait! Think about what we
talked about last night. You can’t just-”
“I’m not going to die,” he said, interrupting her. Brass knuckles equipped, he looked ready to face
anything. “We both know the Sonozakis are involved at this point, and I’m going to make them
give me the truth.”
“It’s… it’s not you dying I’m afraid of at this point.”
Kiryu’s wrath had subsided enough he could understand what Rika meant. “I’m not going to hurt
Mion, and I’m not going to kill any of them, either.”
Rika looked at him skeptically. “Kiryu, we both know you don’t need weapons to…”
She didn’t want to finish, but he knew she was referring to the bloodbath last loop. A chill ran
down Kiryu’s back, and he slowly took the brass knuckles off. He felt humiliated that he hadn’t
considered that he very well could repeat his sins if he wasn’t careful.
“Promise me, Kiryu. Promise me you’ll come back alive. And if possible, please… save Mion.”
Kiryu kneeled and hugged Rika. “I’m sorry I’ve already broken my promise and wasn’t able to
protect Satoko. I swear I’ll save Mion, and protect her no matter what.”
Rika began to cry. “It’s not your fault. And I trust in Mion that it’s not her’s either.”
“I know. I do too.”
“And… if you have to break some bones and crack some ribs, do it. Just please go easy on them,
while still protecting yourself.”
“I will. I swear it.”

Chapter End Notes

Strained my back a bit last week, ironically. I know how Shion feels now.

Chapter 31: Demon's Tears Arc Chapter 13: A Real Yakuza
Chapter Notes

A Yakuza long battle theme may enhance the experience while reading this. Any will do, but I

As Kiryu was saying goodbye to Rika, he saw Rena and Keiichi running towards him. They looked
panicked and out of breath. “Kiryu, what’s going on?!” Keiichi yelled.
“Is Satoko ok or not?!” Rena added.
Kiryu looked at them sternly. “Listen well.” The two stopped in their tracks. “Rika can fill you in
on everything. I have to go. Please stay safe, and watch over Rika. I’m going to see Mion.”
Before either of them could say anything, he ran off towards the Sonozaki Estate. Both faced Rika
looking for answers. She took a breath. “I don’t have anything concrete for you. All I know is that
the body they found was a fake, and we both think the Sonozakis are involved.”
Neither Keiichi nor Rena knew what to make of this. Rena’s expression sharpened. “I think
something is wrong with Mion.”
“What do you mean?” Keiichi asked.
“Do you remember Friday when we were in the library? Mion was worried about Kiryu potentially
being this ‘legendary yakuza’, and was having issues trusting him. Kiryu would never do
something to her, but if it was something involving her family…”
A heavy silence surrounded the trio. Keiichi perked up. “Now that you mention it, I called Mion
Saturday to check up on her and Satoko. She sounded… anxious, but I just thought it was because
she was sick. She also wasn’t at the festival last night. Rika, have you heard anything from Mion
recently?”
Rika didn’t reply. Her mind was too distracted by what Rena had said. If Mion knows Kiryu is the
Dragon of Dojima then… is he going to be ambushed?!
She quickly grabbed Keiichi and Rena’s hands. “We need to go after Kiryu! I think he’s in danger!”
She was about to run off when Rena pulled on her arm. “Hang on, Kiryu just ran off without telling
us anything. What is he doing?”
“… He’s going to storm the Sonozaki Estate and meet with Mion, even if he has to take on the
whole Sonozaki Family.”

The Estate looked like a scene from a mafia movie. The police had attempted to surround it, but
were now in a stand-off with the yakuza blocking every entrance. Most of the cops were on edge,
but Ooishi sat in his car. He seemed almost carefree in contrast to the tense atmosphere. Perhaps
because he had dreamed of this day many times. In reality, it wasn’t that different from his
expectations.
He glanced at the mirror and saw someone. “Ah, here comes the Dragon.”
Hair sleeked back and a determined look in his eyes, he walked up the pathway. Ooishi got out of
his car to greet him. “Mr. Kazuma, I assume you’re here on business.”
Kiryu paid no attention to the sarcastic remark. “I’ll be going in alone. Only send in your guys after
a half-hour, if I don’t come back.”
Ooishi felt a slight chill. “That’s assuming there will be anything left for us to do once you’re
finished.”
Kiryu faced Ooishi with curiosity. “You seem suspiciously fine with a civilian interfering with
police business.”
Ooishi smirked and grabbed a cigar and his lighter. “A civilian yes, but last I checked there’s
nothing illegal about a dragon interfering,” he said, winking. “You’re helping us out, anyway.”
Kiryu nodded. As he approached, the yakuza on the other side got more and more anxious. They
dared not shoot at him in fear of the cops retaliating. The scene caused memories to flood back to
Kiryu.
It’s been almost five years since then. Every day that December, I was fighting for my life. Fighting
to find out the truth. And here I am now doing the same thing. Kiryu smirked to himself. I guess
I’ve grown soft being a civvy. I don’t remember it being this scary. And to think they’re the ones
terrified of me. … Alright, let’s do this.
With a roar, Kiryu ran full force towards the Sonozaki Family. None of them even had time to react,
before a few had a fist right in their face. One behind Kiryu tried to land a punch, but he dodged
with ease and landed a counter hook right to the cheek. Another charged him with a knife, but he
dodged, grabbed the arm, and kneed it cracking the bone. Overcome with pain, he dropped the
knife only for Kiryu to land a clean knockout punch.
The police were in awe at what they were watching. One man was taking on multiple yakuza at
once, without even breaking a sweat. “Who the hell is this guy?” One of the cops asked Ooishi.
Ooishi wore a smile enjoying the show before him. “That is a man, who is an expert in mixed
martial arts, boxing, karate, grappling, street fighting, and brute strength all at once. Though, really
I don’t think there’s a name for his fighting style. Perhaps you could call it custom-made. Just be
glad we’re not on the receiving end of those punches. Poor bastards.”
A few minutes had passed, and a dozen yakuza were on the ground groaning in pain. The main
entrance to the Estate was sealed off. Kiryu sighed. Where the hell can I get in?! Is there maybe a
spot where I can climb over the wall on the side?
Kiryu ran across the wall looking for any entrance. He eventually was on the left side of the Estate.
Two yakuza with katana attempted to ambush him from the bushes. Kiryu barely dodged the slice

of one, as it grazed his cheek. He blocked both of the attacks with his gauntlets and kicked one of
the grunts in the groin. The other was still in shock his attack had been blocked, and he couldn’t
react when Kiryu grabbed him by the collar and slammed him face-first into the wall. He broke the
leg of the one on the ground by stomping on it just to be safe.
It was then he spotted a police car parked next to the wall. The cops inside were bewildered at the
scene before them. An idea struck Kiryu. Nearly shitting themselves, Kiryu rushed towards the
cops’ car. He jumped on top and used the elevated height to climb over the wall. He was now
inside, much to the panic of those nearby on patrol.
“Who the fuck are you?!” One of them cried out. Kiryu stared forward, ignoring the question. “If
you don’t want to get hurt, get out of my way.” Of course, they ignored this as well and rushed him.
There was a massive log nearby, and Kiryu quickly grabbed it. Before they knew what hit them, he
swung at the five, knocking them away. He dropped the log and advanced.
~~~~
Deep underground in the ritual storehouse, the sisters were sitting somberly. Neither of them knew
what to say to the other, nor could they fix anything. Suddenly, one of the Sonozaki grunts ran in.
“Ms. Sonozaki! The Dragon is outside with the police! They found out it was a fake body! What
are your orders?!”
Mion froze. “The… Dragon?”
“Yes, Kiryu Kazuma! He hasn’t engaged us yet, but we are positive he will try to get inside! What
should we do?!”
Shion was shocked to hear Kiryu’s name. As in Mr. Kiryu?! Our teacher?! What is he doing here?!
Thoughts raced through Mion’s mind. How the hell did they find out it was a fake? Was it Rika?
And Kiryu is here?! Oh God, he’s here! What am I doing? I have to do something. I have to do
something! I have to… No, it doesn’t matter who it is. I can’t just freeze up like before. My family is being attacked. I
need to take action, and not shut down. She repeated those thoughts over and over, getting rid of
anything that wasn’t being the Heir.
“Ms. Sonozaki, please! We need-”
“Silence!” Mion stood up with as much confidence as she had. “Gather everyone we have, and do
not let him in, no matter what. Relay the orders to everyone you can. I’ll go tell Granny what’s
going on.”
“Y-yes ma’am!” The grunt then quickly left. Mion was about to do so as well when Shion spoke
up. “Wait, Mion! That’s not OUR Kiryu, right?!”
Mion paused and gritted her teeth. She didn’t reply, but instead reached into her pocket. She
grabbed the key to Shion’s cell, and dropped it on the ground in front of the cell just far enough
away Shion couldn’t grab it. Mion looked at her sister with a miserable look. “Just please stay here
till someone gets you.”

And with that, Mion ran off. “Wait! Mion, come back! Sister!!” Her pleas fell on deaf ears. As
Mion ran towards her house, her only thoughts were about dealing with Kiryu. I have to protect the
Sonozaki Family no matter what! No matter what!!
~~~~
The Sonozaki Estate was divided into three areas vertically. The lowest hosts the entrance and some
gardens. A middle connecting the two with more gardens and decorative statues. Finally, there is
the top level with the mansion, ritual chamber, and a decently sized pond behind the house. Kiryu
was currently trying to get up the stairs and go up to the middle.
He saw a glint out of the corner of his eye, and quickly rolled and dodged. One of the grunts had a
gun, and had missed. Kiryu took cover behind a tree. Dammit, of course, they have guns! He took a
breath and ran with gunfire following him. He very quickly ran out of bullets. “F-fuck not now!”
Kiryu saw his chance and rushed the yakuza.
He was about to knock his lights out, when he saw another grunt not too far away also aiming at
him. He reacted accordingly, grabbed the grunt closest, pulled his arm behind his back near
breaking it, and put him in front of the path of the gun. “D-don’t shoot! Please!”
Not having expected a hostage situation, the grunt fumbled with his gun. Kiryu blitzed towards
him, his buddy still in the line of fire. With all his might, he threw the man towards the other,
knocking them both out.
He was about halfway up the stairs when he saw five grunts rushing him. He also noticed six more
were behind him, getting close. Kiryu was trapped. He clicked his tongue and ran up the stairs. He
football tackled the two in front, knocking them both into two behind. Kiryu then grabbed the fifth
and launched him towards the six pursuing him from behind. They were already climbing up, only
to be blasted back down the stairs from their ally.
And with that, Kiryu rushed to the middle level.
~~~~
Mion was out of breath by the time she reached her house. She ran upstairs to see Oryou sitting
calmly. “Grandma, what are you doing?! Kiryu is going to storm this place!”
Oryou stared back, her expression unchanged. “I’m aware, Mion. I just heard over the radio he’s
entered the premises and will be here soon enough.”
Mion didn’t know what to say. Oryou chuckled to herself. “It’s funny, isn’t it? Man’s most foolish
belief is that we are born equals. It might be only every one in a million, but there are those born
above others. Regardless of them being good or evil, they change the world and their names go
down in history. That’s the type of man we’re dealing with now.”
Mion felt herself getting extremely flustered. “Grandma, this is no laughing matter! The Sonozakis
are going to be done for, if we don’t do something!”
“And what would you suggest we do at this point?”
“ … W-we can… um, I… you… “ Nothing came to mind.

“Mion, that man is a real yakuza. He doesn’t care who he’s up against. He’s the type that could
fight 100 men, and would still be more than able to fight 100 more. He fights for his beliefs, and to
protect his ideals and those close to him. Can you do the same, Mion?”
Once again, she found herself unable to come up with an answer. And it was a soul-crushing
realization. “I… I’m not sure who or what I believe in anymore.”
“… Believe in your pride as a yakuza, and believe in your friends.”
Mion was utterly perplexed. “W-what do you mean, Grandma?”
“You’ve always been stuck between being the heir to this Family and also just being a normal girl
who loves her friends and this community. At times, I’ve wondered if we have severely burdened
you, yet you always prove me wrong, forging your own path, and balancing the two. Maybe this is
the logical endpoint of that. A final trial you must overcome. What will you do?”
This was it. These were the words Mion needed to clear the fog. She seriously contemplated for a
few minutes her next actions. “I know what I’m going to do.”
~~~~
How many men had Kiryu dealt with at this point? 50? 70? 80? 100 even? They just never seemed
to stop coming. He had cleared the middle level and was about to reach the top one, though not
without injury. He had taken a few blows to the head, and was mildly bleeding. As he overcame the
final step, there in front of him was the house. He had expected a small army awaiting him, but
there was a single man instead. He was tall, wore sunglasses, and was brandishing a shotgun.
“I’m afraid you stop here, Kiryu Kazuma.” He was aiming right at Kiryu. There was a solid twenty
feet between the two. Certainly not short enough for Kiryu to close the distance without risk of a
fatal injury. They both stared at each other intensely.
“May I at least have your name?” Kiryu asked.
“What’s it to you?”
“It just seems unfair you know mine, but I have no clue who you are.”
“… Kasai,” the man said after a long pause.
A flash of recognition played in Kiryu’s eyes. Oh, so this is Shion’s bodyguard. He certainly fits the
bill. “Can I possibly convince you to move aside, Kasai? I’d like to talk with your boss.”
“Afraid I can’t do that. You’ve already beaten the shit out of almost the whole family. Someone has
to stop you. It’s not too late for you to leave. I can’t say the Family won’t try to kill you afterward,
but you can always skip town. You got that lovely Kamurocho to return too.”
Kiryu stayed silent for a few seconds. He took one step forwards, causing Kasai to tense. “Y’know,
I can’t exactly do warning shots with this. Don’t get any closer, or you will regret it.”
“Is this really what you want to do, Kasai? I don’t think this would make Shion happy.”
This caused Kasai to waver slightly. In that time, Kiryu took another step, but Kasai was instantly
ready again to shoot his innards out. “It’s orders from the Boss. Can’t say I want to do this either,

but I have my duty to protect the Family. A worse man than me would’ve filled you with holes by
now.”
“I know, and I’m grateful for your restraint so far.” A lethal silence entered. Shit, where do I go
from here? “Do you know where Shion is right now?”
“… She’s fine.”
“She’s one of my students, so I have a responsibility to watch out for her. So is Mion… and
Satoko.”
A visible bead of sweat appeared on Kasai’s forehead. Kiryu took another step. “Ask yourself, are
you really doing the right thing?” Yet another step taken. Kasai had not let go of the shotgun. He
very well could murder Kiryu with one push of the trigger. And yet, he found himself hesitating.
“I’m protecting the Family! You think you can just barge in here and do whatever you want?!”
Kiryu ignored him, and closed the distance a little more. “Are you going to abandon those closest
to you just for the sake of following orders? There’s loyalty, and then there’s foolishness. At the
end of all of this, are you even going to be able to look Shion in the eyes? How would she feel
knowing you helped in covering up the death of the girl she loved like a sister?”
And at that, Kasai finally felt defeated. He finally lowered the shotgun. “Go, Shion is in the ritual
storehouse,” he said softly under his breath.
Kiryu was planning to have rushed him as soon as he had a chance, but it seemed he wouldn’t have
to fight after all. “… Thank you.”
No sooner had the two met, did they part. Kasai looked up in the sky. It looked like it would start
raining any minute now. Dammit, I really have gotten soft.

Kiryu stormed into the ritual storehouse. Calling it creepy would be an understatement. It was dark,
but there was enough light to see a cell in the corner. In it was a familiar girl. “Kiryu, is that you?!”
“Yes! I’ve come to rescue you.”
“W-wait, you really are Kiryu, right?”
“Yeah, don’t you recognize me?”
Shion stared blankly. “I just would have never guessed you’d be able to take on my whole Family.
How fucking strong are you?”
“… Language, Shion,” he said as he searched around for the key.
“It’s right on the ground in front of you!” She said, pointing at it.
Indeed, the key was right there. Kiryu wasn’t sure how or why, but he wasn’t about to question it.
He unlocked the cage, and Shion scrambled out free from her confines.

“I’m so glad you’re saf- oof!” Kiryu was interrupted by Shion nearly tackling him. She embraced
him, as tears began to form. Kiryu hugged her back. “Thank God, you’re ok.”
“Kiryu, please! You have to save, Sis. She’s… she’s about to do something dangerous. Please, it
was an accident! She didn’t do anything wrong. It just…”
Her voice trailed off, but Kiryu understood what she meant. “I… I want to talk to Mion. It’s not that
I don’t trust you, but I want to hear what she has to say. I want to let her know she’s not alone.”
Shion let go of Kiryu. “I don’t know what she’ll do, but please don’t hurt her.”
“I’ll try my best. Whatever happens next, I’ll make sure she’s ok.”
The two left the storehouse, and made the short trek over to the Estate. Kiryu carefully opened the
front door, with Shion following from a distance. She looked behind to see dozens of grunts lying
unconscious. It looked like it had literally rained men. “You… didn’t kill any of them, right?”
“No, but I hope you guys have good health insurance.”
Kiryu peeked inside. There was no one to be found. It almost seemed abandoned. He entered into
the main dining area, only to be greeted with an unusual sight. Oryou was sitting, drinking a cup of
tea. She wasn’t fazed at all by Kiryu’s arrival. “Welcome to my home, Kiryu Kazuma. Or at least
what’s left of it,” she said, bitterly laughing.
Kiryu didn’t know how to react. Even in this situation, she’s exceptionally calm. Did she expect this
would happen?
She sat down her tea on the table in front of her. “Come, have a seat. I imagine, you have many
questions. You’ve certainly earned the right. Or maybe you’re here to punch me, too? Beat me up
till you're satisfied? That seems to be how you operate.”
Kiryu ignored her taunts. “Where’s Mion Sonozaki at?”
“… She’s in the back waiting for you. Don’t keep her waiting. And Shion, you’re awful at hiding
yourself. Get out from there instantly!”
Shion had been hiding behind a wall, but her grandma knew better. She reluctantly entered the
room. Her expression was full of contempt. “Nice to see you again, hag.”
“The feeling is mutual.”
Kiryu hesitated for a second. Oryou looked at him like he was an idiot. “I said, don’t keep her
waiting! The whole Estate is surrounded by police, and you’ve already beaten up everyone for
them! I’ll cut you down if you stay here one moment longer!”
Kiryu took the hint, and left immediately. Oryou sighed, and looked at her granddaughter. “Well,
shouldn’t you be leaving with him?”
“You’re being awful easygoing about this, hag. The Oryou I know would have cut him down as
soon as he entered the estate.”
She laughed, and faced away from Shion. “It’s simple really. … That man might be the only one,
who can ease her burden at this point.”

~~~~
Into the vast backyard of the Estate, Kiryu entered. Rain had stared to come down, and the sky was
a bleak gray. It took him a few moments, but he soon spotted a figure. A young girl with two katana
sheathed around her waist. She stared at Kiryu resolutely. “So you’ve come,” Mion stated.
Despite having gone through everything for this moment, Kiryu found himself unsure of what to
say. He had practiced a few things in his head, and yet what should he say to his student? In the
end, he settled on a simple question. “Please, Mion, tell me what happened. I want to hear the truth
from you. What happened to Satoko?”
Mion didn’t reply. Instead, she took one of the katana out of its sheath. Not expecting Mion to
immediately resort to violence, he took a defensive stance. Unexpectedly, she threw it his way.
“Fight me, Kiryu Kazuma.”
Kiryu couldn’t believe what he was hearing. “M-Mion this is ridiculous! I didn’t come here to fight
you. I just want to know the truth.”
“I said fight me!” Mion roared, ignoring Kiryu’s pleas. “Have you forgotten this is how the yakuza
works? You think you can just tear apart my men, and get away with it?! Even I have my pride.”
“I’m… I’m sorry, I did what I had to do. I didn’t kill any of them, but… yes, I beat up your men.”
“I have to avenge them. It’s my role as the Heir. If you truly want to know what happened, defeat
me Dragon of Dojima. Defeat me in a duel between yakuza!”
Kiryu gritted his teeth. As much as he wanted to avoid a fight, he’ll have to win vs. Mion without
hurting her. At least, as little as he could. “You don’t have to do this, Mion. You’re my student, and
my friend. I… I don’t want to hurt you.”
Mion’s eyes slightly wavered, but her determination returned just as quickly. “Pick up the katana, if
you value your life. If you don’t in the next few moments, I will cut you down.”
Kiryu could tell she was serious. A massive, deep green aura surrounded her. With no remaining
options, Kiryu finally picked up the katana. “If I win Mion, you will tell me everything.”
“As I said. And if you lose, you must leave and never return to this place. You must also tell the
police you were mistaken, and the corpse found was the real one.”
Kiryu nodded, acknowledging the lethal deal. Mion took a deep breath in and out. “Come at me,
Kiryu Kazuma!!!”

Chapter 32: Demon's Tears Arc FINALE: The End of Denial
Chapter Notes

I would suggest listening to Ishin final boss theme for this fight. That was at least what I was
listening to while writing this: https://www.youtube.com/watch?
v=3AKRhnrpWKg&pp=ygUdeWFrdXphIGlzaGluIGZpbmFsIGJvc3MgdGhlbWU%3D

See the end of the chapter for more notes

Lightning scattered across the sky. Beneath the storm had gathered two warriors. Both wishing it
hadn’t come to this. Shion stared from the window in awe. “What the hell is Sis doing?! Is she
trying to get herself killed?!”
Oryou signalled for her to not interfere. “Do not insult your sister’s pride. I would worry more
about the Dragon.”
Shion looked at her like she was crazy, but upon a closer look, Kiryu was the one sweating. Is he…
actually scared?
The two were circling each other. Kiryu tried to keep his breaths steady, while Mion seemed calm
and unperturbed. The dynamic was not one of an adult fighting a child, but two samurai engaged in
a duel.
Though, Kiryu himself knew he was hardly a samurai. She’s far better at wielding a katana than I
am. She’s no master, but whatever amateur experience I have is nothing compared to her. How do I
approach this without losing, or hurting her?
Kiryu didn’t have time to think. Mion finally made a move. She approached unexpectedly quick,
and used a downwards chop. Kiryu blocked it in time, but it had clearly shaken him. He took a step
back, but Mion dared not let him retreat. A horizontal slash, a diagonal, a stab, and finally another
downwards chop with even more strength behind it than the first.
Shion was in awe. “Since when was Sis so…”
“Strong?” Oryou filled in. “She’s one of the strongest people in this town. Not perhaps in physical
strength, but she is the Heir for a reason. I am proud to have her as my granddaughter.”
Shion knew similar feelings didn’t extend to herself, but she couldn’t deny Mion’s strength. She
wasn’t born this way. I know better than anyone else how far she’s come.
Meanwhile, Kiryu was struggling to block all of Mion’s attacks. And yet, Mion was getting
flustered that she hadn’t even landed a clean hit in yet. Is this the gap that separates us?! I’m giving
it my all and I clearly have the advantage. So how is he blocking me so well?! Is it just more
experience?
Mion’s eyes sharpened. She went for a feint on Kiryu’s left. Kiryu anticipated it, only for Mion to
deliver a low kick to his knee. He buckled for a second, and Mion landed a hit on Kiryu’s right

shoulder.
He had managed to avoid it somewhat, but the cut was there nonetheless. Kiryu winced in pain.
The only silver lining, is that it wasn’t too deep. Unfortunately, Mion wouldn’t let him rest for a
second. The onslaught continued.
Shion covered her mouth. “Sis isn’t… actually trying to kill him, right?”
“Something like that won’t kill him. One wrong move and Mion will lose.”
The battle continued. Sparks flew and the sounds of metal clashing filled the air. Kiryu had been
fighting purely defensively at this point, but now even he was looking for some sort of counter
now. He didn’t want to hurt Mion at all. However, this was not a situation where he could just
overpower her. At the least, he needed to do something to disarm her.
An idea came to mind. He put all of his strength into a downwards chop. Mion blocked it, but it
was the heaviest attack from Kiryu yet. Her nerves ached from the impact, and she was caught off
guard by Kiryu following up with a sweep. She panicked as she lost her footing and fell backwards.
Kiryu was hoping she’d drop the katana, or that he could at least kick it away after she fell. Mion
was one step ahead. She grasped some mud and threw it at Kiryu’s eyes. It landed, and Kiryu
immediately retreated, being taken by surprise. He quickly stepped back, wiping the mud away
with his sleeves. Except, Mion was no longer there. Instinctually, he held his blade behind his back
to block a sneak attack from Mion.
She gritted her teeth and backed off. The two were now back to a neutral state. They began to circle
each other again. A minute passed with no advance from either of them. The tension was lethally
high. Kiryu’s stamina had been worn thin, and the pressure was starting to get to him. Mion’s
composure was shaky as well, but she sensed Kiryu’s hesitation.
Mion rushed Kiryu and the two clash. To Kiryu’s surprise, Mion immediately grabbed his arm
afterward. In one swift motion, she put him in an arm lock, causing him to let go of the katana, and
throw it behind him. She let go, and rushed for the katana before Kiryu could stop her. Despite all
odds, Kiryu had been the one disarmed.
Shion’s mouth was agape. “What the hell did Sis just do?” Oryou smirked. “It’s not a traditional
way of disarming someone, but it works well in conjunction with her aikido.”
Dual katana in Mion’s hand, and nothing for Kiryu but bare fists and the gauntlets on his arms for
protection. Mion gave a nervous smile at her supposed victory. “You’ve lost, Kiryu.”
Kiryu didn’t reply. He simply entered his natural fighting stance. If anything, he looked more
confident without a katana. “I fought over 100 men to get here with all sorts of weapons, including
guns. What makes you think I’ll stop now?”
For the first time, Mion went pale. The atmosphere had completely changed. Shion looked at Kiryu
like he was crazy, and in some ways he was. “There’s no way he can actually win now, right?”
Oryou looked on with her usual unreadable expression. “The Dragon is possibly more dangerous
unarmed than armed. Like I said, one wrong move.”
Mion’s heart was racing. She attempted to rationally think through her predicament. He should only
have protection on his arms from the gauntlets, anywhere else should be a free strike. She gathered

her resolve, and made the first move. Two slashes were made. One aimed for Kiryu’s right arm, and
the other aiming for a stab to the chest.
A rather awkward attack for Kiryu to block at this point. Kiryu had special training, though. He
didn’t just relax after leaving the yakuza, he had trained under a master in his spare time. A man
named Sotaro Komaki. He had not learned all the man’s techniques, but at least one would come in
handy here.
With a roar, he used the Komaki Parry with all his strength. It was a simple, but effect move. He
swung his right arm upwards at an angle to knock back the blade. The sheer power caught Mion off
guard, and she took a step back, being unable to follow through on the second slash.
It was a bold and dangerous move, but Kiryu bet it all on this. He tackled Mion, and they both fell
to the ground. Mion had the wind knocked out of her, and sure enough, Kiryu was above her in the
mount position. She had managed to hang on to the swords, but Kiryu held down her forearms. No
amount of aikido knowledge, katana training, or even ground grappling knowledge would get her
out of this.
Just like that, the tables had turned. Mion desperately fought on the ground to get any sort of
strength or release from his hold, but Kiryu had a solid 100 pounds over her and was not about to
let her do anything. Kiryu looked apologetically at her that it had had to come to this. “Mion,
please. Let go of the katana. It’s over.”
She did not reply. Rather, she thrashed about violently, looking for anything she could do. “This
was a fight between yakuza, Mion. I won, and you lost. I took on your whole family, and won.
Please, just tell me the truth of what happened between you and Satoko.”
At that, all of Mion’s strength left. The katana dropped from her hands. She closed her eyes, unable
to bear Kiryu’s gaze. “You wouldn’t believe me even if I told you the truth. My family and I are
nothing but demons that have brought suffering to the Hojos.”
Kiryu got off of her. She opened her eyes in surprise to see him lifting her up, and putting her down
standing. And with that, he did what he had been wanting to do from the beginning. He embraced
her tightly. “Neither you nor anyone in your family is a demon. You are my student, and my friend.
You were a poor girl alone and suffering, and I was not able to recognize it. And for that, I am
sorry. Please forgive your foolish teacher for being unable to help you, when you desperately
needed it.”
Mion was limp in Kiryu’s arms. It felt like time had stopped for her. Gradually, tears began to form.
A slight whimper eventually transformed into bawling. She cried and cried into Kiryu’s chest as
she let her soul weep. Everything she had restrained and kept hidden poured out. Kiryu continued
to hug her, at least till she was ready to let go.
Shion felt like she was dreaming. But it was a wonderful dream. One that she couldn’t believe was
reality. Before she could speak up, she heard a ruckus behind her. Rika, the club members, and
Ooishi along with some cops had stormed the place. “Put your hands up!” One of the cops yelled.
Oryou put a finger to her mouth, shushing him. The cop was confused till he looked past her to see
Kiryu and Mion. The scene spoke for itself. Even the rain had started to slow down, and the sun
was beginning to shine through. No one knew how to really react, except for Rika. She breathed a
sigh of relief, and almost fell to her knees. Keiichi and Rena thankfully noticed, and caught her.
“Woah, Rika!” Keiichi yelled. “Are you ok?” Rena asked.

Rika had a soft smile on her face. “I’m fine. I’m just… so happy they’re ok.”
“Mmm, I wouldn’t call Kiryu fine. His shoulder is bleeding,” Ooishi said, pointing. Upon closer
inspection, the group realized his suit was stained red and cut open. The kids wanted to rush over,
but Ooishi held up his hand. “Just wait a few minutes first, kids.”
Three police officers approached the two. None of the three exactly wanted to interrupt the scene,
but they had a job to do. Kiryu looked up, and gave a nod. He let go of Mion. She had finished
crying. Her expression a strange mix of relief and shame. She took a deep breath in and out.
“Please bring my friends here. They deserve to know the truth.”
The three officers briefly discussed among themselves deciding what to do. They eventually
decided to signal everyone to come over. A small crowd had formed around Mion at this point. She
looked down at the ground, unable to look anyone in the eye. Her mind recited the words Kiryu had
whispered to her before letting her go. “Please trust in your friends.”
She looked up at everyone, mustering up as much courage as she could. Regardless of who judged
her or why, she was going to reveal everything. “I will state nothing but the honest facts and what
my intentions were. I had just finished a wonderful day with my friends, and had invited Satoko
over for a sleep-over. It was the first time I had ever done such a thing with her, and I wanted it to
be special. We played some tag inside. She started going a little too fast, and…”
Mion found herself choking back more tears. She took a second to breathe. “She got going too fast,
and fell down the stairs. She fell and… died.” The silence was deafening. No one knew how to
react. “Knowing the rumors about my family and our history, I didn’t expect anyone to believe it
was an accident. Being the Heir, I had the power and resources to create a body double and create a
false narrative that we had both been sick over the weekend, and that she had died yesterday up on
the hill she usually plays on. It was a desperate, foolish endeavor to try and protect my family.”
She began to start tearing up. “To create a false reality that it was a tragic accident that had nothing
to do with me. That it wasn’t my fault Satoko was dead.” She put her hands on her face, unable to
continue looking on. “She’s suffered for so long, and it was already partially my family’s fault. I
just wanted to make her happy. I loved her so much, and just wanted the best for her. She never
deserved anything like this. I-”
Rika embraced Mion, cutting her off. “It wasn’t your fault, Mion.” Mion looked down at Rika in
surprise. “It wasn’t anyone’s fault. It was just a bad roll of the dice.” She teared up, holding Mion
tighter. “Neither you nor Satoko deserved to deal with this.”
Rena would hug Mion next. “Mii, you’re the strongest and kindest person I know. You sometimes
make mistakes, and you might’ve made a bad one here. But I know you’re not a bad person.
Whatever happens next, we’ll be there for you.”
Keiichi approached slowly, tearing up himself. His and Mion’s eyes met, and she looked away.
How could she face the person she had lied to that she also was in love with. And yet, he too
embraced her. “Look, Mion. I’ve not known you for too long. It does hurt that you lied to me over
something so serious, but I can understand where you were coming from. I don’t know your family
history well, or how you live as a yakuza. But I know you’re not the type to ever hurt someone, if
you can prevent it. You didn’t know me, and yet you treated me like we’ve always known each
other. You welcomed and introduced me to your friends, and even the club. Because of you, I have
a place in this town and have been able to create some wonderful memories so far. So even if

you’ve done some bad stuff, I get that it was a complex situation. And I… I still want to be your
close friend.”
Mion couldn’t believe the words she was hearing from everyone. Her emotions began to
overwhelm her, as the three comforted her. “I’m sorry. I’m so sorry. I never should have let it get
this far.”
“Yeah, you shouldn’t have.” The four looked up to see Shion approach. Her expression was stern
and clearly upset. Mion looked down. Even if her friends could forgive her, her own sister was the
person that was most effected by this, besides Rika. She was suddenly slapped harshly by Shion on
her cheek. Rika, Rena, and Keiichi wanted to say something, but it wasn’t really their place. Mion
just stood there, afraid to look Shion in the eye.
“You absolute fucking idiot,” Shion continued. “Why didn’t you trust in your friends to
understand? Why couldn’t you trust in your own sister to understand?!” Mion looked up, to see
Shion start to tear up. “I’m sorry that I assumed the worst when I stormed into here, but I just
wished you had told me the truth from the beginning. As much as I loved and cared for Satoko, it
was the least you could do!”
Mion struggled to find any words. “I-I’m sorr-”
“Don’t apologize!” Shion said, pointing right in Mion’s face. “I know damn well how sorry you
are. Realistically, this will haunt you for the rest of your life… even if it wasn’t actually your fault.
I don’t blame you for that. Just promise me you’ll never do it again. And over time, I… eventually
want to be able to forgive you for this.”
Mion remained silent. She could only nod her head yes. “As for Satoko, …” her voice trailed off.
Everyone was still in denial it had even happened, much less everything else with Mion. “I think
we all need to take some time and sort out our feelings and grieve. As for you, well… “
Feeling the time was right, Ooishi finally approached. He had an uncharacteristically
understanding, but still solemn look. “For years, I’ve looked into your family. I’ve always wanted
to know the truth behind the Watanagashi murders, and yet when faced with one of you actually
being responsible…” He didn’t finish his sentence, but began to chuckle to himself bitterly. “How
could anyone accuse the Heir of being responsible for four years of death, when she acts like this
over just this one accidental death. Demon, my ass.”
No one, much less Mion knew how to react. She just continued listening to Ooishi. “That being
said, Ms. Sonozaki, you’ve still broken the law even if you’re not a murderer. You and your family
were responsible for hiding the body, and making a fake corpse. All at the age of 14. Can’t say I’ve
ever seen something like this in all my years, so I suppose congrats on showing an old dog some
new tricks,” he said mockingly.
Mion hung her head in shame. No amount of the best friends she could ask for could save her from
the law. She may be a minor, but it wouldn’t be the first time she had been jailed. “Even if I now
myself believe you are not fundamentally capable of murder, we’ll have to go to trial for this.
That’s not even mentioning what else your family could be connected to. If nothing else, I still
suspect some in your family being responsible for the Watanagashi murders,” he said, looking at
Oryou.
Oryou only gave back a bitter smile. “Don’t worry, Ooishi. I’m free to chat later. We can have a
long talk.” Ooishi was unamused, cursing the old hag underneath is breath. “As for all your yakuza

buddies beaten half to death, several ambulances will be here shortly,” he said, looking at Kiryu
with a mix of respect for his capabilities and annoyance that he had single-handedly beaten his
archenemy.
Kiryu avoided eye contact, acknowledging he had made one hell of a scene. I suppose I had
forgotten I’m out of the ordinary when it comes to feats like this. Thinking about it, I did leave a lot
of messes behind me back in 78.
Mion held out her hands. She looked at Ooishi with the little remaining pride as a yakuza she had
left. “I Mion Sonozaki, the heir to the Sonozaki Family, will turn myself in for my crimes.” She
was handcuffed by two police officers, and was about to be led away. She then asked, “Can I please
say some parting words to my friends before I go.” The officers looked at each other, and then both
nodded to her. She turned around to face them all.
She saw a mix of expressions on everyone’s faces. Shion still looked flustered, but she attempted to
give a smile back. The rest also smiled as best they could, considering the circumstances. Mion
didn’t force her smile, but rather it was a genuine one. One accompanied by tears of joy. “Shion
wouldn’t want me to apologize again, so I’ll just say I’ll do whatever it takes to make up for this.
And to all of you, and especially Kiryu… thank you for still wanting to be my friends!” She bowed
as much as she could, handcuffed. “I don’t deserve your forgiveness, but I’ll repay it no matter
what. I swear it!”
And with that, a long day came to a close

Three weeks had passed. The news hit Japan like a truck. The police found and recovered Satoko’s
body in a morgue in Okinomiya owned by one of the Sonozakis. Kiryu in particular was
interviewed heavily for his accomplishment of taking on the whole Sonozaki Family and winning.
A young, rich CEO doing something like it was way too good to pass up for the gluttonous media.
Kiryu hated being the center of attention, but he wouldn’t waste the opportunity. He heavily put
emphasis on it being the mistake of a loss child. That while she had messed up, he pleaded for
people to not harass her and to understand where she was coming from. However, he wasn’t able to
protect her Family as well.
An intensive investigation was done into the Sonozaki household and the Family members in
general. It came to light the Sonozakis were responsible for smuggling several weapons and drugs.
Some murders of small time criminals were also found to be related, but strangely there was
nothing to be found definitively for the Watanagashi Murders or even the 2 Tojo yakuza. Many
were also in high positions in society, and their credibility came into question. To say their
reputation was ruined was an understatement.
Stories about Mion varied. Through Kiryu’s efforts, many painted her as a child stuck between a
heritage full of criminals and her role in it, and also just wanting to be a normal girl. Some others
were more malicious, implying Kiryu was just trying to defend his student, and that she was as sick
as the rest of her family. A few even managed to dig up Kiryu’s past as a yakuza, and questioned
his motives.
On some level though, Kiryu’s passion and honesty got through to the general people of Japan.
Even when confronted with his past and his business being severely effected by these revelations,
he did not deny them. He rather admitted to them, and fervently asked that people forgive Mion, or
if not forgive, at least understand her heart and why she chose her actions.

As for Mion herself, she was currently in a jail cell in Okinomiya. Due to her young age and the
complicated matters of the case, how long her time would be was still being discussed. A trial was
coming up soon to decide. Kiryu had visited her regularly. He had brought Rika, Keiichi, and Rena
each once. Of course, they had limited talk time, so they made the most of it trying to cheer up
Mion and catching her up on stuff. Though, they tried to avoid talking about anything negative
from the media or the state of her family.
It was evening today. Kiryu had come for the tenth time in the last 3 weeks. A police officer walked
Mion out into the room. A glass screen separating the two. “You have 15 minutes,” the officer dryly
said.
Leaving the two alone, he exited the room. Kiryu smiled at her, and Mion sheepishly smiled back.
She was a bit disappointed none of her friends were with him, but just getting to see him was
privilege enough. “Wow, what is it? The tenth time you’ve visited me?”
“I’ve not really been keeping count, but something like that. Are you doing, ok?”
“As ‘ok’ as I can be in an old, dingy jail cell. But yes, I’m… I’m fine.”
“I know we don’t have a lot of time, so if you have anything you want to say or ask, please do.”
Mion contemplated for a few seconds. “Have my friends said anything about me? How are they
handling… Satoko?”
Kiryu considered how to best answer. “They’re handling it as best as they can. I don’t think it really
hit them all at once on that day, but they’ve been grieving and dealing with it, each in their own
way. Rena and Keiichi regularly worry about you, and well, you saw how excited they were to visit
you. Rika is at peace with it, I think. She’s… handled it better than I thought she would.”
In truth, Kiryu wasn’t entirely sure how Rika was feeling about it. Things were in a strange state of
limbo. Takano was dead, there was no war with the Tojo, her town wasn’t being destroyed, her
friends were alive except for… Satoko. He had tried to talk to her about it a few times, but she just
kept saying she’d like to talk about it in the near future. At first, they thought Mion was the one that
had the Syndrome in this loop, but even that turned out to be inaccurate once Kiryu confronted her.
Perhaps it was Takano or someone else, but they really had no clue.
“You don’t have to lie to me, Kiryu. I know Rika is probably taking it the worst out of anyone
besides Shion.” She looked down at the ground with glazed over eyes. Kiryu hated seeing her with
those eyes. It was the same he himself had for a while after Tachibana was killed. “You’re not still
blaming yourself for Satoko’s death, right?”
The question pierced her, but she understood Kiryu’s concern. “Less than I was before. I know you
always say to forgive myself of it, but it… it’s going to take some time. I’m sorry.”
“You’re already carrying a large burden, Mion. Don’t make it any heavier than you have to.”
Mion smiled. “Thank you, I’ll try. I really don’t know where I’d be right now without you.”
Kiryu smiled back. “Of course, what are friends for?”
Mion’s smile faded. “Seriously, I don’t know if I’d still be here.”

The mood changed swiftly. Kiryu shifted to a stern, but concerned gaze. “Mion you’re not still
having thoughts like that, I hope.”
Mion frantically waved her hands. “No! No! I’m… I’m fine now. I wouldn’t do that now after
everything. It’s just… you know where I was mentally.”
“I understand. I just want to make sure you’re ok now… relatively speaking.”
“Kiryu, do you remember when we were fighting?”
“How could I forget?” He said, rubbing his shoulder. “It’s healed by now, but damn it hurt.”
“I’m so sorry I never apologized about that till you visited me. A lot just… happened.”
“It’s fine. What about us fighting?”
Mion hesitated to continue. “On some level, I think I wanted you to kill me. I could make some
awful excuses for literally trying to kill you, but the truth is just I thought if I was serious enough,
maybe you’d… you’d do it for me, even if it was an accident. I didn’t have the courage to do it
myself.”
Kiryu leaned back in his chair and sighed. “Yeah, that would have been pretty bad.”
“I don’t know what the hell I was thinking. Even then, I was being so selfish.” She covered her face
in shame. “I just don’t understand why you’re being so nice to me even now. I nearly forced you to
kill me or be killed. I get that you’re my friend and my teacher, but don’t you have a limit?”
Kiryu crossed his arms. “You’re wrong on a few things. I never felt in danger fighting you. Going
through all you men was one thing, but I was confident I’d be fine once I got to you. It was just a
rather stressful matter of disarming you without hurting you. Sure, my shoulder got a nasty gash,
but it didn’t matter if I could just win.”
Mion remained silent and nodded. “The other thing is that you’re extremely straightforward as a
person. No offense, but you suck at lying or hiding your feelings. Even in my first few days here, it
was pretty obvious you had a thing for Keiichi. And no, I haven’t told anyone that, much less
Keiichi.”
Mion blushed. “D-did you really have to use that as an example?”
Kiryu stifled a chuckle. “Sorry, my point is just I understood what you were dealing with. I have
lost people close to me before. A man who was my only friend in a time of dire need was murdered
by other yakuza. I nearly murdered the man responsible, and I would have had my sworn brother
not intervened and saved me from going down that path. He saved my future, and I wanted to save
yours, even if it meant risking my life.”
Mion wasn’t sure how to reply. “Do I still have a future?”
Kiryu put his hand on the glass. “You can always restart from the ground up, and change your life
for the better. It won’t be easy, and it may take a long time. That said, you’re still young. Not even
an adult yet. You can forge your own path, and in some ways it… might be for the best you are no
longer the Heir. Ex-yakuza to new ex-yakuza, the civvy life ain’t that bad.”

Mion felt herself getting emotional, and wiped away a tear. She had a bittersweet smile. “Thank
you, Kiryu. I’ll keep that in mind. Before you have to go, is Shion doing ok?”
“She still hasn’t visited you?”
“No, but… can you blame her?”
“... No, I suppose I can’t. She’s stayed distant, but I think she’s doing better. I’m positive she’ll
come visit you soon, she’s just trying to process it all. Give her some time, I promise you she’s still
your sister, and she loves you.”
“Time is up,” the officer said.
Mion got up, and said one last thing to Kiryu. “I know I’ve said it a million times, but thank you for
everything.”
Kiryu nodded, seeing her off with a smile.
As Kiryu left, he took a deep breath. Right, let’s go talk to Rika now.
~~~~
It was about 4 p.m. The higurashi sang their familiar song, but it wasn’t really a comfort to Kiryu.
In some ways, he had been procrastinating on this talk as well. But enough was enough, he needed
to confront Rika about it. He knocked on her door. Hanyuu appeared. Half of her body was peeking
out from the second floor. “Oh, Kiryu! What are you doing here?”
“Just checking up on Rika, and… we need to talk.”
Hanyuu’s expression became serious. She nodded, and disappeared. Less than a minute later, Rika
opened the door. “Oh, Kiryu. Come on in, please.”
Kiryu nodded and entered the house. It wasn’t the first time he had entered it, but it was still only
the third. They had been using Hanyuu as a messenger, so it still felt a little weird to privately talk
like this. “How is Mion?” Rika asked.
“She’s hanging in there. We had a really good talk today. Gave her some good advice, encouraged
her, etc. Just doing the most I can do for her.”
Rika smiled. “I’m happy to hear that.”
“Anyway, I wanted to… talk to you about… “ A strange smell entered his nose. His gaze wandered
to a nearby bin with some empty wine bottles in them. He looked back at Rika with a mix of
confusion and mild disgust. “Are you… are you drinking?”
Rika made an audible squeak. In truth, she hadn’t told Kiryu EVERYTHING about herself. Shit, I
forgot to clean those up. She averted her gaze to Hanyuu. Dammit, Hanyuu! Why didn’t you warn
me?!
Hanyuu looked at Rika with an unamused expression. Because I’m tired of feeling like a filthy
drunk! You’ve downed 15 bottles within the last 3 weeks!! Takano may not have killed you this loop,
but the alcohol will!

She scowled at Hanyuu. “Traitor,” she whispered under her breath. She hesitantly looked back at
Kiryu. He had a mildly judgmental frown. Rika rolled her eyes. “Don’t judge me, you drink too.”
“Sure, but not that much. And-”
“And what?” Rika interrupted. “I am over four times older than you, don’t act like I can’t drink.”
“I get that, but… that can’t be healthy for an 11-year-old.”
Rika put her chin on the table and pouted. “Both you and Hanyuu act like a couple of annoying
parents.”
Both Kiryu and Hanyuu sighed. He then sat down across from Rika. “Regardless of the alcohol, we
need to have a serious talk. … Actually, maybe especially because of the alcohol. I had my
concerns, but that confirms it for me. Forgive my language, but you’re a fucking wreck.”
Not even a hint of sugarcoating. With everything out in the air, Rika decided to be blunt too. “I
know! I know, ok. I got everything I could ask for in this world, except my best friend is dead!
Every time the truth hits me, it feels like a hot knife in my soul! But at the same time, if we go to a
new fragment, I have to start over from the very beginning with even less time! We both also have
to kill ourselves to even do that, leaving behind a pair of corpses, which will absolutely traumatize
everyone for fucking life!!”
Rika held her head with both hands, a familiar headache returning. Kiryu was a bit taken aback. He
figured it was bad, but not outright awful. “Do you… think you can eventually accept Satoko’s
death?”
The question didn’t sting Rika as much as it should have, if only because it had drilled her head
constantly. “I just… am I being too selfish? I wanted to save EVERYONE! Is that too much to ask?
Takano, I can maybe live with. I want to save her, but she might be the hardest of anyone to even
get through to, much less ‘save’. But just… not Satoko, please. Why did it have to be her?”
Her grasp on her head tightened, as she fought to hold back the tears. “Am I just doomed to be
miserable even in the luckiest loops?”
Kiryu carefully assessed what he would say next. “I can’t say the same thoughts haven’t occurred
to me. If we could somehow restart the loop without suicide, that would be ideal, but even then …
“
A grim silence filled the room. A minute or so passed before Hanyuu spoke up. “I may actually
have a way to do that.”
Both looked at her in shock. “The only reason I haven’t mentioned it yet, is because I wasn’t sure
for a long time if it would work. I’m still not positive now. Um, what I’m trying to say is that I’ve
restored a bit of my power, by regularly staying in the shrine these last three weeks. I’m just going
off a hunch here, but theoretically I could maybe transfer our souls to another fragment without
having to use suicide.”
It sounded unbelievable, but it would be a miracle, if true. “What would happen to the ‘us’ in this
world, if we did that?”

Hanyuu pondered for a few seconds. “From what I’ve observed, the Rika of each world is her own
alternate Rika until our Rika here possesses her. Our Rika here then seems to fuse with the other
Rika, and the other Rika gains the memories of the one possessing her. I’m sure you felt something
similar when you first arrived here, Kiryu.”
Kiryu tried to remember, but didn’t have much luck. “I don’t think I forgot, but it’s more like a
traumatic blur. Do you know what happens after the ‘possessor’ leaves?”
Hanyuu looked away. “Well, no. Rika always… dies before that. Again, I’m just saying it’s a
possible, but not even concrete option. Best case scenario, we leave and the versions of us here
retain their experiences in this world, losing the memories of the previous world and their
connection to higher realms. Worst case scenario, I… don’t know.”
Rika hadn’t said anything. She was seriously thinking about what to do.
“If you want, Rika, I can give you some time. We don’t have to do it immediately.”
A few seconds went by, and then Rika answered. “No, let’s do it tonight.”
Hanyuu was surprised. “A-are you sure? You don’t need to rush into this.”
“No, we need to do this. Despite my horrid history with luck, I’ve met and allied with Kiryu this
loop and didn’t even have any of my friends catch the Syndrome. If I don’t take any risks, I won’t
be able to claim the future I want. Though…” She turned to face Kiryu. “I don’t know if I really
have the final say here.”
Kiryu nodded. “No, I agree. Let’s take this chance while we have it. How do we do it, Hanyuu?”
Hanyuu took a deep breath, trying to calm her anxiety. “Like I said, I don’t have a sure-fire method,
but probably our best chances are to do it in the Shrine.”
Rika stood up. “If that’s the case, let’s head on over.” The other two nodded, and the trio left Rika’s
house.
~~~~
It was now about 4:20. The three were now in the shrine. For Rika and Hanyuu this was an
unorthodox place of comfort, but for Kiryu it was still a nightmarish torture chamber. “Are you ok,
Kiryu?” Rika asked. “Yeah,” he replied. “I’m just not the fondest of being here… “
Rika held back a giggle. “I suppose everyone has a fear, no matter how strong they are.”
Kiryu blushed. He was going to say Rika was the odd one out for liking this place, but he took a
look at Hanyuu and decided to be nice. “Let’s just get this done with.”
Hanyuu beckoned them to in front of the statue of Oyashiro. “This is where I feel the strongest.”
“Ok, how do we go about this?” Kiryu questioned.
Hanyuu thought about it briefly. “Put out one of your hands, palm up.” Both Kiryu and Rika
followed her instructions. Hanyuu put out both her hands and “touched” them. She closed her eyes
and began to chant in a language foreign to a human tongue. Not even Rika knew what she was
saying. She could only guess it was something like speaking in tongues.

The world begin to change around them. It stretched and turned. It became clearer, and yet blurred.
Everything was a visual cacophony that overwhelmed both Kiryu and Rika, but they dared not let
go. The color began to leave the world, and a blinding white light surrounded them. Before they
knew it, the world had faded away.

9:00 A.M. Kiryu opened his eyes to the sound of nature’s natural alarm clock. The higurashi singed
their serenade. It wasn’t as harsh a first awakening as last time, but he still panicked a bit. He got
out of his bed, checking his whole body. … I’m still in one piece. He looked at the calendar on his
nightstand. It was Wednesday. One day further than last time.
He tried to check the memories of this fragment’s Kiryu, but it was unexpectedly fuzzy. He went to
the bathroom, and looked in his mirror, just to double-check everything. Sure enough, it was the
Dragon in the flesh. Confirming his own condition and that he didn't want to be too late for school,
he quickly got dressed.
Kiryu was about to leave when he heard a knock at the door. Is that Rika? A trickle of sweat
dripped down his neck. He suddenly had a bad feeling about this. He walked down the stairs
silently. A knock came again, though this time considerably more impatient sounding. He heard a
muffled voice outside. He couldn’t make it out what it was saying, but it sounded aggressive.
Kiryu noiselessly grabbed a nearby kitchen knife. He slowly approached the door. He unlocked it,
and stepped to the side, hugging the wall. He figured the best time to take on whoever was behind
the door was to wait for them to force their way in and backstab them. Seconds passed, the tension
in the air palpable. Kiryu had no idea what was happening, but he was not about to be caught off
guard.
Suddenly, the door was kicked open. “What’s the fucking hold u-” Kiryu lunged with his knife, and
stopped a few inches from the intruder’s face. Half because it was someone he recognized, … and
half because he also had a knife a few inches from his neck. “Majima?!” Kiryu yelled in surprise.
Majima gave a crude grin, and put his knife away. “And here I was worried you’d gone soft,
Kazzy.”
Kiryu was still flabbergasted Majima was even here. “What the fuck are you doing here?!”
Majima scowled. “I’m here to assist ya, dumbass. Didn’t you talk to Nishiki about this just last
night?”
Kiryu searched his mind. The memories had started to become clearer. The events of last night
became apparent. A phone call with his sworn brother. One where he reluctantly had accepted help,
as time was running out. Though, neither Kiryu had known who was the help. Oh, you have got to
be shitting me.

Majima paused for a few seconds, and then slowly put away his knife. “Ok, fine. It is you.

“You got it!” Kiryu answered quickly. “Just know this is going to sound completely insane, but it’s

Majima lowered his knife, and pointed it at Hanyuu. “Oh, don’t worry! Your Beelzebub Buddy

Majima was a bit taken aback by the reply. The 'monster' resembled a young girl more than

Kiryu nodded. “Sure, just know it’s going to be another long story.”

And so, Kiryu explained it all, or at least summarized it to the best of his ability. The ability to time
travel across ‘Fragments’, the past two loops he had been involved in. Hanyuu and Rika, the

Majima calmly listened the whole time, though he was confused at multiple points, mostly in
regard to the time travel aspect. As Kiryu wrapped up, he gestured to Majima if that would suffice.
Majima didn’t reply for a minute, still trying to decipher the chaos that had been thrown at him
within the last half hour. “A-are you ok, Majima?” Hanyuu sheepishly asked.
Majima shrugged his shoulders. “Yeah, minus having a few new gray hairs.”
Kiryu scoffed. “You’re 29, you’ll be fine.”
“Yeah yeah, you two want to explain why I am supposedly able to see and interact with her? That’s
the shit that set this off to begin with.”
Unfortunately, neither had the answer. Hanyuu shrugged. “We still don’t know why even Kiryu
can. The only guess I have is that a higher being than me is the cause. Neither Kiryu nor anything
related to the Tojo have ever showed up in a loop before.”

“Yes,” Kiryu affirmed.
Majima shook his head. “No wonder your ass was in a tizzy.”
Kiryu ignored Majima’s comment. “Anything else you’d like to know?”
Majima contemplated it for a few seconds, and then began to cackle. “You’ve outdone yourself this
time, Kazzy! Only you would end up in a situation like that. Just one more side quest to complete!”

Kiryu blushed a bit. “Yeah, and you’re here now too, smart ass! Are you going to help out, or not?”
“Of-fucking-course I am! Life’s been way too boring as of late. It’s about time I had some
excitement!”
Hanyuu tilted her head. “You are … awful enthusiastic about all this.”

really do.”
Majima’s wild grin calmed down a bit to a simple smile. “I’d be pretty heartless to ignore a poor
girl in need. I’m just going to have some fun while I’m at it.”
“Don’t you dare get any wise ideas, Majima,” Kiryu threatened. “You already got on me for not

Majima gave a mischievous grin. “Hey, that’s not changed. I’ll follow what you say. I mean it.
Doesn’t mean we can’t get a little… ‘creative’ with your P.E. class. ”
Kiryu held his head back, looking up. What am I doing with my life? The sky and trees above were

“YES, YOU CAN JOIN THE FUCKING CLUB!! HAUL ASS! WE HAVE TO GO!”
Kiryu began to jog, and Majima skipped after him. “Music to my ears, Kazzy!”

Dogs around? I need to have a serious talk with these two once they’re done.

No one knew what to say. “Does this count as martial arts?” Keiichi questioned.

Kiryu didn’t reply. He looked back at Majima with a determined stare. Majima winced in pain. He

“Yeah.”

As the sun set over the horizon, Okinomiya was getting ready for another Friday night. The streets
were bustling as people were heading home, or perhaps going out to drink. A blond man in his late
30s with a tacky red Hawaiian shirt was wandering the streets. Anyone passing him gave him

people over.
He was proud of that, and how could he not be? Divine luck must have been on his side. He had the
Tojo Clan itself trying to kill him, and yet he had gotten away with it. He had escaped the biggest
Yakuza group in all of Japan, and it was his greatest achievement. Who wouldn’t be giddy being
able to pull something like that off? Making the impossible possible.
Of course, he hadn’t actually done anything. Teppei had no clue why the two yakuza sent after him
were killed, but he sure wasn’t complaining. Maybe it was the Sonozaki Family, or they just had
some rotten luck. But either way, it wasn’t him. He had survived and was now about to score big

“My apologies, I can’t hear you very well. Could you come a little closer?”

He was about to get up close and personal, yelling into Majima’s face. He was maybe a few feet
behind Majima, before Majima whipped around, grabbed the collar of Teppei’s shirt, and slammed

what was going on, as his face was slammed again. Majima grasped the back of Teppei’s head and
hair, as he dragged Teppei’s face against the wall like a cheese grater. Majima finished throwing
him into some nearby trashcans as they toppled over, dunking all sorts of garbage onto Teppei.
Teppei could barely catch his breath, as he tried to sit up against the wall. His face was covered in
cuts and bruises, and his forehead was bleeding. He knew he was in trouble, but it was only now
clicking in his brain what he was probably dealing with. He looked up at his attacker. The eye
patch, the suit, the dull, merciless eye staring back at him. Even Teppei was smart enough to
recognize this man was a yakuza, and probably one from the Tojo Clan.
His fight or flight instinct activated. Despite his bravado, Teppei was very much a coward. A man
who always picked on people weaker than him. He had taken flight many times, but there was no
escape here. As pathetic a man he was, he would still choose to fight, in a situation like this. He
scrambled to his feet, and got into an amateurish fighting stance. Fitting for the street brawler, he
was.
Majima only scoffed at him. Teppei wasn’t a threat to him, only a nuisance. Teppei gritted his teeth
as his eyes were frantic. “D-don’t fuck with me!” He threw a sloppy punch, which Majima easily
sidestepped. He wrapped his arms around Teppei’s throat in a standing rear naked choke. Teppei
tried to break out, but stood as still as a statue as Majima hissed into his ear. “Try to yell for help or
get out of this, and I’ll break your neck.”
In a manner of minutes, Teppei found himself in the worst possible situation. He kept his mouth
shut as Majima continued to talk. “You’ve caused us a lot of problems. I can’t tell if you’re just a
dumbass, or if you really thought you were safe out here. I’m going to go with both, considering
you’re now one step away from dying.”
A faint whimper escaped Teppei’s lips. “P-please don’t kill me.”
“Oh, you misunderstand. We very much need you alive.” Majima lowered his voice into a more
sinister tone. “Though, you might wish you were dead by the time you’ve repaid your debt.”
Any remaining hope in Teppei’s eyes died out, as two other yakuza finally appeared. Majima
roughly threw him to the concrete ground. “You know where to take him. I’ll meet you two there.”
“Yes, Boss!” The two answered in unison.

Teppei was crumpled on the ground, in shock. It was only now starting to don on him. He had been
baited into this. He probably could have gotten away, if he wasn’t so easily aggravated. It was his
own reckless nature that had gotten him into this, and he cursed himself as he continued to grind his
teeth. Dammit! Dammit! Any feelings or thoughts vanished, as his nose was assaulted by a
chloroform-soaked rag.
Far away from the scene, Rena and Kiryu would soon arrive home by taxi. There was an
uncomfortable air between the two. Kiryu was fairly certain this was for the best, but he could still
see Rena with doubts. “Are you ok, Rena?”
Rena was startled by hearing her name, but quickly relaxed and put on her typical chipper smile.
“Hauu, don’t scare me like that, KIryu. I’m fine. Everything is fine.”
“… Is it really, Rena?”
Her smile shrank, as Kiryu pushed the topic. “Well, I guess I do have some worries.” She glanced
at the driver in front of them, and then leaned in to whisper. Kiryu took the hint, and did the same.
“They’re not going to do anything too badly to him, right? It’s maybe cruel for me to say, but I am
fine with them doing some stuff to him, considering how he treated Satoshi and Satoko.” She
looked at Kiryu with anxious eyes. “But I feel like we may have gone too far.”
Kiryu opened his mouth, and promptly closed it. The right thing to say here wasn’t easy to figure

guy, I was willing to even use you. It’s best if you just forget this night ever happened, Rena.
Ignorance is bliss, and you don’t need to know, much less see the world I left.”
Rena pouted. “Kiryu, I know I’m young, but I’m not an absolute child. You don’t have to treat me

to cleanse.”
Kiryu didn’t reply. He was well aware of Rena’s past, but this fragment’s Rena wasn’t aware of
that. He took a moment to come up with some encouraging words. “I think most people in
Hinamizawa are dealing with something like that, Rena.”
Rena looked up, a solemn expression still covering her face. “Really?”
“I don’t know what you’ve dealt with, but I’ve done some research on the history of this town. It’s
not all sunshines and rainbows, I can get that.”
Rena briefly panicked. “You’re not thinking of leaving, right?”
Kiryu gave a reassuring smile. “Of course, not. I know the residents of HInamizawa are good
people. And you’re a good kid too, Rena. I may not know what you’ve dealt with, but I trust you.
… Oh! And I know about Oyashiro’s curse, and how to avoid it. Hopefully, nothing happens this
year, and we’ll all have a great time together.”
Rena was surprised Kiryu knew as much as he did, but it also eased many of her worries. She had
wondered, once or twice, if she should bring up the curse. But Kiryu had gotten used to
Hinamizawa’s culture and ways as easy as could be. Oh, thank God. He’ll be ok. She wore an
adorable smile, forgetting all about her worries. “You’d better help me win a kyute prize, Kiryu.
I’m counting on you.”

Kiryu grinned. “Is that a challenge, I hear? You’re on.”
As the two travelled home, they truly had no idea what was in store for Teppei.

Jumbled words and noises filled Teppei’s ears as he came to. It was a slow, groggy awakening, and

“Oh, look who finally decided to wake up.” One of the grunts pointed out.

milking this guy for all he’s worth! Just give me some time and-”

Chapter 41: Red Soul Blue Flame Arc Chapter 9: Dine and Dash
It was early Saturday morning in Okinomiya. Tourists were doing sightseeing, some brave souls
arriving specifically for the Watanagashi, wishing to seek the event out of either genuine or morbid
curiosity. Hotels were almost fully booked, and it was a lively, hot day for everyone out and about.
There was one man wearing a barrette walking down the street, slightly standing out due to his
stereotypical artist look. It was Ichiro Maebara, Keiichi’s father.
It was rare for the man to be outside. Often, he would be cooped up inside his study, painting away.
So why was the man out and about, today? Simple, he was pursuing his one somewhat regular
activity outside. He was seeking some quality food from Angel Mort. While the man did tend to go
there for more vulgar reasons, something about the food and coffee did get his creative juices
going. So he wasn’t there entirely to be a lecher.
He wasn’t fully paying attention as he walked down the street, daydreaming about ideas for his
next painting. His daydream was abruptly halted as he bumped into someone. “Oof, oh, sorry! I
didn’t see you there, pal.” His eyebrows raised in recognition. “Yasunori?”
Rena’s father’s face mimicked Ichiro’s. “Ichiro?”
Ichiro chuckled. “Well, I’ll be damned. What are you doing walking around here?”
Yasunori nervously laughed. “Hehe, I suppose you wouldn’t believe I was trying to find a place to
grab a snack?”
“Well, that’s what I’m up to myself. But what about you? Where’s that Rina girl of yours you’ve
been dating recently. You’d best not be cheating on her, ya sly dog. It’s not every day you get to
