somehow she knew it would be ok. A long pause passed. “I think it’s best for you to go home for
now, Kiryu. I can’t put into words how grateful I am for you helping us. We can talk in the morning
about what we’ll do next.”
“You’re not concerned about them attacking tonight?”
“It’s a six-hour drive from here to Kamurocho. Even the Tojo aren’t strong enough to raid us
without preparation. Try to get in contact with Majima, and we’ll make plans, tomorrow.”
For the first time that Saturday, Kiryu smiled. “Thank you, Mion.”

Mion’s face reflected Kiryu. “No, thank you, Kiryu. Thank you for being a crazy enough bastard to
do this.”
Kiryu was going to say something about her language, but now was hardly the time. “Before I go,
Mion. One more thing.”
“Yes?”
“I swear we will rescue your sister. And if they so much as touched a hair on her head, I’ll-”
“I know, Kiryu. We already have a vague idea where she is. We’re going to try to rescue her,
tomorrow.”
Kiryu paused, as something came to mind. “I may actually have some way to help with that. But
I’ll need to talk with him first.”
“I’ll take whatever I can get. Just… I pray, she is ok. I don’t know what I’d do, if they kill her.”
“She’ll be ok, Mion. We’ll rescue her. I have to go now, but I need you to know. Despite
everything, I am your friend and ally in this.”
“... Thank you, Kiryu. Just… thank you.”
~~~~
After a much less tense, but still on edge return down the stairs and out the Estate, Kiryu felt
himself breathing a sigh of relief. He quickly walked home. He felt sad he saw no signs of Rena,
and wanted to beat himself into a pulp over what had happened. Gotta stop thinking like that. Or
else, Rika will be the one to turn me into a pulp. I’m just lucky she was patient and forgiving with
me this time.
As he began to unlock his door, he heard the phone going off inside. Who could be calling at this
hour? He entered, and closed the door behind him, promptly picking up the phone. “Yello?
“It’s about damn time you picked up, Kiryu! Where the hell have you been?!”
Kiryu almost doubted his ears, hearing Majima on the other line. “Wuh?! Majima?! That’s my line!
Where the fuck have you been?!”
“That’s…! Actually, fair. But just shut it, ok! I don’t know how much time I have. You’d better sit
your ass down, and listen to this.”
There was a rare urgency in Majima’s voice, so Kiryu heeded his demands. “Speak away.” What
followed was Majima recapping what had happened last night. The interrogation session with
Teppei, how he knew nothing, how Shimano had appeared, and how Teppei had mentioned Angel
Mort. It was what he had feared the most, but that was becoming routine now.
“It sounds like they’re coming tomorrow night, Kiryu. I don’t know what you can do within that
time, but evacuate the civvies at least. Hinamizawa is about to become a battlefield.”
“I know, Majima. Enough about all that, can you rescue Shion?”

“... I was lucky to be able to sneak in this call. Maybe Shimano thinks I’m no threat now since he
already has his excuse to go to war. I’ve been able to take a few glances at Shion. She’s guarded
heavily, but is pretty much unharmed. They seriously think she’s the Heir. I don’t think I can rescue
her right now.”
“... What about if a group of Sonozaki’s best so happened to hit where you’re at tomorrow
morning?”
Kiryu couldn’t see Majima, but he could still sense the grin crossing Majima’s face. “Now there’s a
damn good plan, Kazzy.”

Chapter End Notes

Chapter 44: Red Soul Blue Flame Arc Chapter 12: It’s What’s On
The Inside That Counts
Chapter Notes

Fair warning, there is some graphic, disturbing imagery in this chapter. Theoretically, nothing
worse than what I've already written in this fic or that is present in Higurashi itself. But, I felt
it was appropriate to give a heads-up.

See the end of the chapter for more notes

The Saturday sun would soon set over Hinamizawa. A tapestry of stars spread across the sky,
constellations in full view. The higurashi slowly falling away to a somber stillness that spread over
the town. But that was a few hours from now. For now, a mix of yellows and oranges spread across
the dam construction site. Small hills worth of discarded objects and garbage spread out along the
dump, the sun reflected off of various objects.
This was Rena’s home away from home, and really the only home she had right now. No one would
be there to welcome her. Possibly Rina would be, but she was terrified of the idea of seeing her
now. She was partially responsible for her partner’s death, and she wasn’t sure herself how she’d
act around Rina right now. So here she hid away. Crying only to herself, but at least comforted by
objects of familiarity and joy. Her little slice of Heaven, far away from the Hell that surrounded her.
She kept picking at parts of her body. Scabs, old cuts, her neck, etc. She kept telling herself to stop,
she knew this was bad for her. There is a saying that the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak. Her
spirit was poor, and her filthy flesh sought to consume itself. There was no Oyashiro to comfort her,
she had already called on the divine figure, pleading to help her. No response, and could she blame
the deity? Obviously, it would abandon her after everything she’s done. Perhaps it could forgive her
in time, but she deserved the loneliness she felt now.
She hugged a stuffed animal that was supposed to represent a bear, but resembled some mauled dog
now. There were holes with fluff sticking out in multiple areas. It mirrored the openings Rena had
created in her body. Who knows how many marks she had left on her body as a whole. What boy
could love the body of a girl like her? Ugly, filthy, rancid, diseased, dirtier than the pile of junk she
resided in.
Thoughts of self-deprecation and hatred swirled around in her mind. What would it be like to cut
open her own skull? Would there be anything inside, or would it just be a nest of bugs puppeteers
controlling her? Their antenna and limbs gouging her brain, feeding and tunneling inside it. She
dispelled the hideous imagery immediately, lest she make more of her filth visible, vomiting it out
and defiling her sacred place. Or maybe she should. This was her home, the outside should reflect
her insides.
That train of thought was interrupted by the sound of trash shuffling outside the van she was in.
Even in her current dire state, Rena’s instincts were present. Her nata was behind her, and she
reached back to grab it. It wasn’t impossible that the Tojo had somehow tracked her down. She
wouldn’t hesitate to slice open the face of any that dared to threaten her safety. She could already

envision the nata inches deep cutting vertically along the face of one of them. Their eyes bursting
out at an odd angle, ruined sunglasses barely hanging on, blood and brains leaking out on to her
nata.
“Renaaaa?! Are you around here?!!” Rena froze. “Keiichi?” She whispered to herself. “Rena,
please if you’re here, say something! It’s just me, Keiichi! Sorry, everyone else is dealing with
stuff, but I wanted to come check on you! I know you like to hang around here! Are you here,
hello?!”
She stayed as still as a statue. Truthfully, she was incredibly grateful Keiichi was here. If she could
turn to anyone, it would be him. They were in the same situation in her mind. But for him to see her
secret place and for her to be in this state? For her to reveal she was partially responsible for his
father getting shot? Would he so willingly accept her after everything? … Did she have a choice?
The flesh desired to keep her down, stripped of any happiness. But if anyone could raise her spirits,
it would be Keiichi. He continued to call out for her, and in a hope for desperate salvation, she
answered. “Keiichi?!”
She heard the footsteps pause, and then continue towards her. “Rena, is that you?! Where are you?!
Speak up, I can’t find you if… you… “ Now it was Keiichi’s turn to be unsure how to act. He had
found Rena, sitting all by herself in this van. Dried blood had stained her clothes and fingernails,
and it looked like she had made a cut along her neck. Her cheeks were stained with tears, and were
about to be stained with more as Rena’s eyes watered.
Even if he was at a loss for words, there was obviously a friend in need. He carefully opened the
door, and slowly sat down next to Rena in the van. “Are you ok, Rena?”
“... No,” she answered, holding back sobs.
“Er, sorry, it’s clear you’re not ok. That was insensitive of me to ask. … Can I help in any way?”
Rena didn’t answer, a downcast gaze being the only reply he got. “Is… is this about our dads?”
Rena tensed up, confirming Keiichi’s suspicions. He looked away outside the window, all sorts of
junk encompassing his vision. ‘Magician of Words’ he may be, but it would take more than a
simple magic trick to say the right thing to Rena now. If there even was a right thing to say in this
situation. His father was conscious, and would hopefully recover soon. But what about Rena’s?
Would her father wake up, was their situation even remotely the same?
“Rena, I… “ Rena slightly looked up, as his voice trailed off. He sighed, and faced her again. “For
once, I don’t know what to say in this scenario. I want to help, but I don’t know how. All I can say
is that if you need a friend to rely on, I’m here. I’ll listen to whatever you have to say. We all will,
but for now allow me to just sit by you as your pal. I won’t ask you to say anything. Just talk
whenever you’re ready. I’ll wait the whole night, if I need to.”
“... Won’t your parents get worried?”
Keiichi gave a reassuring grin. “I think my mom has her hands full with Dad as is. And I can
always just explain later. Trust me, it’s not a problem.”
Rena gazed away, returning to her view of the van’s floor. “I wouldn’t even know where to begin,
Keiichi.”

“Then think about it, or don’t. We have time either way. I’ll just sit here till you’re ready.”
“You’re ok with that?”
“Well, duh! What are friends for?”
Rena’s head lowered even more, fresh tears forming. “... Even if I might be responsible for what’s
happened.”
Keiichi couldn’t even think of how Rena could be at fault. Whatever it was, she was probably being
way harsher on herself than she needed to be. “Even if that’s true, I’ll hear you out.”
Rena didn’t reply. In fact, neither of the two said anything for some time. Keiichi kept his promise,
and kept silent gazing out into the junkyard, occasionally stealing a momentary glance at Rena.
Maybe ten minutes passed before Rena finally spoke up. “I… I need to tell you what’s happened.
It’s a long story, but I don’t know who else to tell.”
Keiichi perked up. “Uh, go for it! Like I said, we have time.”
Rena took a couple deep breaths. And then, she began. She explained the truth behind Kiryu and
Majima, the plan they had come up with, what had happened last night, her fight with Kiryu, what
had possibly happened as a result of all this. It was a long confession, occasionally broken up by
sniffles and pauses. By the time Rena finished, Keiichi was still trying to wrap his head around the
whole ordeal. Forget being a magician, he’d require an entire council of wizards to make heads or
tails of this. But it was just him alone, so he’d have to do his best.
“I just don’t know what to do, Keiichi.” She faced Keiichi, distraught and hopeless. “Because of
me, our fathers have been shot, and the Tojo could come invade any time now! W-what do I even
do?! What if they come back and kill your dad and mine?! What if they kill us and our friends?!
I’m scared, Keiichi! I don’t want to die! I don’t want our friends to-”
“Woah, Rena! Rena! That’s not going to happen! Calm down!” The words weren’t as elegant as
he’d like, but it was the best thing he could think of right now. “I get it, you’re terrified! I’m scared,
too! But getting wound up like this isn’t going to do anything! We need to talk to the others, make a
plan of action, and figure out what we’re going to do! And… I’m still trying to process everything
you’ve told me, but you’re making a lot of assumptions here! I don’t think it’s you or Kiryu or
Majima’s fault! It wasn’t maybe the best idea, but… you… “
As he was now grasping the full picture, he understood it was probably the best thing they could
have gone for. And it was just a tragic coincidence their dads had gotten caught up in it. He wasn’t
going to blame anyone but the Tojo for that. How could he? They were the demons that had created
this mess. However, the results were dire and now was not the time to worry about assigning
blame.
He shook his head, the words he needed arriving. “We can talk about who’s at fault later. That
doesn’t matter now. We need to protect our friends and family. I… I don’t know how, but we need
to start somewhere. I have your back, Rena. Trust me as your friend, we can get through this. We
can do this together, no one can beat us when we work together!”
He grasped Rena’s hand and leaned in close. “Please, don’t give up and trust in me and your
friends.” A resolute look was in his eyes. His magic had worked. Rena was enamored with Keiichi.
His unwavering determination, his strong but gentle hand holding hers, his beautiful eyes, his

handsome face maybe a little too close. The two blushed almost exactly at the same time, and
leaned back, with Keiichi letting go. “S-sorry! I didn’t mean to get so close!”
“N-No! It’s fine! Rena didn’t mind! I didn’t, really!” Rena stammered out. The two rapidly looked
away, lest they die of embarrassment. Eventually, Keiichi forcefully coughed. “Soooo, are you
feeling any better now?”
“Y-yes! I… I am. Thank you, Keiichi.” She still felt plenty nervous and guilty, but Keiichi’s words
had lifted a great burden off her mind. “Thank you for coming out here, Keiichi. I really needed to
hear what you had to say. I’m going to go home and patch myself up.”
“I wasn’t sure if it was appropriate to bring it up, but are you ok physically?”
Rena hesitated to answer, but nodded her head. “It’s a… bad habit. Don’t worry about it, I’ll be
fine! I will!” Rena said as convincingly as she could.
“A-alright, if you say so.” There was still an air of awkwardness between the two. It was almost
always the whole club together, or at least three people. To be this close in a confined space all
alone. It felt almost unbearable for the two teenagers still sorting out their feelings. Keiichi would
be the first to crack under the silence. “W-welp! I’d better get going! Do you need someone to walk
you home, Rena?” It would still be just the two of them, but at least the two walking home was a
familiar activity and a lot less cramped.
“I’ll stay a little longer, Keiichi. Um, can you promise to keep all of this a secret?”
“Oh, this hiding spot of yours? Sure, I don’t mind. It will be our little secret.” Keiichi said with a
wink that made Rena’s heart flutter momentarily.
Unfortunately, he had also completely misinterpreted what Rena meant. “I-I mean everything with
Kiryu and Majima…”
Keiichi’s face became solemn, a grave reminder of what would soon come. “Right, we can cross
that bridge when we come to it. For now, let’s meet up with everyone in the morning. Don’t stay
out here too long, you won’t have any light soon.”
Rena nodded her head. Keiichi gently opened the door. As he left, he waved and then carefully
stepped down and through the sea of junk before him. Rena sat there on her throne, the queen of the
dump, surveying her surroundings. She watched Keiichi with eagle eyes, as he eventually
disappeared out of sight. Darkness was creeping in, and light would soon leave her kingdom.
She wordlessly exited the van, walked over to a nearby abandoned suitcase, and opened it up.
Around her kingdom, she walked. Even with light fading, she knew every little detail of this dump.
It was her land, and within it were her possessions. You could find anything and everything
abandoned. Humans are temporarily alive creatures, and the objects they possess live a fraction of
that time before being discarded.
But new life can be breathed into an object. It just requires someone to love and cherish it. And
Rena cherished every single little object in this dump. Many of them she had added herself. They
were like her children, the residents of this land she ruled over. It was time to defend that land, and
some sacrifices might need to be made to do so. She was saddened at the idea of losing some of her
citizens, but they were born for such a task. That was always their role in life.

As she finished packing her supplies, a resolute look could be found on her face. You’re right,
Keiichi. It’s time to act. I won’t let the Tojo defile my happiness, no matter what.
~~~~
As the sun began to take cover behind the many hills surrounding Hinimizawa, Keiichi found
himself troubled with many thoughts as he walked home. He was only now truly starting to grasp
everything Rena had said. The gravity of the situation. The truth behind Kiryu and Majima. His
mind flashed back to the conversation he had with them. It felt blatantly obvious in hindsight, but
was the eye patch not a red flag? Had he had not joked with the rest of the club that the two looked
like sworn yakuza brothers?
And there was something harrowing the way Rena had described her argument with Kiryu. The
way he had somehow known Rena was considering doing something awful. It scratched at
something primal in his brain. He had had dreams, no nightmares about Teppei. He didn’t even
know the man all that much, apart from his history with Satoko and Satoshi. And yet, he had
experienced disturbingly realistic dreams about the man.
Of him returning home and abusing Satoko again. The despondent, almost corpse-like state it put
the poor girl in. How he would desperately search for any answer to save Satoko. How he would
always land on killing the bastard that did that to her. There was a scene all too familiar to him. A
bat in hand, as he chased down the man as he pathetically cried out for help.
It was ridiculous, the man deserved no mercy, no help. As horrifically as he had abused Satoko, a
child? Could such a man even acquire forgiveness for hurting her? For hurting his friend? Not to
Keiichi Maebara. Down came the bat on to his head. His blond hair stained red with congealed
blood. His skull malformed, shaped into something like a cracked egg.
No, that was right. The bat wasn’t coming down on his head, it was scraping through to the inside.
Believe it or not, there was a human brain beneath that fractured skull. There was something human
in that flesh sack pretending to be one. I mean, it made sense it must’ve been some creature
wearing the skin of a human. A being that had mimicked the brain of a human, or had stolen one
and transplanted it into its head. A demon! That could be the only explanation for how horrific that
‘man’ was. He was just a demon that had forsaken any humanity he had pretended to have. Quite a
wonderful disguise it had created for itself.
It’s not like he was a demon as well. It’s not like he had repeated nightmares of bashing in the
skulls of his own friends. Mion’s body mangled in a twisted mess. Rena’s eyes forced out from her
own cranium, pushing them out of the sockets. Crimson blood everywhere, soaking him and the
room he was in. Clawing out his throat and severing his own vocal cords as he confessed to Ooishi.
No, that was ridiculous. He’d never cause the entire village to be wiped out. He couldn’t just wish
into existence the deaths of people like a devil. It was a delusion, that he had killed Takano, Irie, the
whole damn village including the person he was trying to save. Speaking into reality, an entire
genocide? Absolute malarkey.
No, he could never be a demon. He could never hurt others. What happened to those young girls,
those actions he took were something he had gotten rid of, his old sinful self. He was human now,
he had to be! All those blood-curdling nightmares were still just dreams! They had to be, what the
hell else could they be, if not?! Killing that waste of space, that monster mimicking a homo sapien.
Mocking our species with his very existence. He was just a cockroach that didn’t even count as

anything to be killed. In the end, he was a righteous hero, slaying a demon. Nothing more, nothing
less.
…
…
Keiichi felt like he was going to throw up. His blood ran cold, and yet his whole body felt sweaty.
His stomach howled, growled, and finally it roared. Stomach acid and his lunch lurched from inside
him, out into the grass. It came, and refused to stop coming. Eventually, there was nothing but
spittle and half-digested food bits dripping from his mouth. He collapsed to the ground, laying on
his back next to the mess he had made, thankfully having not fallen into it.
He stared at the sky above. There was the faint appearance of stars as the orange would shift from a
dark blue to black. The smell was awful enough, he forced himself up, and kept walking despite
feeling dizzy. In some ways, he was astonished he had kept himself together with Rena. Was he
better at keeping his composure than he thought, or had his brain delayed fully understanding
Rena’s confession, lest this had happened?
Truthfully, he didn’t care if Kiryu and Majima were secretly yakuza or ex-yakuza or whatever.
They were trying to project the village, they were on his side. No, what truly disturbed him to his
very core. He would have done the exact same as Rena, if he were in her position. He would have
gone along with the two yakuza’s plan.
But that’s fine, right?! How could he ever blame Rena? No one was at fault, they were unified for a
just cause. There was nothing monstrous or demonic about it, they had gone to slay the beast. He
would have happily joined them. A party of four on a virtuous mission, it was like a fairy tale from
old. And yet, he had missed such a chance. Oh, well! There was always next time! They should
have invited him in the first place, but that’s life!
He wasn’t a demon. He was a human, he was just a normal 14-year-old boy wanting to spend time
with his friends over the summer making happy memories. Nothing was going wrong, even this
stuff with his father would pass, and he was sure Rena’s would wake up soon. Keiichi Maebara was
just a regular kid that wanted to create a normal life, cherishing it and his friends.
He could never turn into a demon and kill them, kill the entire village, kill himself in the end. Did
someone need proof? He’d happily provide it. He’d break open his own skull, show the whole
world his brain was that of a human. Tear out his very soul to prove he wasn’t some husk passing
as a man. There was nothing demonic about him in the slightest. He was just an everyday guy, a
normal boy in school.
… So why the hell did he keep hearing the footsteps of a demon behind him?

Chapter 45: Red Soul Blue Flame Arc Chapter 13: Rescue and
Repayment
Chapter Notes
See the end of the chapter for notes

The morning of Watanagashi had come. Tonight, there would be a grand festival. And also possibly
a night of bloodshed, as both the residents of Hinamizawa and Okinomiya feared another duo
added to the death tally. There would be far more corpses tonight than just two, if things didn’t
change soon. Majima sat in a chair in the corner, his futon sloppily laid out next to him. He hadn’t
gotten much sleep, but that was fine. He was too pissed off to care about missing some rest.
The clock in the corner of his room continued to tick down. It was a little past 7 in the morning, and
he had been up since 6. Any time now, a bunch of Sonozaki men would raid this place, and he’d
spring into action, or at least that was the plan. When they said tomorrow morning, he assumed
they’d appear while most of the remaining Tojo here were asleep or just waking up. By now,
practically all the grunts were up and about.
Were these Sonozaki boys not professionals, or was this a part of the plan? Had something awful
happened, and the plan fell through, leaving him and Shion alone without any help? All he could do
was speculate, hoping any moment he’d hear the chaos out there. But no, all the company he had
was his knife. He looked down at it, his reflection staring back at him.
They had already removed the phone from his room, realizing they had made a stupid mistake. A
couple of the younger and dumber grunts had threatened to take his knife away too, but a quick
beatdown sorted that out real quick. At least, everyone else here were wise enough not to mess with
him. Unfortunately, that also came with the requirement he didn’t do anything dumb himself. Lest,
he put both himself and Shion in danger.
He bolted right up, hearing some grunts yelling. A blasting noise that sounded like a shotgun went
off, a door falling to the ground as a dozen gunshots were suddenly heard. This was the perfect
distraction he needed. He cautiously crept to the door and put his ear to it. Closing his eyes, he
could sense the two guards had left. He opened the door slowly, not wanting to get hit by a random
bullet, much less friendly fire.
He peeked outside the door, only to immediately retract his head and fall to the ground, seeing a
corpse fall in front of him riddled with bullet holes. His knife was held ready, as the unmistakable
sound of a shotgun had gone off. He moved to one corner of the room away from the door. Instincts
were telling him to not make any sudden moves, that this was probably an ally. It didn’t make him
feel any less on edge.
The door came crashing down as the shooter kicked it open. Every muscle in Majima’s body tensed
as he was now face to face with the firing end of the shotgun. The man using it was tall with
sunglasses, short hair, and a well-trimmed beard. The two stared at each other, as he slightly
lowered his shotgun. “Goro Majima?”
Majima gave a strained smile in response. “The one and only. Thought I was about to get caught in
the crossfire myself for a second there. Your name?”

“Kasai… you can put the damn knife down, I’m not gonna shoot you.”
“And I won’t gut you like a fish, so don’t worry about it.”
There was a slight tension between the two, but Majima eventually lowered his knife. “I was
wondering when the hell you guys would show up. Is Shion ok?”
“Other than scaring the poor girl half to death, she seems fine.”
Majima cracked a smile. “Oh yeah, you’re her bodyguard or something, right?”
Kasai became unusually quiet. “Yes, this was a side of myself I was hoping to never show her,
but… it is my job.”
Majima’s smile vanished as he took a glance at the man lying in his own puddle of blood near the
entryway. “You can figure out her and your feelings later. Let’s get out of here.”
Kasai nodded, as the two men exited the room. Only now did Majima really get a chance to see the
carnage that had unfolded. He felt himself grimacing, but he couldn’t hide it. It was mostly
Shimano’s men that had been standing guard here, but a few of his own had ended up in the
massacre. The man below him was one of them. He wasn’t particularly close to any of his men, but
he strived to treat them well. There was a bitter pit in his stomach seeing a face he had known for a
year now battered and bloody.
It was just how things were in the Yakuza. You could have a Family of 100 men one day, and none
the next. That was the cruel, merciless world he had made his home in. No matter what it took, he
accepted he would stay in this batshit insanity for the chance to see his sworn brother again. He
could act as crazy and wild as he wanted, but even his mask had to slip rarely. It’s not like he had
killed them, but it didn’t make him feel any less grimy.
What is my fucking problem? I tell the guy to figure his feelings out later, and here I am getting
frustrated over a couple fresh corpses. Suddenly, he saw a man behind Kasai at the end of the
hallway. One they had missed, with a gun raised. “Die, you bastard!” Before Kasai could react,
Majima charged forward. The gun went off, Majima parrying the bullet with his knife. As the man
was briefly stunned, Majima threw his knife. It impaled the grunt right in the center of the man’s
forehead. He dropped the gun, and crumpled to the ground.
Kasai stood there in disbelief. This man he wasn’t sure if he could even trust had just saved his life

“... Thank you, Majima. I-”

As the Sunday sun set below the horizon, night arrived once more for Hinamizawa. What would

rebuild. But lives lost could not be replaced, and that was a lesson she had learned many, many
times.
“Our home is in a corner and out of sight, Satoko. I don’t see it burning down or anything.” I hope.
“Hopefully so, yes. I half-considered laying some traps around our house, but I’d hate for anyone
we know to get caught in them.”
“True, your traps show favor to no one.”
Satoko slightly smirked. “Only the best traps from a genius like myself, ohohoho!”
The laugh was forced, her smirk straining to stay put. There was a dower atmosphere over
everyone that had evacuated, and these two girls were no exception. Satoko’s face fell, and a
frustrated look entered her eye. “Why does something always seem to happen on this day, Rika? I
just don’t understand, it’s not fair.”
Rika’s eyebrows raised up and then came together as she scowled, looking at the ground. I’ve
wondered that for a long time myself, Satoko. The Rules of this world are not only unfair, they’re
downright cruel. I dearly hope we can break through them soon. You’d think with Kiryu we just
need to roll the dice carefully, and yet there is a constant string of new problems to deal with. And
at best, I fear we only have a few chances left.
Satoko continued. “I still have nightmares about Nii-Nii. Where is he out there? Is he even still
alive?” Tears formed, dripping down her face. “Am I going to lose someone else I love tonight?”
Alarmed, Rika quickly put her hands on Satoko’s shoulders. “No, they’ll be fine! I’m sure of it!”

“How do you know, Rika? You always seem to know things others don’t, but I just don’t
understand how you can be so certain.”
Rika avoided Satoko’s gaze. “I’m not, Satoko. But I fear more the idea of not believing in the
possibility they’ll live, and something awful happening. So, I trust things will be ok. Maybe it’s
naive, but I want to believe in Mion, Kiryu, and everyone fighting to protect the village. The best
thing we can do Satoko is pray they’ll be ok, and root for them here.”
Satoko sniffled, wiping a tear from her cheek. “I’ll try that Rika. Would you mind reminding me to
do that, if I start tearing up again?”
“Sure, Satoko. And if I begin to break down, help me stand back up again.” That’s the only thing
we can do. Just pray and hope for a miracle. But if anyone can pull it off, I believe Kiryu can. So
please, my friend, do whatever it takes to keep yourself safe and win.

“Boss…” The word slipped out from Kiryu’s lips, and fell to the ground.
The man scoffed. “I’m not your damn boss anymore, Civvy. Some ‘Dragon’ you turned out to be.”
Kiryu was utterly baffled. There before him was Daisaku Kuze, the most tenacious, formidable, and
determined man Kiryu had ever met. Perhaps, besides his own father. Five times he had fought his
man, and five times he had won. But he kept coming back stronger each time. And here he was
again, like a ghost that refused to leave him, haunting him till the day of his death. “What the hell
are you doing here? Last I checked, you were in prison.”
“Correct, and you know what? I was ok with that. I did the best I could, and I wasn’t able to stop
you. Serve a decade in the slammer, do a few more years in the Tojo, and then retire. It wasn’t a
bad plan, and then they decide to get me out of there a few months ago. Said ‘I was needed’. That
the current Tojo could use the extra muscle. Damn Sera to Hell, he just has me as a glorified grunt.”
He took a step forward, wiping some blood from his knuckles on his suit. “The worst part? I heard
you never came back. A man with the potential to become the Chairman himself, and settled to be a
damn civvy. I thought I saw something in you, kid. The making of a legend in the Tojo, and maybe
you did get that. But all I see now is a sad shell of what you could have been.”
Kiryu felt himself humbled. Their positions had completely swapped in regard to how successful
they were, but Kiryu couldn’t help but feel he had slighted his old boss. “Sir, with all due respect, I
chose to leave on my own terms. There’s nothing for me in the Tojo. I live a happy life now, away
from that horrific world.”
“And yet, here you are. Don’t lie to me. You could say you don’t want to be involved as much as
you like, but you’ll still involve your pathetic self in Tojo matters. I could at least somewhat respect
it if you stuck to the real estate shit, but no. You just had to be a thorn in our side, once again.”
A genuine smile crossed Kuze’s face. “That said, I’m not unhappy to see you. I always wondered
what would happen, if we had a rematch. The idea eventually faded, a ridiculous thought with what
I last saw. But looking at you now, you’re a fucking joke.”
Kiryu grimaced. He let his brass knuckles and gauntlets fall to the ground as he took a fighting
stance. “Years ago, Sir, I told you I’d rather fight a hundred Tojo men than fight you then. I keep to

that notion, but I will add something to that. I did beat down a hundred plus men less than a month
ago. I respect you greatly, Sir, but with what I was fighting for and still am, that’s nothing to me
now. Don’t you dare think you can put me down here and now.”
Kuze snorted, his eyes eager for a fight. “Still the same damn punk that always pissed me off. You
should’ve kept those on, but maybe I have underestimated you. Show me what you got, kid.”
The two men began to circle each other. Kiryu’s right leg forward, his left leg behind him, both
spread apart to give himself a good base of support. His right fist near his face, and his left near his
hip. Kiryu’s standard fighting stance, not specialized in anything but could intercept almost any
move. Meanwhile, Kuze’s legs were similar, with his right hand out partially open and his left in a
fist near his face. A traditional boxing stance meant for use at long range, guarding and feeling out
your opponent with jabs.
Kiryu stepped forward aiming for a high front kick to Kuze’s face. Kuze sidestepped it, closing the
distance immediately and jabbed Kiryu in the face. Kuze kept close, preventing Kiryu from
kicking. Kiryu performed a jab of his own, which Kuze weaved around with ease. Kuze used a 1-2
jab and then cross. Kiryu weaved around the jab, parried the cross, and lunged forward with a
straight of his own. Kuze blocked it, and delivered a horizontal elbow into Kiryu’s guard.
Kiryu took a step back. That’s right, he’s not just a boxer. He’ll use any tools he has to win. Kuze
stepped forward after Kiryu, striking with a low kick checked by Kiryu. The Dragon lunged with a
right hook, Kuze dodging and rewarding Kiryu with a body blow for his efforts. Kiryu coughed,
and used a teep kick to Kuze’s gut to make distance.
“I’m impressed, Kiryu. You retained your skills, after all.”
“I could say the same to you, Sir. Most let their skills rot in prison, and you’re not getting any
younger.”
Kuze frowned. “Age has nothing to do with it, damn you. I’ve only become more experienced.”
Kuze feinted a few jabs Kiryu could barely react to. Another kick to Kiryu’s leg, he took with his
shin below the knee to reduce damage. Kiryu feinted a front high kick and then used his leading leg
to step forward with another straight. Kuze brushed it aside, and used an angled straight, almost a
cross, to collide with Kiryu’s temple.
It grazed Kiryu’s head, as he went for an uppercut. Kuze blocked it with his forearm, and went for
his own uppercut, Kiryu narrowly dodging it. Both men exchanged blocked jabs and straights, as
the King of Hell ducked a cross hook and countered with a straight to Kiryu’s ribs. He gritted his
teeth taking the pain. His head leaned back to avoid a straight, and he delivered a side-kick to
Kuze’s hip.
The old man didn’t even buckle, he tanked it with the vigor of a man forty years younger. Kiryu
sloppily blocked a left hook stinging the back of his hand, and ducked under a haymaker going for
a tackle. Kuze clinched Kiryu in response keeping his ground, and delivered a foul kidney punch to
Kiryu’s back. Kiryu winced. This was no official ring, and illegal techniques were welcomed here.
The Dragon kneed Kuze into the gut, getting him off. He breathed heavily, keeping a close guard.
This was Kuze’s domain. The Japanese style of boxing was heavily based around using speed to
blitz their opponent with intense, close quarters action. An emphasis on closing the gap, and getting
up close and personal. Always moving forward with consistent technique and perfected jabs. And
above all else, having grit and determination. The ability to take knock out inducing punches, and

still keep going. That was the type of fighter Kiryu was contesting with, and Kuze had grit in
spades.
“You’re not wussing out on me, are you, Kiryu?”
“No, Sir. Just impressed with your perseverance.”
“Good to know, now come at me!”
Kiryu decided it was best to switch up tactics. He engaged Beast Style tanking a straight to his
cheek, grabbed Kuze’s outstretched arm, and dragged him forward with a heavy kick into Kuze’s
ribs. It made Kuze stutter, but only briefly. He repaid it with a liver shot, making Kiryu almost go to
one knee as he let go. Kiryu ducked a hook, and rose back up with an uppercut.
Kuze hit Kiryu’s wrist with his own, but the Dragon’s hand continued forward anyway. It grasped
on to Kuze’s face, allowing Kiryu to deliver two quick body blows to Kuze. I can’t be wasting my
time on this. The longer I’m here occupied with Kuze, the more people are going to die! Kuze
ripped off Kiryu’s hand, and delivered a straight to Kiryu’s face.
He couldn’t avoid it in time, so he might as well change its trajectory. He slightly ducked it, letting
it connect with his forehead. And a good thing too, because Kuze’s thumb had been extended. A
slightly different movement, and the knuckle could have jabbed out his eye. Both of the men’s next
strikes connected at the same time. An upward angled elbow from Kiryu to Kuze’s chin, and an
inside roundhouse kick to Kiryu’s chest. Kuze nearly fell over, and Kiryu gasped for breath.
“Didn’t know you’ve learned Muay Thai since I last fought you.” Kuze commented, holding his
jaw.
“I haven’t, but you learn some things sparring with people.”
Kiryu stepped forward with a right knockout straight. The King stepped in himself letting it graze
the back of his head, as he slammed his left hand into Kiryu’s outstretched elbow. A jolt of pain
surged through Kiryu, as the blow made it stretch at an awkward angle. He continued forward with
a left straight Kuze leaned back to dodge. He did not expect Kiryu to convert it into a horizontal
elbow across his cheek. “I can fight dirty too, Kuze!”
Kuze spat out blood, and lept forward with a cross. “You think I give a shit?!” Kiryu tried to
escape, but Kuze whipped his arm around Kiryu’s neck trapping him into a clinch. Kuze’s free
hand landing a blow into Kiryu’s gut. The Dragon shook him off, but he pursued and got Kiryu into
a clinch again. He intercepted Kuze’s strike this time, grasping his wrist and arm and pushing them
in opposite directions. Kuze grunted in pain, his shoulder on fire.
Kuze retreated, but Kiryu initiated a clinch himself. He lowered his head, and then slammed the top
of it into Kuze’s face with a rising headbutt. The two men separated as Kuze bounded forward with
a straight and then a high kick aimed to Kiryu’s face. He was already prepared to dodge it, but the
King had other plans. Midway through the kick, Kuze stomped his foot down into Kiryu’s keeping
him in place.
Kiryu’s head bolted back, a knockout strike thrusted into his face. Kiryu briefly blacked out.
Something awakened in him. On instinct, the Dragon used his leaned back head to gain momentum
for another devastating headbutt right into Kuze’s skull. The King took a step back, not even
Enma’s strength enough to take it without wavering.

Kiryu’s right leg stepped forward, his right fist seeking to lodge itself in Kuze’s nose. While
frazzled, the old man had enough sense to weave around it. It was a trap, as Kiryu’s left leg dealt a
destructive blow with an inside calf kick. Kuze wasn’t done yet, he whirled back slightly charging
an uppercut and surged upwards. Kiryu met his strength with a downwards elbow, bone connecting,
but Kuze’s cracked.
In his haste to finish the fight, he had missed Kuze’s other fist heading for him. He stood his
ground, taking the hook to his cheek. He stared at Kuze with a hard, unwavering glare, and
delivered a counter hook right into the King’s liver. Kuze bent over in pain, the King offering a
rare, involuntary bow. Kiryu raised his leg high into the air, and slammed it into the top of Kuze’s
head with an axe kick. Finally, one of the men fell as Kuze crumpled to the ground.
Kiryu stood there breathing heavily. He wasn’t heavily damaged, but injured he was nonetheless.
The only other sound was Kuze’s soft laughter, as he sat up. Blood was running down both of the
men’s faces, but Kuze’s was certainly the worse for wear. Kiryu’s eyes sharpened. “I’ll be direct
with you, Sir, no, Kuze. If we fight anymore, I can’t guarantee I won’t end up killing you. And I’d
rather not do that.”
“Bah!” Kuze scoffed. “You think you could kill me, brat?” He slowly stood up, spitting out blood
on to the nearby grass.
“No, Kuze. You’d somehow find a way to haunt me in the afterlife. But as for your mortal and
weakened flesh… I don’t think I have to elaborate on that.”
Kuze smirked. “Ah, fuck it. Go.”
Kiryu blinked a few times. “Wait, what?”
“Go, you dumbass! What do you think that means?!”
“... I was just surprised you weren’t going to fight me more.”
A self-derisive laugh escaped Kuze’s lips. “Heh, look at me, Kiryu. I’m just a stubborn old man
that doesn’t know when to quit. I don’t give a shit about this Sonozaki nonsense, I just wanted to
kick your ass. And I achieved that. Not as much as I would have liked, but still.”
“Kuze…”
“Ah, don’t get all floppy and sentimental on me, I still have half an interest in punching you. But I
learned something in prison. You get plenty of time to think there, too much damn time. Life isn’t
just about getting back up no matter what. There’s got to be a point to it. And I’ve reached a period
in my life, where I have to actually consider that. You have to know your place in the yakuza, and
with this being my sixth loss, I think it’s time to put this chapter of my life behind me.”
The King creaked his neck, folding his now broken glasses and returning them to his pocket.
“Unless, you’re really that desperate to fight.”
“... No, Kuze. I really need to hurry, speaking truthfully.”
“Then get your sorry ass out of my sight! I got what I wanted, and you proved you’re not a civvy
sap! Fuck off, and go do what you have to do, before I start wanting to cave your face in again!”

Kiryu kept silent, and bowed. “Thank you, Kuze.” And with that, Kiryu put back on his brass
knuckles/gauntlets and rushed off. Kuze was now alone, he sat down leaning against a nearby tree.
He pulled a spare cigarette out of his pocket, and lit it. “Can’t even call him a damned kid,
anymore. He’s grown up, and made a real name for himself.” He inhaled, and then exhaled smoke.
“Getting too old for this shit.”
A few minutes later, the man of Enma left the battlefield. Years later, he would retire avoiding the
police that night. But that’s not the focus of this story. No, Kiryu had many more trials awaiting
him. Everyone there did. Unfortunately, no one was prepared for what Rena had set up, and the
night was about to become a lot more grim.

“Get back here, you fucking brats!” Keiichi could feel his blood pumping, his heart beating far too
fast. His muscles screaming to slow down, but he couldn’t. He was a meter behind Rena, both
running from a dozen or so Tojo chasing after them. Things had been going fine, for the most part.
This was their home, and they had the element of surprise.
But, they were only two kids. More than once they had narrowly avoided being shot, impeccable

Keiichi!”
Rena slipped around a corner, with Keiichi scrambling to get behind it, to grant even just a few

“We’re almost there, Keiichi!”
They almost ran into a few other Tojo, who decided to join the hunt. The night was alight with

The command made Keiichi’s mind freeze, his jumbled thoughts becoming surprisingly clear, if

Satoko. No time to be daydreaming, they were about to cross said bridge. Like Rena had said, jars

Keiichi was about to start running away, but Rena clasped his hand “Wuh, Rena?! We need to go!”

there’s too many!”

The boy was stunned, finally adding it up. “R-Rena, what are-!”

As much as Kiryu could within a few minutes, he treated his minor injuries. A cut on his forehead
the most pressing one, possibly blinding him, if it opened again. He had disposed of ten more Tojo
in the short time that had passed since he left Kuze. Realistically, he could go almost the whole

As he ran through buildings, the night shined out of the corner of his eye. Fire, smoke, and wood

His composure returned, as another man suddenly appeared. He had come around the corner of a

Keiichi’s vision felt muddled. He saw Rena above him yelling something, but he could hear

this.” Her eyes were bloodshot, she turned her nata, the blade now facing Kiryu. She flew into a

but she was also going faster and with her full strength. Every blow could be a lethal one, as Kiryu
concentrated to block or dodge each of her blows.
Like a family of rabbits escaping their home, Tojo poured out of the hole rapidly. Panic was
expected, but Nishiki barked out orders and kept them focused and in line. With thirty seconds left
on Rena’s timer and everyone out, they all bolted away from the house running past Kiryu and
Rena fighting. Rena made to swing at one that got close, but Kiryu stepped in her way. He
roundhouse kicked the side of the blade nearly making it fly out of her grasp again.
Seeing that was his sign, Kiryu circled her. He grabbed her arm forcing her to drop the nata,
scooped her up, and ran away from the house. She kicked and made a fuss, but Kiryu wouldn’t let
her go no matter what. Kiryu gritted his teeth, and braced for an impact any second. … But it never
came. He had run some hundred meters from the house, turned around, and saw it still standing in
the distance.
There was never a timed bomb to begin with. Just a desperate girl’s gamble that almost paid off.
Truthfully, it could have become a bomb, but that would have required a risky play on Rena’s part.
But here she was now in Kiryu’s grasp, kicking in the air like a toddler throwing a tantrum. Kiryu
put her down. Not exactly gently, but Rena wasn’t giving him much choice.
She turned around and punched Kiryu in the gut. Kiryu flinched, but it had no strength behind it.
The girl had exhausted everything she had against him, but she didn’t care. She continued to pound
him as tears welled up in her eyes. “It’s not fair, dammit! Why does my father have to die?! Why
are the people I care about put in danger?! Why is my home burning to ashes?! Why?! Why?!
Why?!! WHY?! WHY?!! WHY?!!!”
She fell to her knees, utterly defeated. “Why is my life just one tragedy after another?! Why can’t I
just… *sob* be happy?!” And with that the girl broke down, and wept. She unleashed everything
she had caged up. She had armored herself in self-loathing, hatred, suicidal recklessness, and a
determination to recover her happiness no matter what. It now cost her everything, and there was
nothing more to protect the girl now.

So she felt confused, when a new embrace found her. Kiryu had kneeled, and held her tightly. He
looked close to tears himself. “I’m sorry, Rena. I wish things had gone better. I wish I had chosen
differently. That I was a strong enough man to have prevented this all. Even saying this, I feel is
self-serving.”
“But I want you to know I don’t care about what you’ve done tonight or have done before. That I
can live with you hating me, but that I’ll be there for you regardless. There’s one thing I must ask
of you. A hypocritical thing to ask after everything. A struggle I will deal with myself for a long
time to come, but one I must ask you nonetheless. Please, forgive yourself. Even if it takes years to
do so, one day, I want you to be able to do that.”
Rena couldn’t utter a word. Kiryu’s had stolen her breath away and filled her mind. The silence was
broken by Keiichi stepping forward. “Rena, I… did just pull a fast one on you there. I had to save
them, but still. I’m sorry for that. Not just for that, but everything. I should have stopped you
sooner, and realized that I was encouraging you in the wrong direction.”
He got on his knees, and embraced Rena as whole. “Usually, I have the words for a situation like
this. But like Kiryu said, it feels self-serving to say. And I think he put it better than even I could
have. So, all I’ll say is that we have a lot to answer for. I don’t know what happens next, but I’ll be
there for you. By your side every step of the way. He and I both forgive you, and want to go
forward. Together.”
Fresh tears entered Rena’s eyes. “Why… why are you two the ones apologizing? I’m the one who
nearly killed Kiryu’s brother. Keiichi, you nearly died so many times because of me. I’ve killed…
so many people tonight all in the name of protecting Hinamizawa, and for what? Is there even any
of Hinamizawa left?”
Kiryu let go and faced both Rena and Keiichi. “We’re all killers tonight.” The words left both kids
mute, as Kiryu’s face was filled with regret. “Caught up in the madness of war. This night is just
another blip on history, another grand showing of how cruel humans can be. It probably sounds
pretentious as hell, but that’s just the state of things. I don’t have any of the answers. But what I do
know-”
Kiryu stood up, stepped in front of the kids, and stared at their audience. “I’m not letting either of
you get hurt.” Nishiki had been left stunned at the scene before him. It was extremely rare he ever
saw Kiryu this emotional and vulnerable, but Kiryu’s words brought him back to reality. One of the
men next to him was drawing a gun, and aiming it at the kids. He immediately drew his own, and
aimed it at the man’s temple. “Don’t you fucking dare.”
“The hell are you doing, Boss?! They killed OUR men! I’m not going to just stand by and let them
go!”
“Did I stutter, asshole?” Nishiki shoved the gun’s end into his head physically to make his threat
clear.
“You’re not even our Boss.” One of the other grunts pointed out. “I don’t care if you outrank me!
I’m going to kill the bastard myself!” Nishiki panicked, he obviously didn’t have a second gun to
stop this guy. Rena’s eyes widened, and a new sense of clarity entered them. She stood up and ran
in front of Kiryu, her arms outstretched.
Kiryu was too late to react. “Rena, what are-!” A bullet fired. And after that, there was dreadful
silence.

The Dragon wasn’t able to protect her at that moment. Someone else did. The grunt dropped his
gun, grasping his hand in pain. Ooishi, gun in hand, had just clicked his trigger. He breathed a sigh
of relief. “Phew, that was close. Glad I could make it in time.” Four other officers arrived and
pulled out their guns. Sirens could be heard in the distance. Ooishi clicked his tongue. “Oh, NOW
they send back-up when everything is wrapping up. Damned cowards.”
He cleared his throat and stepped forward. “You’re all under arrest! This war is over!” He glanced
at Kiryu with a smile. “Though, some of you might not be there for long.” A helicopter flew over
making an announcement. “Attention, everyone! This is the Watch Dogs! Put down your weapons
and surrender immediately or we will fire.”
After a few seconds, the Tojo complied and officers got to work cuffing various people. Kiryu
whirled Rena around to face him. “Rena, what the hell were you thinking?!”
“I… I just didn’t want anyone else to die. Weren’t you about to do the same?”
“Yeah, but…!” Kiryu swallowed his words and eventually laughed to himself. He was too tired to
argue anymore. “Ah, never mind. Just never do that again. It’s been a very, VERY long night.” And
now, it seems to have finally come to an end.

1 week later
To say the fallout of the war was catastrophic would be an understatement. 93 Sonozaki men and
145 Tojo were killed. Plenty others were wounded, and the hospitals nearby were well occupied.
The only reason more police and the Watch Dogs had shown up was for Tokyo to cover
themselves. But it had already deeply gotten out of hand. A solid third of Hinamizawa had burned
down, and another third had taken some form of property damage. A rebuilding effort was already
being planned to bring relief to the residents, as everyone decided how to continue going forward.
Shion was worried sick and gave Mion multiple choice words after seeing her injuries in person,
but was more than overjoyed to see her alive. Nishiki had been arrested, but thanks to Ooishi and
Kiryu’s good word he was in there only for a few days. Though, he was still being heavily
investigated for his relations to the Tojo Clan. Satoko and Rika’s house was one of the handful of
buildings that took no damage, not that the poor girls had anywhere else to go. They returned
safely, and were able to continue living normally.
The situation with Rena, Mion, and Keiichi was a lot more complex. All three confessed to
multiple crimes, and due to their young age and the complexity of the whole situation, there was a
massive legal nightmare going forward in regard to the trio. Though, Mion would hopefully be out
sooner than later after everything was handled. Majima would be under arrest for the foreseeable
future, confessing to being involved, but not directly responsible for the disappearance of Teppei
Hojo and murder of Mamiya Rina.
As for Kiryu, the Dragon rested. For the day or so he was in prison, he did almost nothing but
sleep. Almost two months now, his life had been turned upside down. And for once, he got the
break he much deserved. Of course, there was never rest for the weary. He had many news
reporters and police questionings to attend to, much like the last fragment.
On some level, it was dreadfully boring to him, but it certainly beat being in war. There were also
rumors going around he may have been involved in Teppei’s disappearance, but Majima denied it.

Ever since that night, Rena had been residing in a psychiatric hospital. At some point after
everything was over, the girl fainted. Since then, she had been recovering slowly both mentally and
physically. Day and night blurred by, and she felt like she was in a purgatory of sorts. Perhaps, a
fitting consequence for her actions. The only thing keeping her from utterly abhorring herself was
Kiryu’s words. It was hard to feel anything positive about herself, but for his sake, she would try.
When she heard she had a guest, she assumed it was another police officer. She nearly gasped when
Kiryu entered the room. “Kiryu! What are you doing here?!”
He slightly smirked. “Is a teacher not allowed to see how his student doing?”
It was meant to lighten the mood, but Rena still looked downcast. She couldn’t bare to look into
Kiryu’s eyes. “I’m sorry, Kiryu. I feel like I have a billion things I need to say, but I don’t know
where to start.”
“Hey, it’s fine.” He sat in a chair next to her bed. “I’m just here to visit. Let’s keep it simple, I’ll
start. How… have you been?” Kiryu cringed at himself on the inside. Yeesh, assuredly I could have
come up with something better than that. We’re both anxious, I guess. But I don’t want her to feel
bad, so fuck it! Fake it till you make it!

Evening had arrived in HInamizawa. The town was in a poor state of affairs, but still people lived

Rika’s smile fell, and she shrugged. “What else can we do?”

Any moment, I’m going to hear those bugs. Sure enough, the familiar serenade of the higurashi

After a shower and getting dressed, Kiryu joined Majima at the table and ate his breakfast. He

“Oh, yeah. I have a vague recollection it burned down. A shame too, it’s a nice house.”

“Can I just tell my name for now?”
“Sure, it’s something.”
“Ok, just, if you’ve heard of me, don’t freak out or anything. I probably couldn’t answer your
questions anyway, I’m trying to figure out things myself. I’m not even sure what year it is.”
“I won’t freak out, so tell me. What is your name?”
The lad hesitated to answer, but eventually did so. “Satoshi, Satoshi Hojo. I need to find my sister,
and make sure she’s ok.”
Time seemed to stop for Kiryu. And who could blame him? One of Hinamizawa’s greatest
mysteries was being answered right in front of him. One not even Rika held an answer to. What the
fuck?

Satoshi Hojo. The boy who murdered his aunt in 1982. The love interest of Shion. And most
importantly, Satoko’s lost older brother. Not since his first loop did Kiryu have so many questions
on what could be going on. But Satoshi’s look of fear brought him back to reality. Kiryu closed his

Kiryu hesitated for a half-second. The girl hadn’t exactly been ‘ok’, but a lot better than under her
abusive aunt and uncle. “Certainly, she is now better than she used to be.”
A wave of relief flooded over Satoshi. “Oh, thank you. I’m… really grateful… to hear she’s doing

The lad crumpled in Kiryu’s arms making him instantly alarmed. “Oy, Satoshi! Stay with me!”

Things were starting to add up in Kiryu’s head. … Is that where he’s been all this time? Not

Satoshi. He looked exhausted, but simultaneously at peace. There’s a lot of missing links here, but I
can ask about those later. I need to get this kid some help, and I get the feeling the Irie Clinic is the

Deep in the Irie Clinic, a man was putting in a number into a phone like his life depended on it.

“The puppeteer, the mastermind, the 11th hour villain. Yeah, I get it. I’ve read a decent amount of

Yet another morning revealed itself to Hinamizawa. Satoshi closed his eyes tighter as light poured
in through the window. His body resisted, but he had long left the land of sleep by now. He blinked
a few times, his eyes adjusting to the light. He still felt tired, but far more rejuvenated than before.
After stretching with his body making a popping noise or two, he got out of bed and looked at the
time. 9:30? Oh dear, I slept in. He could hear sounds in the kitchen. Groggily, he stood up, folded
his futon, and put it away. Kaieda had provided some spare clothes out of his own money for
Satoshi, and they fit him nicely. Though, a quick sniff proved he needed a shower before anything
else.
With that out of the way, he exited the room to see Satoko and Rika waiting for him. As well as a
guest. “Oh, Shion I-” He cut himself off as he squinted. “... Sorry, are you Shion or Mion? You two
look so similar.”
The Sonozaki girl smirked. “Hehehehe, I wonder.”
Satoshi paused for a second, and sighed. “Mion, it’s clearly you. Shion doesn’t have such a boyish
sounding laugh.”

“Wuh?! That’s not-” Both Rika and Satoko giggled. “Good morning, Nii-Nii. We cooked breakfast
for you!”
“Oh, wow! This looks… delicious!” Jeez, when was the last time I had something like this…
Mion cleared her throat. “We figured it had been a while since your last proper meal. So I arrived
early and helped out!
“I see. Thank you for letting me sleep in.” I definitely needed it.
“Also, Satoshi. I have some good news.”
“... Yeah?”
“I’ll go over what happened last night and this morning. It’s not exactly a secret now you’re back.
News travels fast here. So, my goal last night was to explain the situation to Grandma and have her
address the town.”
Satoshi flinched at Oryou being mentioned. “Ok… how did she react?”
“Relax! I said it was good news, right?”
“You did. It’s just… you know.”
Mion’s excited face fell slightly. “I’m aware, Satoshi. The history between our two families is…
well, we don’t need to go into that. Point being, I’m on your side. You want to know how Grandma
reacted? She smiled at hearing you had been found.”
Satoshi had to do a double take. “She smiled? Her?!”
Mion’s smile shifted to a more sheepish one. “She… does have a reputation. But she’s not exactly
the cold-hearted demon you think she is. She’s going to call a general assembly today, and explain
the situation. Things are going to be ok.”
“I was surprised too, Nii-Nii. But this is a good sign!”
Satoshi glanced at his sister and then back to Mion. “And the police?”
Mion went to say something, paused, and transitioned to a serious expression. “That was the other
thing I wanted to talk to you about. I don’t think it’s anything to worry about, and I’ll personally be
accompanying you. However, Ooishi has asked if we could meet him at the Irie Clinic.”
Satoshi’s heartbeat rapidly increased. Rika put a comforting hand on his shoulder. “Meep, it’ll be
ok, Satoshi. They don’t think you did anything wrong. They just want to ask some questions about
the Irie Clinic.”
Satoshi swallowed as he tried to calm his heart. “R-right. It should be fine. Excuse me for a second.
I have to go to the bathroom.” He sloppily stood up out of his chair, and stumbled over to the
bathroom.
As he entered and closed the door, the three girls looked at each other concerned. “Is Nii-Nii ok?”

“I’m… I’m not sure, Satoko. We all know something happened to his aunt before he disappeared. I
know they pinned it on that guy, but… “ Mion contemplated on how best to say it.
“That guy was the culprit behind his aunt’s murder. Let’s just leave it at that.” Rika firmly stated.
“And even if he was responsible… he’s our friend. I’m not going to let him be taken away again
after he’s just now returned.” It was a morally dubious thing to say, but both silently agreed with a
nod.
Both faucets were on as Satoshi rubbed his face with water. He turned both faucets off and stared
into the mirror, his reflection staring back into his soul. I’m powerless. I’m a murderer that has
gotten off scot-free. I could call it a miracle, but that doesn’t feel like the right word in this
situation. None of this is a good thing, I got lucky. I don’t know what the hell I’m doing, or what I
need to do going forward. All I can do is rely on my friends.
He used two fingers to open his right eye. It was blood shot, and even with the sound sleep he had
bags under it. He stared at it for a long time occasionally blinking. There was nothing demonic in
his eyes, and yet he wasn’t sure if he still counted as human. Irie, I hope that medicine is as
effective as you say. I might be human after all. But that won’t keep this guilt from consuming me.
And Oyashiro himself help me if I go beyond that.

all.

The duo exited the café leaving the trio by themselves. Satoshi had a quick look around. “Are we
the only ones here?”
“My uncle owns the place, so Sis was able to convince him to let us have the place to ourselves.
Though, I feel like she went a bit too far.”
“Do they have any staff here? Who’s going to serve us?” Satoko wondered aloud.

“That would be my job, Ms. Hojo.” The two Hojos looked behind their booth to see Kasai
approaching. He bowed. “I’ll be your server.”
Shion lightly giggled. Kasai raised his head. “Is there something wrong, Shion?”
“I’m just wondering what you’d look like in the Angel Mort dress.”
Even with the sunglasses hiding his eyes, his face showed clear discomfort. “An amusing idea,
Shion. However, I must stay dressed like this for professionalism’s sake. Lest I bring shame to the
Family I serve.”
“Overly serious as always. I know what I want.” Shion stated, pointing at an item on the menu.
Kasai nodded, and wrote it down. “And for you Satoshi? If you need some more time, I can come
back.”
“Um, I’ll just… have this.”
“Good answer, Sir.”
“Wait, I didn’t know you could cook, Kasai.” Satoko interjected.
The slightest of smiles appeared on Kasai’s face. “Who do you think has been helping Shion
learn?”
“Urgk, … you didn’t need to let them know that, Kasai.”
“Perhaps, but it would be wrong to deceive our esteemed guests. I’ll go start cooking the food.”
“Hang on, what about my order?” Satoko questioned.
“Ah, that. Shion has already prepared a meal choice for you rich in a variety of nutrition.”
Satoko’s face soured. “Not with vegetables, right?”
“Satoko, it’s about time you tried asparagus. I’ll put some mayo on it. It’s delicious, I promise.”
“... I don’t want to.” The girl was ready to fabricate crocodile tears.
“You want to look brave in front of Satoshi, right? I’m sure he wants his little sister to be eating
well.”
“That’s… not fair.” Satoko pouted. “I’ll try a bite, if I must.”
Shion with a victorious smile motioned to Kasai the matter was settled. “Very well, I’ll be out with
your food shortly.”
Satoshi was baffled at the exchange. “What’s going on?”
“I think I mentioned it before, but I’ll say it again. If Keiichi has been like an older brother to me
while you were gone, Shion has been like an older sister to me. … Perhaps, too much so.”
“Oh, don’t say that, Satoko. You need a proper diet.”

“You’ve been taking care of her?” Satoshi inquired.
Shion blushed slightly. “Well … yeah. You asked me to.”
Satoshi finally recognized what Shion was talking about. “I did, that’s right! I didn’t forget that, I
just… it didn’t come to mind. … You two do seem very close.”
“She’s family to me, and I don’t say that lightly. I could never be a substitute for you, but I… I
wanted to see her happy.”
“Shion…” Satoko’s voice waned.
“Sorry, Satoko. I don’t mean to talk like you’re not here, but I want to be genuine with how I feel.”
“... I know. And I’m grateful for all you’ve done, even if I hate you forcing me to try veggies.”
“It’s what a good older sister would do.”
As Satoshi watched the exchange, he lowered his head with a bitter smile. “Man, I really went and
left both of you with a burden to carry.”
“W-what?! No!” Shion frantically denied. “I don’t mind at all. I love Satoko and I lo-... I care
deeply for you as well, Satoshi. I’ve kept at it, because I had hope you’d return one day. And now
you have! There’s no burden! Both I and Satoko have become stronger waiting for you to return!”
“It’s true, Nii-Nii! Please don’t blame yourself. It wasn’t your fault, it was the syndrome!”
“Yes! The… pardon, what now, Satoko?” Shion did a double take.
Satoko quickly covered her mouth realizing she probably shouldn’t have spilled the beans. “Go
ahead, Satoko. Shion deserves to know.” Satoshi insisted. After a few seconds passed, Satoko
explained what they had learned from Irie about the Hinamizawa Syndrome and how it affects
people. Shion listened intently, though she felt deeply unsettled by the implications. Perhaps some
even involving herself, but that was best saved for later.
“... As Satoko said, you had to be taken to the clinic because of your disease. You didn’t wake up
for nearly a year’s time! That’s how badly it was affecting you!”
“Perhaps, but I can’t blame everything on sickness.”
“Yes, you can! You’ve not been a burden to us, Satoshi! I promise.”
Her words were sincere, but something about them bothered him. Dark, suffocating thoughts crept
into his mind, and he began to grit his teeth. “You don’t understand. I’m not who you think I am. I
should still be in that bed trapped beneath that clinic.”
Shion couldn’t understand what Satoshi was saying, and was growing irritated. “That’s nonsense,
Satoshi! Why would you even say such a thing?!”
“Because, Shion, I’m not a good person.”
“You’re the sweetest boy I’ve ever met, Satoshi! Please, be kind to yourself!”

“Why should I be? I’ve done something horrific.”
“What could you POSSIBLY have done to justify how you’re acting right now?!”
“Nii-Nii please, this isn’t like you.”
Satoshi lowered his head, a small, humorless laugh escaped his lips. “Why are both of you acting
like you don’t know? If you know me so well, it should be easy to guess. Ooishi knows. All my
friends know. Everyone pretends they don’t, it’s ridiculous.”
“Would you spell out whatever the hell you’re referring to?! Seriously, Satoshi! You have no reason
to badmouth yourself!”
Satoshi slowly looked up. His bangs covering one eye, and the other glaring hard at Shion causing
her to tense slightly. “Maybe you really don’t know, Shion. So I’ll put it as plainly as I can. I
murdered my own aunt, Shion. I’m a killer. That’s the kind of person you’re looking at right now.
I’m neither the brother nor person you think I am.”
A chilling, horrifying silence filled the room. Shion was struck mute by Satoshi’s confession.
Satoko had realized the truth at some point in the past, but it still rocked her world to hear Satoshi
say it. “Nii-Nii…”
Gradually, Shion’s head lowered to the ground, her bangs covering both her eyes. Satoshi could
only pathetically smile. “The truth finally comes out. But at least it’s out there now. It’s relieving,
but I can’t stop at just confessing. I should turn myself in later today. If I’m not being too selfish
here, I’d at least like to enjoy one last meal with my sister and you, Shion. Truly, thank you for
everything. If I must have one final memory before I spend time atoning for my sins this is the best
I could ask for.”
“Who cares?” A soft inquiry whispered from Shion’s mouth.
Satoshi furrowed his brow. “What, Shion?”
“WHO CARES, GODDAMMIT!!” Shion stood up and slammed both her hands down on the table
startling both of the Hojos. “You really think no one else wanted to get rid of those pieces of shit?!
That no one else wanted to kill them?! Your aunt and uncle weren’t humans! They were abusive
demons that hurt you and Satoko every damned day! What else were you supposed to do?! Just sit
there and take it while you both withered away! Something had to give!”
“S-Shion?! B-but I-”
“Obviously killing isn’t the right answer, but how else are you going to get out of that situation?! I
don’t care if you did it or not! Maybe the syndrome pushed you toward it, but then even more so
you’re not at fault! No one was crying over her death! No one mourned for that flesh bag
pretending to be human! That useless uncle of yours skipped town! And if he ever shows up here
again, I’ll personally make sure he’s-”
Shion froze. Her gaze shifted to Satoko. She was staring back at her with horror, as if she no longer
recognized her. A tsunami of regret washed over Shion as she slowly sat down. She covered her
mouth in shock. “Satoko, I… I’m so sorry I lost control of myself and…”

Only silence met her outburst. She put both of her hands over her face and leaned back. “Oh, I
should have just kept my mouth shut. … No. I could have phrased it better, but I don’t regret what I
said. And I need to say this to you, Satoshi.”
She uncovered her face, fresh tears running down her cheeks. “I just got you back. I can’t lose you
again. What you did wasn’t the right thing, but no one would blame you. And it is possible your
disease brought you to that point.”
“Please, don’t turn yourself in. Not after all I just got you back. Not after Satoko just got her
brother back.”
Satoshi was lost for words. He stared at Shion, and then looked at his sister. She was crying now
too. “I… I want to believe it was Hinamizawa Syndrome, Satoshi. I don’t think you’d be capable of
murder normally otherwise. Please don’t turn yourself in. Don’t leave me alone. I don’t want to
lose you again, Nii-Nii.”
Her response completely broke his resolve. Defeated, he buried his face in his hands as he slumped
in his seat. “Even if I don’t turn myself in, how can I live with myself? How can I atone for what
I’ve done? If I don’t absolve myself of this guilt, I’m afraid I’ll do something horrible again. Either
to myself, or someone I care for.”
“You do what you can, kid.” All three lifted their heads and turned their attention to the source of
the voice. It was Kasai. He awkwardly cleared his throat. “I didn’t mean to listen in, but I heard
Shion’s outburst and was looking for a good time to interject. Assuming, you don’t mind me saying
some things to the boy, Shion.”
After a few seconds, Shion nodded her head. “I’m not great with words, so this will come off as
blunt and maybe offensive. I’m a yakuza. Often, we get our hands dirty. Sometimes, we get them
dirty with blood. I’ve killed more than one person in my youth, and had more than one man under
me die from my orders now as I’ve grown older. I’ve killed both intentionally and unintentionally.
I’ve spent years in prison for my crimes. And it is still equally possible I’ll find myself dying with
lead in my stomach in the future.”
“I’ve chosen this path and its many regrets. If I could, I’d go back in the past and avoid killing
those I’ve murdered. But the fact of the matter is that their blood is on my hands. And all I can do
is try to do good now where I can. I know it might sound odd for a yakuza to say this. Especially,
when I’m a man who still stores a double barreled shotgun in the trunk of his car secretly, just in
case of emergency.”
“But with the Sonozaki Family wanting to transition from crime to going clean and becoming a
general guiding force for the town… I think there’s a better future waiting for us all. Perhaps one
where I can truly turn over a new leaf. Satoshi, boy. You are just a child with your whole life ahead
of you. Someone has already taken the fall for you. You no longer need to serve time.”
“Did that result from luck? Absolutely, but so did your return to the world of the living. You also
have something a lot of us don’t. Friends and family willing to support you as you go on with daily
life. A support network that can be there for you when needed. It might seem selfless to turn
yourself in, but from my perspective you’re being a selfish brat trying to make yourself feel better.”
“You really want to throw it all away? Your life is not your own. You have friends that want to
welcome you back. You have the Head of the Family I serve preparing the town itself to have you

here. You have a cute sister whom you mean the world to. And you have a girl, so head over heels
in love with you, you’d have to be as dense as a rock to not see it, but that’s tracking so far.”
Shion’s face went beet red. “K-K-Kasai!!!”
That familiar slight smile returned. “I know his type, Shion. You’d have to literally spell it out for
him sooner or later.”
“Then let me do it on my own terms, dammit!”
“My apologies, Ms. Sonozaki. You can yell at me later.” He returned his gaze to Satoshi. “Point
being, kid. And pardon the language. Don’t be a dumbass and make the right choice. Or I might
just personally storm in there and break your sorry rear out of prison myself. Knowing Shion, she’d
half consider ordering me to do it, anyway.”
“You only get one chance at life, kid. Don’t waste it. Now if you excuse me, I think I smell the food
burning.” And with those final words, he rapidly left to finish the food.
Satoshi’s lips were mouthing words like a fish out of water. Satoko kept silent waiting to see what
would happen next. Shion covered her face in embarrassment. “Stupid Kasai…”
Eventually, Satoshi flopped his arms in the air and leaned back. “I give up.”
It was so flippant it caught both his sister and Shion off guard. “So… you’re not going to turn
yourself in, Nii-Nii?”
“What would be the point? I still have the guilt, but he made such a sound and concrete argument, I
have nothing. Literally freaking nothing. I feel so seen through, I might as well be naked.”
A soft sound bellowed from Satoko’s throat as it transformed into a full-blown laugh. “Nii-Nii, I’ve
never heard you sound like that before.”
Shion was desperately trying not to crack a smile, but shortly she found herself giggling as well.
Even Satoshi had to laugh a little. “Man, I really am a mess.”
“You are a mess, Satoshi. But-” She reached over and firmly grasped his hand. “You’re my mess.
And I’m never letting go of you again.”
Satoko pouted. “Hey, don’t forget he’s my brother.”
Shion laughed again. “Sorry, he’s OUR mess. And you’re stuck with us.”
“... Like I said, I still feel a lot of guilt. And I don’t even know where to begin about ‘atoning’. But
if not for my self, I’ll… I’ll try to live a normal life for you two. If I trip along the way, please be
there to help me get back up.”
“Of course, Nii-Nii.”
“We will.” Shion answered.
Afterward, their food arrived. A few bits burned, but edible. “My sincerest apologies. I wasn’t able
to completely save the food… “ Kasai stated.

“Truly, it’s fine. Now go rest, Kasai. You’ll need it for later.” Shion remarked with eyes closed and
a devilish smile.
Kasai gulped. “Y-yes, Master Shion. As you say.”
Satoshi grabbed his chopsticks, and took a bite of his lunch. It tasted wonderful. He looked at both
Shion and his sister happily eating their meals. His gaze then turned to outside. It was a splendid
view outside, the sun shining brightly and people walking to and fro. Life moving on as was
intended.
Satoshi took another bite. It warmed his insides, and for the first time that day he felt at ease. I don’t
know what’s ahead in my life. I have no clue where to begin in how to live ‘normally’ now. But for
them, I’ll give it a shot. I must.

Night had come, and the higurashi’s activity had ceased. Kiryu was reluctantly sharing bed space
with Majima once more, but it was what they both had to deal with. Kiryu was almost asleep.
When he felt Majima tapping his shoulder. “What is it, Majima?” He grumbled more than asked.
“I need your help with something.”
“It’s past 11. Let me go back to sleep.”
“No, I’m serious. I’m trying to remember something.”
Grumbling more, Kiryu flipped on to his back looking at Majima. “What?”
“Do you remember those disco places you and I used to dance at?”
Kiryu slightly frowned. “They’re still around? What does this have to do with anything?”
“I was just thinking about it. Today’s Friday, yeah? There was some really catchy song I danced to
a few times there. It would go like ‘Can’t stop dancing all night long. Jumping and shaking
something? Move your body. Don’t stop the music all night long. Keep it on. It’s a… Friday
evening or Friday night?’”
“I think I remember a song like that. But why do you ask?”
“I’m trying to remember the name of the song.”
“... You’re screwing with me.”
“No, I’m serious! I’m trying to remember what the name of the damn song was!”
“Really? Majima, it’s called ‘Friday Night’. You literally said the name in the lyrics.”
The realization hit Majima hard as he facepalmed. “Ohhhhh, I’m a dumbass! How could I forget?!
It’s literally a Friday night right now! Geez, no wonder it felt so familiar.”
“... Was that it?”
“Huh?”

“I thought you said it was something important.”
“Yeah, it was. It was going to keep me up all night trying to remember the name of that song.”
The silence was deafening. “... Go the fuck to sleep, Majima.” Kiryu rolled back over, grumbling a
few curses under his breath.
Majima crossed his arms. “Hmph, fine! See if I help you the next time you can’t sleep! Bitch!”
Majima dramatically got back into bed and turned away from Kiryu on his side.
Unbeknownst to the two, Hanyuu had been watching their shenanigans the whole time. She was
utterly nonplussed. How again did these two become the key to saving my daughter?
