That time of year had arrived once more. The day before Watanagashi. A time for everyone to do
their part. And certainly, the kids were busy. Mion was helping lead multiple projects. Rena was
obsessed with the prizes at one of the booths, a massive teddy bear having enraptured her from her
work. Most of the men including Keiichi and Satoshi within reason were doing physical labor and
helping set up exhibits and the stage for Rika to perform on.
And as for Rika herself, she was confined to her practice as usual. A role so mind-numbing to her
now, she could practice freely while she let her mind drift. So it was a pleasant surprise when her
friend called out to her. “Satoko? Meep, why are you here?”
She held her hand up, recovering her breath. “I forgot to tell you about yesterday.”
“Ah, how did it go? Hopefully really well.”
“Yeah! … For the most part.”
Rika’s eyes narrowed. “Did something happen?”
“... Yes, something did. The result wasn’t a bad one. But it was something that needed to be
discussed.”
Satoko summarized Satoshi’s confession and Kasai’s speech. Rika wasn’t terribly surprised to hear
based on how he was acting, but Satoshi was the one friend of hers she had no future knowledge of.
No patterns to recognize, no actions in previous fragments to consider. So it did leave her feeling
uneasy. “Will he be ok?”
“I think so. You saw him this morning. He has a lot more energy than yesterday. Not that his guilt is
gone, but I think he’s in a much better place mentally.”
“Nipah! That’s great to hear!”
“It is! And if there are any setbacks, I’ll help him through it. It’s… it’s my turn to protect him this
time.”
Rika exhaled sharply. “I’m… sure he appreciates it, but don’t push yourself so hard, Satoko. Things
aren’t how they were. We’re all in a much better place now.”
Satoko nodded. “I understand your concern, Rika. But he’ll be living with us for right now. If you
think I’m going too far just… let me know.”
“Meep, I will! See you later, Satoko!”
Satoko smiled and waved as she dashed away. Rika’s smile faded away as apprehension coated her
body. Here I am once again. On the precipice of yet another possible tragedy. All I can do is just
pray nothing bad happens.

Further away, Satoshi and Keiichi were helping move various supplies. Satoshi stuck to carrying
lighter things, and took a short break now and then to conserve stamina. The monotonous nature of
the labor comforted him, kept his mind away from bothersome thoughts. This was the most time he

since they had exchanged only bits of small talk, but he was able to observe how he carried
himself.
He was full of vigor, and more than eager to help out. Despite being a newcomer and outsider at

had changed. The people around him were strangely nicer than they had been before. Judgmental

Everything had moved so fast in just a few days. An unusual sense of pride filled him for being

His mind returned to Keiichi in front of him. About how this young man had helped Satoko in his

“How long have you been here?”

Satoshi’s eyebrows rose a fraction. “Ah. I won’t poke the bear on that one then.”

“And you as well, Keiichi. May it be a wonderful partnership.”

After a slow, but steady journey to Okinomiya, the boys had arrived at a local store and in a matter

two. The boys were having a relaxed chat as they walked towards their bikes parked a ways away.
They were about to turn the corner when Satoshi stopped. “Keiichi, watch out!”
“Huh? Oof!” He wasn’t looking where he was going, and walked right into a man rounding the
corner.
“Agh! Where the hell do you think you’re walking, brat?!”
Keiichi realized he had messed up badly “S-sorry, Sir!”
“And as for your friend…” The man’s expression shifted from rage to befuddlement. Keiichi
followed his eyes to Satoshi. The boy’s face was pallid, ill, and rancid with fear and shock. Both
bags clattered to the ground, as Satoshi began to shake. “... Uncle?” Dread shot through Keiichi’s
body as he realized who the man was before him. He could only keep silent, unsure of what would
happen next.
Teppei’s confused face changed to a slimy grin. “Well, I’ll be damned. Is that you Satoshi?”
Satoshi didn’t answer. He was still reeling. “W-w-what are you doing here?”

“I have my reasons. Where have you been hiding? … Actually, it doesn’t matter. I was about to
catch a taxi before your… friend bumped into me. It’s fine, though. Accidents happen.” There was
a not so thinly veiled malice behind his words.
Keiichi was about to say something, but Satoshi stepped forward. “What do you want?”
Teppei grunted. “Want?! Does an uncle need a reason to see his nephew? I was heading to our old
home. Assuming, the piece of junk is still in one piece. … Why don’t you come with me, Satoshi?
Visit our old stomping grounds.”
Before Satoshi could answer, Keiichi interjected. “Oh! So you’re his uncle! I’ve heard about you!”
Teppei arched a brow. “Huh?”
Keiichi wore a regular smile, but his eyes were giving a challenge. “Yes, MANY things.”
“And what exactly is that supposed to mean?”
Keiichi was wading in murky waters with a predator right in front of him. But he didn’t care. He
wasn’t about to let something happen to his newfound brother. And yet, Satoshi put a hand on his
shoulder with an intense gaze that pleaded not to do anything. Satoshi, what are you doing?
“Just all the shenanigans we got into when I was younger! Y’know, old silly stories.”
Teppei was obviously skeptical of the claim, but he could let it pass by. Because who could have

Reluctantly, Satoshi nodded. “Keiichi, I’m sorry to ask, but could you take these two bags.” He
bent over stuffing the spilled items back into the bag, and handed them to Keiichi. “I know it’s a

It was a hard glare. One that did demand a lot, but in their current situation, Keiichi could only nod.
What was he going to do? Make a scene? Run away with Satoshi? Presumably, Teppei was still
Satoshi’s guardian. And Satoko’s as well. Oh no, Satoko! “But Satoshi, what about your sis-”
“It’s fine. … I’ll handle it and keep her safe.” His voice was low, but demanding.
His sheer resolve made Keiichi flinch. “But Satoshi, you can’t. Your condition-”
“Will be fine. Everything will be fine.”
Keiichi felt like he was about to cry. Could he really do nothing to help his friend? “Then what

“Would you two brats quit yapping! I don’t have all day, Satoshi!”
Briefly, Satoshi gritted his teeth, but found some level of calm. “Just be patient. And make sure

“I… ok.” With a final nod and a mutual understanding, the two parted. Keiichi took a deep breath,

“About damn time you two quit it. Yeesh, what is he? Your boyfriend?”
There was a brief change in Satoshi’s breathing as it sharpened. But he kept his temper. “No, Uncle
Teppei. Just a new friend.”
“Ya don’t say.” He eyes went back and forth between his nephew and his friend. He spotted a taxi
coming, and waved it down. “Let’s get going, Satoshi. I’m sure we have a lot to catch up on.”
At that, Satoshi’s facade fell. And whatever blessings he had gained seemed now like nothing more

The ride to their old home was torturous. Teppei asked a few questions, but after Satoshi kept
giving the most bare minimum of an answer, he got annoyed and gave up and closed his eyes. After
roughly a half hour, they arrived a few houses away. His whole body felt wobbly, but Satoshi
steeled himself and silently followed Teppei. A brief walk, and Satoshi had returned to what he
might think of as his own personal hell.
Teppei grumbled a few times as he kneeled and searched for something. He picked up a heavy
rock, and underneath in a hole was a small box. Inside was a spare key to the property. He cursed
once as he stretched his back, and unlocked the door. Only to find out it was unlocked to begin
with. He looked over his shoulder. “Oh, yeah. You mentioned you live with Satoko and that Furude
girl now, huh?”
With a measured expression, Satoshi nodded. Teppei looked away pondering something. “I’ll go
grab her later.”
Alarm bells rang off in Satoshi’s head. “I’ll get her!” The outburst made Teppei pause and look at
him suspiciously. His throat felt as dry as the Sahara. “A-As in, I’ll get her for you. You probably
just want to relax, right? She’s my sister, let me take care of it.”
Teppei grunted, and opened the door. “Whatever. Just don’t pull any funny business.” Both entered
the house, and Teppei held his nose. “Damn, this place smells dusty!” He kicked aside some trash
on the floor. He looked around and eventually plopped into a nearby chair. “It’ll do. Beats some of
the places I’ve been to.”
His sharp eyes turned to Satoshi sending a chill down his spine. “Sit down.”
Satoshi didn’t argue. He took a seat in another chair facing Teppei. His face scrunched briefly, the
dust being worse than imagined. An unpleasantly familiar sight played out. His uncle grabbed a
cigarette, lit it with his personal lighter, and leaned back in the chair. He crossed his legs, his eyes
now resting on Satoshi anymore. “So, tell me.”
“Tell you… what?”
“Isn’t it damn obvious? Where and what the fuck have you been up to the last year? You killed that
bitch of a wife I had, and fled the scene. And none of my guys have heard shit about you since.”
His blood turned frigid. An undeniable terror across his face, which Teppei only smirked at.
“What? You think them pinning it on some random bastard meant I couldn’t figure it out?”

He began to shake like a leaf. “I… I…”
“Oh, don’t get me wrong. You did me a favor, Satoshi!”
Satoshi froze. He had no idea what to say next. Not that Teppei gave him a chance to say anything.
“You know how many times I contemplated wringing her neck? I’m sure the broad considered it
for me a few times. Having to flee my own home was inconvenient, but I have connections. It
wasn’t that bad, and I found me one hell of a babe. No clue where she’s been the last few days, but
this house has more than enough room for her. Consider her your new aunt.”
Satoshi still didn’t reply making Teppei raise a brow. “The fuck is your problem, kid? Did you have
nightmares I’d come avenge her and make you black and blue? Break every bone in your body.” A
nasty smile formed, amused by his own violent capabilities. “Eh, I can’t blame you. You know your
place. That said, I’m still curious what all happened. So enlighten me, and keep it simple. I’m not
one for drawn out stories.”
Satoshi swallowed and somewhat regained his composure. “I… don’t know how simply I can
explain I was in a coma.”
Teppei frowned as he blew out smoke. “The hell? You’d better not be pulling my leg.”
“I’m not! Genuinely!”
Teppei stared him down, every second for Satoshi feeling like an eternity. Eventually, his uncle
shrugged. “Get on with it.”
As efficiently as he could, Satoshi elaborated on his and Satoko’s history with Hinamizawa
Syndrome. That he had been in a coma underneath the Irie Clinic for a long time, and was a test
subject for medicine. He got more than one baffled look as a reply, but even to Teppei it was clear
Satoshi was telling the truth.
His uncle put his now finished cigarette in an ash try, as he mulled over the story. “Isn’t that some
shit? Both you and your sister need this specialized medicine?”
“Yes, … and it’s free! So you don’t have to worry about costs.”
Teppei was only half listening now, lighting another cigarette. “Hell of a story, you got, Satoshi.
The way you describe this syndrome shit. I can’t help but wonder. Perhaps, that’s what led you to
murder?”
Satoshi went pale. A satisfying enough answer for his uncle. “Damn, and here I thought maybe you
had grown some balls. Doing nothing but defending that pathetic sister you have.”
Satoshi tensed for a fraction of a second, but he kept his cool. “So… what now?”
Teppei snorted, something about the question entertained him. “What now, he asks?” He got up
from his chair, rising to his full height and walked over to Satoshi. “Did that coma give you brain
damage, too?”
“N-no, sorry for asking.” His eyes never fully met Teppei’s, his uncle now towering over him.
“We’re gonna be a family again, ya moron. What else would happen next? … Though, it doesn’t
hurt to lay some ground rules.” He slightly squatted reaching eye level with Satoshi, forcing him to

stare back into his soulless eyes. “You and Satoko do everything I say. No questions asked, no
attitude, and we’ll get along just fine.”
Without warning, he grasped Satoshi’s throat with one hand. The boy spasmed, and reached for the
hand with his own, but he knew he could do nothing in this situation. “But if you pull some shit.
Try to ice me like you did your aunt. I’ll fucking kill you and that shit runt sister of yours.
Understand?”
Satoshi vigorously nodded. Teppei kept a tight grasp a few seconds longer, and then let go. His
nephew gasped and began to cough violently. “Good boy. Now get off your ass and start cleaning
up around here. I’m going out to grab some drinks. And call wherever Satoko lives now, and tell
her to get her ass over here.”
Without a modicum of care to his still coughing nephew, Teppei put out the cigarette and walked
out the door. It slammed loudly behind him. As Satoshi recovered, crippling fear consumed him.
Reality was setting in. Nothing had gotten better. Nothing had changed. And now his sister would
suffer again with him being in no condition to protect her. If Oyashiro existed, all he could do is
whimper and pray that things would be ok. If only he knew she was doing the same not far above
him.

After what felt like eons, Rika was finally free to go home. All of her friends had already left for
home including Satoko, which made her feel lonelier than usual. In truth, she felt on edge. The vast
amount of fragments she had passed through, the numerous tragedies she had seen. It almost gave

went wrong?
It was strange to think of Hanyuu in that way now. ‘Someone you could consistently rely on’ was

dangers, there was always a comfort in Hanyuu’s renewed self and Kiryu being a steadfast ally.
Things must be changing for the better, they managed to find a fragment where Satoshi had
recovered.
And yet unease gnawed at the back of her skull. She tried to put it out of her mind as she began to
walk home. The higurashi serenaded her, an experience so common, so repeated the girl no longer
registered it as anything but background noise. In a way, it perfectly represented her life. A
cacophony of white noise unchanging that ceased to exist as night came, and a new day brought the
same repetition.
Feeling philosophical today, aren’t we brain? Her stomach growled, a consequence of no lunch that

No, this wasn’t the first time she had felt this sensation. So much had happened in the last three
fragments. Had it completely escaped her mind, or was she so in denial that it could happen again

“Hanyuu! What happened! Speak to me!”
The goddess slowly shifted her gaze over to Rika. Puffy eyes and tear stained cheeks greeted her.
“Welcome home, Rika.” Her voice was uncharacteristically monotone. It made Rika start. Hanyuu

A smidgen of light returned to her eyes, perhaps aware of how she must have looked. But it just as
quickly vanished, not even having the energy to maintain appearances. “I’m… I’m so sorry, Rika. I
couldn’t do anything.”

“What happe-”

“And then I remember what’s happened every other fragment where someone killed Teppei. He’s

“Yes, you can! The alternative is his blood on your or my hands!! And I don’t trust either of us
enough to avoid that!!”

There was a long, agonizing silence between the two. Both stared on steadfastly not giving any
corner. “Majima. If something happens to her, are you going to take responsibility?”
“It was never our responsibility in the first place, Kiryu. The worst mistake we made was bringing
the underworld into all this.”
“If Teppei has so much has hurt a hair on Satoko’s head, I’ll wrench his-”
“He already has, Kiryu. Rika saw it all. She was being brave and protecting Satoshi from him.”
For a second, Kiryu was like a deer in headlights. But then reality set in and every emotion poured
forth as he grabbed Majima by the collar, slammed him against the wall, and got ready to punch his
face through it. His fist stopped centimeters from his face. He was breathing heavily, unrestrained
rage on his face.
Majima looked at him blankly. “Damn. Your fears about losing control weren’t unfounded.” He
wrenched Kiryu’s hand from his collar. “I said I’d be your ‘Nishiki’, Kiryu. And I meant that. But
unlike him, I don’t mind getting violent. If you’re not gonna listen to reason, you’re going to have
to go through me before I let you do something stupid.”
The Dragon offered no resistance. He sagged to his knees. No tears came, but his face was wrought
with bitterness. “Can I really do nothing, Majima? Am I so powerless to protect her?”
“You’re only one man, Kiryu. An impressive man, but still a man nonetheless. I wouldn’t say
there’s exactly nothing we can do. But if we just storm out to his house now, it is guaranteed to end
poorly. We need to consider our options carefully. And if nothing else…”
He grumbled a little before continuing. “This sounds corny to say, but Rika is right. You should
hold on to hope that something good can happen. Think about the fragment that happened before
you arrived. It did end in Takano murking everyone, but before all that. They managed to
collectively save Satoko. Now, I don’t know how that might work with Satoshi mixed in. But there
is a path here we can take.”
Gradually, Kiryu stood. He took long, deep breaths. There was still some denial there, but he was
able to accept the current situation, if just barely. “Sorry. I completely lost my cool there. You
didn’t deserve any of that.”
“I mean, I wasn’t really complaining. I’ll always take a chance to kick your ass.”
“Is that your way of trying to cheer me up?”
“Yeah, it’s my specialty.”
“A specialty in bullshit, maybe.”
“Absolutely, I acquired that years ago.”
The corner of Kiryu’s lips formed the smallest hint of a smile. “Fuck this. I’m going to bed,
Majima. I feel awful about hearing that news, and will probably have nightmares tonight about it.”
Kiryu stated dryly. “But it would be wrong to not attempt to get a good night’s sleep.”
“What about your dinner?”

Kiryu raised an eyebrow. “Do you really expect me to have an appetite? I feel like throwing up.”
“No, I guess not. That was dumb of me to ask. I’m feeling pretty ass myself right now, so I think
I’ll join you. Let’s both get some rest.”
“Just make sure you don’t forget the names of any songs before going to bed.”
“Oh, fuck off. Are you still mad about that?”
“Not so much mad as just still annoyed. But I suppose that’s a regular feeling with you around.”
Majima grunted. “Happy to provide.”

Chapter End Notes

I've noticed this chapter and the last one were hard to write in some ways. Teppei is a
character that is pretty easy to write, but I just kinda hate writing him lol. He's necessary for
the narrative and I think it can be interesting to explore how other characters react to him
being around. Especially now with Satoshi in the mix. But I will say I think every chapter of
this arc going forward will be a lot more interesting to write. I'm also writing this on not much
sleep, so perhaps that's a contributing factor.

Chapter 59: Bloodstained Angels Arc Chapter 8: Killing Intent
“What a shit morning this has been.” The Mad Dog said it to no one in particular. Just a basic
observation, a meaningless grumble he voiced aloud. It was a succinct way to illustrate the last few
hours. He had never seen Kiryu this down before. The Dragon fulfilled what he thought was best.
Establishing a meeting with the rest of the club members at the school, and explaining what was
going on.
It was a predictable set of reactions. Shock, anger, frustration, sorrow, and a brutal acceptance that
they would have to wait and figure out what to do next. Rika had been deeply empathetic to Kiryu.
The century old girl continued to surprise, Majima. He figured she would be the one suffering the
most, but humans are resilient and adaptive creatures. Numbing detachment and desensitization
could come for anyone. It wouldn’t be wrong to call it compassion, but it was a jaded compassion
all too eager to be able to resonate with someone else.
Or maybe I’m just being too cynical. Whatever it was, Kiryu was in slightly better spirits after a
talk with Rika he had left to give them privacy. But now here came the fun part. Shion had arrived
not too long ago. He could hear her muffled yelling through the walls. A determined Kiryu trying
to talk her down, but met with little success. A sigh from the abyss itself rose up out of Majima’s
throat. Time to do my part. He had volunteered to handle her if she got out of hand, but he wasn’t
exactly ideal for the job. Still, he’d keep his word.
Shion was mostly a good kid, but she could be impulsive and especially violent at times. If the two
sisters hadn’t switched, he pondered if she would have been perfect for the role of Heir. Of course,
there were matters of nature VS nurture, and how Mion would turn out. And who knows, there was
probably a world like that in this damned sea of fragments. But contemplating about alternate
timelines wasn’t going to fix the headache rapidly approaching him.
“Fine! I’ll go kill Teppei myself and save them!!” Her declaration echoed through the school.
There it is. One eye or not, he saw this coming from a mile away. More muted pleas and cries from
other friends this wasn’t the way. Any moment now, Shion would come storming out the building
with a murderous vendetta.
An old speech flowed through his bones. At the time, it was beyond frustrating to hear. In the long
run, it was the best thing he could have heard then. And now it was his turn to tell it to a foolish
youth in need of it. Sera, you son of a bitch. He cracked his neck, and mentally prepped himself to
stop Shion.
Thirty heartbeats later, the girl charged out the school door, slamming it open. If she saw Majima,
she paid him no mind. Eye on the prize, a deep green aura surrounding her. Majima blinked and it
went away. “If you kill him, Satoko and Satoshi will never see you the same way.”
Her motion ceased, her body stilled. “Stay out of this!” She threw the order over her shoulder.
Majima ignored it, and placed a hand there instead. “Would you stop and listen to me?”
“No!” Shion whirled around, throwing his hand off. “Nothing you say will-” She stiffened, as she
noticed a knife not far from her chin. Majima glared down at her, not a bit of patience in his lone
eye. “Have you ever killed someone before, kid? Because if you haven’t, you’re just being a
dumbass and saying shit.”

He sheathed his knife, the girl’s full attention on him now. “N-no, but- !”
“Genuinely, what the fuck do you think you’re going to accomplish? Make everything worse?
Because that sure is the route you’re on right now.” Shion wasn’t shy to profanity, but it still threw
her off. “Look, I don’t have the mindset Kazzy has with kids. And I definitely don’t have patience
for a stupid brat like you. So I’ll make this as clear and unsubtle as I can for you.”
“When both siblings learn what you’ve done, it will hurt them in a way you can never fix. Oh, they
might be thankful. They might apologize that they weren’t stronger. But you know damn well
they’ll suffer for it. My brother killed eighteen people. And don’t misunderstand me. I would have
joined him if I had the chance. Tried my hardest, and lost an eye for it.”
“But the point is that he killed, so I didn’t have to. My hands were technically clean, but only
because his were drenched in blood.” Shion took a step back, fear plain on her face. “Just… who
are you?” The Mad Dog grimaced, but it eventually changed to a wry smile. “I’m a yakuza. Just
like your sister.”
“And I know you might be thinking ‘then do something to stop Teppei’. I wish I could. I really
fucking wish I could get rid of that waste of space. But nothing good ever comes from involving
yakuza in things like this. Tensions are high between the Sonozaki Family and the people I work
for. Them getting involved on Sonozaki turf could be catastrophically bad.”
It was a lot to take in. The righteous fury Shion had felt was replaced with befuddlement and
doubts now. So strongly Majima had come on. But dark thoughts and feelings were returning as
quickly as they had left. “So I’m just supposed to leave things as is?! I just got Satoshi back! And
now him and Satoko are at the mercy of that bastard?!”
“Yes. And you killing him will be worse than any of that.”
“Then what can I do?!”
“Nothing.”
Shion mentally flat lined for a second. Majima’s brow rose, recognizing he might want to make an
addendum. “Let me rephrase. Nothing without help from us and your friends. There’s nothing on
this Earth you can do to repay someone for taking a life for your sake. All you will do is burden
them.” His eye sharpened. “And you would be the biggest fool in history to make that boy’s burden
heavier than it already is.”
Shion was a fish out of water mouthing for words to say. But the last line about Satoshi put any
desire for bloodshed to rest. There was already one death on Satoshi’s hands. Would she become a
murderer herself to join him in a twisted love? No… I can’t. I could… never do that to him.
She gazed at Majima with lost, sad eyes. His cheeks slightly flushed, and he avoided eye contact.
“Sorry, kid. Tact ain’t my specialty. And honestly I shouldn’t have just so casually said I’m a
yakuza but uh… do me a favor. Don’t tell anyone. I don’t want your sister to freak out. I’m on her
side, promise.”
“Ok, fine. But… what should I do?”
“Talk to Rika or Kiryu. It sounded like they had some ideas before you got here.”

“Ok, I… I need to get my thoughts straight. Um, but I did want to say I’m sorry about your
brother.”
A sharp exhale. A softened, bitter laugh. “Me too, kid. Me too…”
“Do you think Satoko and Satoshi will be ok?”
“For now? No, it’s a heavy situation. But those two kids are stronger than you think. Satoshi
protected his sister from both his uncle and aunt for what? Years? And based on everything I’ve
heard, Satoko has come a long way. Have some faith in them.”
“Ok, I’ll try. … You can be really scary, Majima. You know that?”
Majima cringed at himself. “I said I was sorry. I’m not as good with kids as Kazzy. … And besides,
you’re terrifying in your own right.”
“... Am I?”
Majima arched a brow staring at her blankly. “How do you think they’re feeling there right now?”
Shion felt herself shrink. Her grand show not even being five minutes ago. “I… need to apologize
to some people. If you’ll excuse me.” Mustering any dignity she had left, she returned to the scene
of the crime.
Majima scratched the back of his head. Good. That’s done and over with it. What next of the
checklist from Hell?
~~~~
In the distance, Satoshi could hear sounds of the Watanagashi festival. It was lively. People’s voices
and music carrying even to the Hojo house a ways from it. It sounded like people were having a
great time. Sure would be nice to be able to go out there himself. “Satoko! Get your ass in here
with some more sake!”
He flinched from his uncle’s voice. Its echo clashing in his mind, a strong reminder of his current
reality. Not that he needed one with a bruised wrist. Satoko was worse for wear. He couldn’t bear to
look at her. She had agreed to work alongside him, but she still made sure to take the main brunt of
it all. Any attempt on his part to defend Satoko just made her more desperate and receive yet
another blow.
He could feel himself and Satoko regressing. Returning to a past they wanted to leave behind.
Where was the future to be found in this situation? Satoko set down a glass full of sake. Satoshi
half wondered if maybe they could give him enough to kill him. But his uncle had become sharp.
Still a moron in many ways, but a killer for a nephew kept him on edge.
Satoshi presented himself in as docile and domesticated a way he could. Nothing more than a dog,
if that could lessen Satoko’s pain. A thought brought him pause. … No, I’ve not regressed. I’ve just
remained stagnant… stuck in a coma. Reality being nothing but a distant thought. He glanced at his
sister. She was battered, but with a steely look of minimal respect for her uncle needed.
There was poison in those eyes. A viper patiently waiting to strike. How, he didn’t know. But
Satoko believed her friends would help her somehow. She’s… the one that is stronger now. So

much time had passed him up. So little and yet so much had changed. Teppei was watching some
game show, cheap evening entertainment to pass the time. A verbal hiccup made his red face
vibrate.
“This is the good life! What more does a family need?”
A break in Satoko’s mask, but only momentarily. “Yes, a family.”
“You’re not used to having that are you?”
The corners of her lip spasmed as she maintained a neutral expression. “What do you mean,
Uncle?”
Teppei took another sip of his drink. He leaned his head back gesturing at Satoshi himself. “Well,
take him. He hasn’t gotten a chance to live much of a life cuz of you.” Satoshi tensed, and Satoko
was one step away from her facade breaking. “I mean, take your life in general. You were always
fucking things up for your family. Your mom could never find anyone to stay with her, and by the
time she actually did, they died. Poor bastards.”
A fire lit in her eyes. Satoshi tried to grab her attention shaking his head. It’s not worth it, Satoko!
Pick your battles! She caught her temper, Teppei too drunk to notice any of the cracks in Satoko’s
act. He drawled on with his impromptu speech. “You really screwed up big time calling protective
services on that one father of yours. And for what? You were such a shitty little brat. … But I like
the current you. You well aware of your place, but you’ve grown a pair. Who figured you’d turn out
to be more of a man than your brother?”
He laughed heartily at his own joke. “Shut up.” Teppei’s guffawing ceased. Satoshi was frantically
shaking his head. There was still time to play it off as the TV or that he was just hearing things.
“Don’t talk about Satoshi like that.” If looks could kill. If looks could completely disintegrate one’s
soul. Satoko wore that look intensely. A lethality Satoshi could never have envisioned his little
sister having.
Teppei set his glass down, and turned off the TV. He rose from his chair, stood to his full height,
and drunkenly walked over to Satoko. He looked down at her, a sadistic grin present. Satoshi felt
like he couldn’t move. He wanted to interfere, but wouldn’t that just make things worse? But they
were supposed to be a team, siblings, right?! But every time he did, she would receive another
blow. Another welt that was his fault.
Was… was this how Satoko felt when I protected her? Satoko’s whole body was shaking. She was
bleeding dread like a cornered mouse. With everything she had, she kept back her tears and stared
back up at her uncle. She was nothing like the sister he knew. But she didn’t have to do this. Why?
Why won’t she just do the minimum required? What if he seriously hurts her?
The boy was about to stand up and swap places. Do ANYTHING to stop her from being hit. And
then Teppei spoke. “You killed your own parents, didn’t you?”
… What? Any obstinate rebelliousness Satoko held. Gone. The roar of her engine completely shortcircuited. Replaced with a pallid, nigh anemic face. Eyes shining with a chaotic mix of
bewilderment and horror. She took a few steps back to the wall behind her. “W-what are you… “
“I always did find it odd that BOTH of them fell off. And you were the only one there? It didn’t
make any damn sense, but I had no choice but to accept it as an ‘accident’. No choice but to take

your sorry ass in. But your uncle is pretty smart. Ever since Satoshi told me about this syndrome of
yours. It finally clicked.”
“If it could make him kill my bitch ex-wife, then what’s to say it didn’t make you kill your own
parents? Not that I gave much of a shit about them, but they were still family. Our flesh and blood.”
He kneeled down and sneered at his niece with a wicked grin. “You’re a fucked up little girl.”
Satoko’s shaking intensified. No longer like a leaf in the wind, but in a hurricane. Frenzied tears
began to form in her eyes. Satoshi was about to throw everything in the wind. Consequences be
damned. To torture Satoko with an accusation like that was unforgivable. He was the murderer.
How dare he suggest Satoko was one as well.
“N-n-no that… that can’t be. No, I couldn’t have… it was… it was an accident. I… I didn’t mean
to!” He froze. His sister… didn’t deny it. What was going on?
“Ohhhhhhhh, but you did. You did it, your poor wittle girl. You’ve done nothing but fuck up your
entire life. I thought maybe your brother had finally gotten brave enough to actually do something,
but he was just following in his sister’s footsteps the whole time. You were the stronger one, and
yet hid behind him. What a goddamned joke.”
Satoko was as still as a stature. He cackled at her, but she said nothing. Even the tears on her cheeks
looked frozen in time. Teppei found himself annoyed at the lack of a reaction. “Hey. The hell is
your deal? Wake up!” He lightly slapped Satoko’s cheek not so gently. No response. He scowled
and inserted his foot into her abdomen. Not a kick as more a poke. “You just gonna stand there and
say nothing? Where’s all that moxie you had a second ago?! Huh?!”
Pushing with his foot, she crumpled to the ground. Crooked, leaning against the wall. Like a puppet
with its strings cut. At that, Teppei grunted. “Freak.” He stated bluntly, and then left the room to
head up the stairs. “Take care of your sister, Satoshi. I don’t know what to do with her.”
The words passed right by the boy’s ears. He slowly, carefully approached Satoko. “Satoko?”
Her brother’s voice brought some light back to her eyes. “Nii-Nii, I… I remember.” Sorrow and
self loathing beyond measure consumed her. “I pushed them off the edge! I killed them! I killed
them!! I killed them!! IT’S ALL MY FAULT!!” Before Satoshi could react, his sister grabbed a
discarded sake bottle.
And slammed it against her forehead with enough force for it to break. Blood spurted, a gash
formed as the bottle shattered from the impact.
“Satoko! Stop!!” Her brother cried out, but there was blood streaming down her forehead now. A
few minor cuts appeared on her face from the scattered glass. “It’s my fault!! I pushed them off the
ledge!! I- !”
“Satoko, control yourself!!” Satoshi firmly held Satoko’s shoulders. “What are you talking about?!”
“At the park! I… they were on the observation platform! I thought they were going to kill me, so
I… !” She slowly looked up and met Satoshi’s eyes. Blood and tears mixed together. “I pushed
them off the edge. I killed them.” There was still a piece of broken glass in her hand. And she
began to raise it to her neck.

Satoshi grasped her hand. He winced, the shard cut into his palm but he didn’t let go. “Satoko, I
don’t care what happened! Don’t hurt yourself, please!” His sister was horrified to see blood on his
hand. “... He was right.”
Bloodshot, puffy eyes devoured by despair gazed back at him. “Everything is my fault. You still get
hurt because of me.” She completely broke down sobbing. Satoshi tried to hide his now bloodied
hand, and held on to her with his other. “Satoko, I don’t care what you’ve done! It was the
syndrome! It’s not your fault! It’s not … “
His voice cracked. The emotions catching up with him. Fresh tears formed. All the boy could do
was hold his sister trying and failing to comfort her. As they both descended into a sea of misery
with no hope in sight. And no light to help them find the way out.

Midnight fast approached as Kiryu still found himself wide awake, staring up at the ceiling. Rika
had decided it was best to start with the child consultation center. He vaguely recalled how Rika
had explained how they had gone about it, but specifics were a blur. The whole day had felt like a
blur.
The most vexing thing about the situation was that it would take time. It took Rika and almost the
entire town getting together to save Satoko. What time? Watanagashi has already passed. What
was the fate of Takano? Was someone dying right now? Were somehow Satoshi and Satoko in
danger of dying?
He gritted his teeth in frustration, but calmed himself. At the least, Majima was able to find sleep. It
would be rude to wake him up with his own struggles. Realistically, Teppei won’t kill them. Satoko
and Satoshi should have their shots, so no worry of the syndrome going out of control. Tonight
should be fine.
But what about tomorrow? Or the next day, or the day after that? Were they now on a doomsday
timer? More thoughts that made him want to tear his hair out, so he distracted himself. If he wasn’t
getting any sleep, he might as well brainstorm what he should say at the center tomorrow. Would
they act sooner with her teacher there backing it up? I don’t know squat how child protective
services work.
Damn it, I need to watch myself and make sure I don’t lose my temper. If they’re reluctant to
interfere… The thought trailed off. It was a bitter pill to swallow. They have to take incidents like
this in a measured manner, it’s their job. I have to remember that. They want the best for every
child, but there are… steps to how this works.
He nearly fell out of the bed when the phone rang. Majima groggily rose his head. “Why the hell is
someone calling this late?” So much for his beauty sleep. “Good question.” Kiryu held a
nauseatingly bad feeling about the call. But be answered, it must. Better to just rip off the band-aid
and get it over with.
“Hello?” Kiryu reluctantly answered.
“Kiryu, it’s Rena. This is serious, really serious!”
Fuck. “What’s wrong, Rena?”

“Um, I… I heard a police car go by my house. I couldn’t sleep, so I went to check it out. There’s
five or six of them around the Hojo Household!” The Dragon’s heart dropped, if not far. “But
Satoko and Satoshi seem to be ok!” The heart remained suspended, but it was still beating
ridiculously fast. “Lead with that first! … Sorry, I shouldn’t yell at you.”
“I-I apologize! But, um…”
The weight of the world seemed to linger on her words. “What, Rena?”
“I… I don’t know understand it. How… it came to this. But they arrested Satoko.”
Kiryu jolted right up at hearing that. “What?!” Majima was still groggy, but Kiryu’s shout made
him wide awake. “What do you mean they arrested Satoko?!”
“I asked an officer what had happened. She… she called the police herself. They… found her
covered in blood with a knife in hand. Teppei’s corpse was in the living room full of stab wounds.
She said she killed him and… and her parents. W-what should I do, Kiryu?!”
She continued calling his name as the phone nearly slipped out of his hands. … What?
